News.title: Freight train smashes into overturned bus at entrance of Channel Tunnel leaving at least 19 passengers injured
News.content:
CRASH HORROR Freight train smashes into overturned bus at entrance of Channel Tunnel leaving at least 19 passengers injured







Next

SEVERAL people are critically injured after a freight train smashed into an overturned bus full of passengers.

The horror unfolded at the entrance to the Channel Tunnel in France at around 8pm.



A minibus flipped over and landed onto the railway tracks outside the Eurotunnel entrance – before being struck by an oncoming freight train.

Several fire engines, medics and a helicopter raced to the scene of the terrifying collision in Pas-de-Calais.



Initial reports suggest there are “numerous injuries” with at least five people in critical condition.

The current toll of injured stands at 19 people – including the driver – who have been struck in the head and legs.

None of the wounds are considered life-threatening, according to local Pas-de-Calais authorities.

The freight train was unable to stop or change direction, according to local reports.

Eurostar has cancelled its last two trains due to depart from London St Pancras and Paris Gare du Nord following the horror smash.

Travel for freight trains between England and France has also been severely disrupted in both directions.

News.title: Man, 62, killed his brother, 58, with single punch during drunken ‘play-fight’ in pub before celebrating with arms aloft
News.content:
Next

A MAN killed his own brother with a single punch during a drunken “play-fight” at a pub before celebrating.

Brent Clayton, 62, had been enjoying an evening drinking with his younger brother Simon, 58, at Waterfoot Social Club in Rossendale, Lancashire.



CCTV footage taken from inside the boozer on Saturday, November 23, 2024 shows Clayton shadow boxing inside a nearby function room and calling his brother over to join him.

Simon can be seen reluctantly standing before the two appear to play fight but events escalated after Simon caught Clayton on the lip.



Clayton then moves forward and throws a hard punch to Simon’s face, causing him to drop his arms.

He then throws one more, pushing Simon backwards and causing him to hit his head on the floor – Clayton is seen raising his arms up in victory after delivering the fatal blow.



Simon was rushed to hospital but was unable to survive his injuries and sadly died the next day.

Witnesses later said that when they got into the room to see Simon on the floor Clayton told them that Simon had hit him first, before telling the witness not to call an ambulance because “he will get up in a minute”.



But they called 999 after Simon was not responsive as emergency services arrived at the scene at around 11.45pm that night.

Meanwhile, Clayton was put in cuffs on suspicion of assault causing grievous bodily harm and was put in the back of a police van.

Clayton can be heard saying on an officer’s bodycam footage: “I know it’s my brother. At the end of the day he hit me first.”

In custody, he also told officers that he had “chinned” and “uppercut” his brother.

Clayton was intiailly interviewed before Simon died where he gave a prepared statement saying he was distraught to learn his brother was in a critical condition and could not answer any further questions.



In a second interview, Clayton gave another prepared statement, maintaining his upset, expressing remorse and saying he believed it was a play fight that escalated while they were both drunk.

A Home Office post-mortem examination determined that Simon had died from a hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury due to cardiac arrest and blunt force trauma to the head, with acute alcohol intoxication being a contributing factor.

In his final interview on 27th November after Simon had died and Clayton had been arrested on suspicion of murder, Clayton continued giving a prepared statement to say he was distraught at what had happened and didn’t feel he could answer any police questions.



On Wednesday, Clayton was jailed for four years at Preston Crown Court after having previously been found guilty of manslaughter following a trial.

Sentencing, Judge Robert Altham told Clayton: “You’ve lost your brother. Whilst you needlessly brought that about, you will feel the pain of that for the rest of your life.

“You claimed you acted in self-defence, which was contradicted by the CCTV and your comments to the police on the night.

“You said, ‘When someone assaults you, what do you do? Knock them out’.

“I am sure this was not a case of you using excessive force. I am sure you did not genuinely believe you needed to defend yourself.”



During the trial, jurors were told the brothers had spent much of the day drinking before bumping into each other and going to the club in the evening.

By 11:30pm both had consumed a large amount of alcohol and Simon was unsteady on his feet, the court heard.

Simon’s wife described him as “larger than life and an extremely hard worker” in a heartbreaking victim personal statement.

“There are no words that can describe the devastating impact losing my husband has had on my children, grandchildren and myself,” she said.

“Our worlds have been destroyed, and the person who did this was Simon’s own brother.



“Simon was my husband, my best friend, my protector and the person I expected to grow old with. We were already making plans for our life when we had more time to ourselves.

“Never in a million years did I imagine our future would be taken away from us in such a violent and senseless way. My life will never be the same again.”

She added: “His brother has taken away the future that Simon and I planned together, the future my children expected to have with their dad and the future my grandchildren should have had with their grandad. The future Simon deserved to have.”

News.title: Cop shoots wife dead as she works out at gym before turning gun on himself in horror murder-suicide as tributes paid
News.content:
TRAGIC END Cop shoots wife dead as she works out at gym before turning gun on himself in horror murder-suicide as tributes paid







Next

A COP has shot dead his wife before turning the gun on himself in a horror murder-suicide in Brazil.

Luciano Vieira Tavares Pereira walked into the gym where his wife was working out and fired a volley of six shots at Karla Alessandra Domingos, 49, before shooting himself in the head.



The public shooting unfolded in the coastal town of Lajinha on Wednesday afternoon.

Karla was pronounced dead at the scene – but her husband initially survived the suicide attempt.



Emergency services raced Pereira to hospital in critical condition.

He stabilised while in care in Lajinha – but later passed away while being transferred to César Leite Hospital in Manhuaçu.



Brazil’s military police have launched a probe into the tragic gun horror.

A motive has not yet been established as tributes pour in for wife Karla.

Heartbreaking Facebook messages describe her as a “special person” and “excellent teacher”.

An obituary shared online reads: “It is with deep sorrow that we announce the passing of teacher Karla Alessandra Domingos.



“Karla was an excellent teacher, a special person, and very dear to everyone who had the privilege of knowing her and being with her.

“Her passing leaves a lasting memory and a mark of affection and respect from all who were part of her journey.

“At this moment of farewell, we keep the memories and the recognition for her dedication and the affection shared throughout her life.



“Our condolences to family and friends. May they find strength and comfort to face this irreparable loss.”

Lajinha City Hall shared a tribute to both the victim and her killer in a Facebook post.

The post read: “The City Hall of Lajinha expresses, with deep sorrow, the passing of the couple Luciano Vieira Tavares Pereira and Karla Alessandra Domingos, which occurred this Wednesday.

“In this moment of immense pain, we express our solidarity to the family, friends, and everyone who had the privilege of sharing moments of their lives with Luciano and Karla.

“May God, in His infinite mercy, comfort the grieving hearts, granting strength, faith, and serenity to face this irreparable loss.

News.title: Woman grabbed cop’s privates and made explicit remarks to his colleagues for her own ‘sexual gratification’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

VILE ABUSE Woman grabbed cop’s privates and made explicit remarks to his colleagues for her own ‘sexual gratification’







Next

A WOMAN grabbed a cop’s privates and made explicit remarks for her own “sexual gratification”.

Robyn Murdoch, 31, also repeatedly made the sexual comments to two other officers in the run-up to Christmas last year.



She then groped the first officer, attempted to bite and spit on him and repeatedly kicked out at him.

Murdoch, 31, pleaded guilty to a string of offences which took place on John Wood Street in Port Glasgow on December 21, 2025.



She admitted directing a sexual verbal communication at the officers by repeatedly uttering sexually explicit and derogatory remarks towards them.

The perv also admitted directing a sexual comment at a female police officer and uttering sexually explicit and derogatory remarks towards the cop without her consent.



Greenock Sheriff Court heard Murdoch made the remarks intentionally and for the purposes of obtaining sexual gratification or of humiliating, distressing or alarming the police officers.

She was also charged with urinating on the floor at Greenock police office and uttering offensive and derogatory remarks while she was in the station.

Her not guilty plea to that charge was accepted by the Crown.

Sentence has been deferred until November 4 and Murdoch was released on bail.

News.title: Girl, 11, abducted off street by men who then sexually assaulted her after being ‘isolated’ at house
News.content:
SICK FIENDS Girl, 11, abducted off street by men who then sexually assaulted her after being ‘isolated’ at house







Next

AN 11-year-old girl was abducted off a street by men and was then sexually assaulted after she was “isolated” at a house.

Sadak Ali, who touched the girl over her clothing, was jailed for seven years today, October 15.



Birmingham Crown Court heard that the victim was “deliberately isolated” at a house after being initially abducted by co-defendant Hamza Sharif.

Sharif was jailed for five years for child abduction after Judge Roderick Henderson said the 36-year-old, of Birmingham, was the “driving force” of the offending, as he first met the victim on the street.



Ali, 28, of Birmingham, was found guilty at a trial of sexual assault and child abduction after jurors heard the youngster was taken to a property where he was using drugs.

Prosecutor Usha Shergill told the men’s sentencing hearing that the victim, who they did not know, had left her home in the early hours without notifying anyone and had encountered Sharif near a railway station in east Birmingham.



Sharif suggested that the girl should go to a house with him, where she declined an offer to take cocaine, and Ali asked her “invasive” sexual questions and assaulted her.

In a victim personal statement read to the court by Ms Shergill, the girl, who cannot be identified, said: “I thought the man wanted to help me but what happened changed me forever.”

She also said it felt like she was being punished, found it difficult to trust any adult and suffered “nightmares and flashbacks” in which she could picture the two men.

Before sentencing, defence barristers Simon Burch and Simon Williams accepted the defendants had used illegal drugs.



Mr Williams said Ali had “experienced trauma” in Somalia, which had affected his mental health, and had turned to alcohol and drugs as a coping mechanism.

“He is currently undertaking a personal social development course (in prison). In short, he wants to become a better person,” Mr Williams said.

Making representations by videolink, Mr Burch said there was no evidence that Sharif, who also appeared by videolink, from HMP Hewell in Worcestershire, had supplied the victim with drugs.

The court heard that Sharif had experienced “various tragedies” including the deaths of his wife and uncle.

Passing sentence and rejecting Mr Burch’s suggestion that Sharif had a “benevolent motivation” towards the victim, Judge Henderson accepted both defendants had experienced significant difficulties in their lives.



Ordering Ali to register as a sex offender for life and making both men subject to restraining orders, the judge said the victim was desperately vulnerable.

He said of Sharif: “He was the person that first made contact. He was therefore the driving force in the abduction.

“She (the complainant) was deliberately isolated for a significant length of time.”

News.title: Twisted teacher, 38, took photos of schoolgirls before creating AI-generated nude images to trade for child abuse pics
News.content:
DEEPFAKE PREDATOR Twisted teacher, 38, took photos of schoolgirls before creating AI-generated nude images to trade for child abuse pics







Next

A TWISTED teacher has been jailed after secretly snapping pictures of schoolgirls in their uniform and trading AI-generated nude depictions of them online for images of child sexual abuse.

Christopher Gerald Savage, 38, fed images of girls he had covertly taken as well as those he had found online to a chatbot and told it to undress them.



He then traded those AI images with 13 users on Telegram in exchange for more than 1100 child abuse images, the Ipswich District Court heard.

Savage pleaded guilty to 31 child abuse-related offences, The Courier Mail reported.



He was sentenced to six years behind bars on Thursday after admitting to storing more than 53,000 images and videos, in Ipswich, near Brisbane, Australia.

Savage targeted more than 20 children aged between 12 and 17 with his AI depictions.



He described having sexual interest in children as young as 10, the court heard.

One of his victims told the court that the twisted crimes had “cut her so deep”.

She said: “I’m here to express how negatively you have impacted my life and many others.

“Knowing that someone I knew and thought I trusted could do this to me and others makes me feel sick.



“When I first started to talk to people about this, all anyone could say was that they were extremely sorry and they felt so bad for me.

“Because of you, I will never be able to maintain a healthy relationship with anyone, especially men.”

When he was arrested in September 2024, Savage was a head of department at Lowood State High School.

Cops raided his home that month, finding files that showed sexual abuse of children, including infants, across eight devices.

But the sick school teacher was not working at that school when he took the photos of young girls, between 2023 and 2024.



Prosecutors said he admitted to masturbating to the AI images in messages.

Judge Craig Chowdhury said: “You spent considerable time and effort engaging in cumulative child pornography but also engaging in going around and photographing these children who you should be looking out for.

“You mastered your own destiny and mastered your own domain, and you made your choice to go down this dark road.”

Savage was sentenced to six years in prison and had his teaching registration suspended.

News.title: Supply teacher, 37, who took ‘horrendous’ upskirting pics of female pupils then used AI to sexualise images is jailed
News.content:
SICK PICS Supply teacher, 37, who took ‘horrendous’ upskirting pics of female pupils then used AI to sexualise images is jailed







Next

A FORMER supply teacher who took upskirting photos of female pupils and then used AI to sexualise the images has been jailed.

Abusali Rahman, 37, admitted carrying out the “horrendous” abuse of trust.



He used a phone to covertly take images of children within the school, and planned to sell the images to other paedophiles online.

Cops discovered that he had taken upskirting images of 12 girls, whose parents were alerted.



It is understood that he placed his iPhone in the top pocket of his clothing in order to capture the images.

Greater Manchester Police said the girls were aged between 13 and 16, and attended seven high schools across Bury, Bolton and Salford.

In all, Rahman had taught at 25 schools across the North West.

In addition to the upskirting, Rahman stole images of girls he had taught from their social media profiles, before using AI to create sexualised images and post them on social media.

He came to police attention when pictures of students at schools in Bolton were seen on X accounts which were linked to Rahman, a British national.

At Bolton Crown Court today, October 15, Rahman was sentenced to six years in prison.



Prosecuting, Tom Farr said that Rahman had worked in schools across the North West since October 2022 but only qualified in July the following year.

The police became involved after reports were made about three X accounts which featured “images of numerous teenage school children”, thought to be students at schools in Bolton.

Rahman had used AI to sexualise images of one girl.

In one her appearance had been altered so that she was wearing a bikini, and in another a PVC outfit.

He had transposed the image of the same girl onto the face of an adult engaging in sexual activity.



An image of another girl was posted next to adults engaging in sexual activity, in which Rahman posted the caption, “wish it could have been this young bop in the blacked scene instead”.

The accounts had posted further images with captions such as “daddy” and “age gap”.

Police were able to trace the X accounts to Rahman.

Following his first arrest in June last year, Rahman said: “As soon as I knew it had been reported to the police, I stopped. I’m worried I’m going to lose my job.”

His laptop was seized and was found to contain upskirting images which had been taken “covertly in schools”.



Mr Farr said the upskirting images had been taken in “corridors, classrooms and around the school”.

Rahman was also found to have recorded the names and addresses of pupils.

After a further arrest, he refused to give police the PIN number to his phone.

He gave “no comment” interviews to police throughout the investigation.

Police discovered information within the notes section of his iPhone which promoted the sale of sexual content online, which he described as “me best shots and vids”.



Mr Farr said: “It promoted a Telegram account for a one-time payment of £20, via a Paypal account, to receive all the best ‘candid candy’.”

Rahman had made searches about “how to upskirt without getting caught”, and “where to buy spy cameras”.

He was involved in chats with a network of other paedophiles and discussed the “sharing of images and interest in schoolgirls and upskirting”.

He also searched what defences there could be if a teacher was arrested for making images of children, and what the sentence could be.

The upskirting images were taken between January and June last year.



Rahman had downloaded almost 200 indecent images of children between December 2023 and June 2025.

Sentencing, Judge Kenderick Horne told Rahman: “You were a trusted supply teacher. Your position of trust gave you access to schools and classrooms.

“You were trusted to be in close proximity to female school pupils as young as 11. You abused that trust. You took photographs of the girls showing their underwear between their legs.

“You used equipment and methods that you had researched.

“In May 2025 you made preparations to set up a Telegram account in which you would charge £20 for sexual images which you described as ‘Candid Candy’.



“I am sure that the images you were planning to sell were those you had taken at school.”

The judge said a colleague had spoken highly of Rahman.

He added: “That does not give you any real mitigation. It was your ability to teach to a good standard and gain the respect of your colleagues that helped you to maintain the trust they placed in you.

“Badly regarded teachers are more likely to face scrutiny and are less likely to have the opportunities for abuse that you had.”

Rahman, of no fixed address, but from Salford, pleaded guilty to 21 offences.



He admitted 12 counts of taking an indecent image of a child, four counts of publishing an obscene article, three counts of possessing indecent images of children, one count of distributing indecent images of children, and one count of voyeurism.

Defending, Emma Kehoe said of Rahman: “There is nothing in his life to suggest he has been anything other than a good member of society, a good husband, a good father, a good son, up to his arrest for these offences.

“He found himself out of control and unable to stop.”

She said that his arrest “came as a relief” to him.

Ms Kehoe said that Rahman had previously approached an imam for advice about his “difficulties” but he was told to get married.



“It wasn’t taken seriously,” she said. “But he did go and get married, he did as he was told. It was an arranged marriage. But it didn’t stop the difficulties he was having in his head, it didn’t stop his offending.”

She added: “He [Rahman] does not in any way try to excuse his behaviour. He wants to make that exceptionally clear. He knows what he did is horrendous. He is a father himself.”

Ms Kehoe said that Rahman had been a ‘good teacher’ and that his crimes were “completely out of character”.

She said his “dream had been to become a permanent teacher, but that he was unable to secure a job so he became a supply teacher.

“It was a job, these offences aside, that he was very proud of,” Ms Kehoe added.



She said Rahman “knows he is going to prison for a long time” but asked the judge to give him “some light at the end of the tunnel”.

After today’s hearing, Alexandra Mann, Senior Crown Prosecutor, said: “Abusali Rahman abused his position as a teacher to capture images of children without their knowledge in a school environment where they were entitled to feel safe.

“Rahman also created and shared sexualised deepfake images of pupils on social media which is a gross breach of trust.

“Misuse of emerging technology is a serious crime, and it has had a profound impact on both the victims and wider community.

“We worked with police to piece together strong evidence from his devices and locations at the time the photos were taken to build a comprehensive picture exposing the extent of his offending.



“I hope this case sends a clear message that we will robustly prosecute those who use technology to exploit children.”

After Rahman pleaded guilty, Detective Chief Superintendent Rebecca McKendrick, head of GMP’s Public Protection Division, said: “Our Online Child Abuse Investigation Team has painstakingly worked through the evidence to build a case against Rahman.

“The victims have been at the forefront of our investigation, and we have kept their parents and guardians and their schools informed and supported throughout this process.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Protecting children remains our highest priority, and we will continue to work closely with and meeting the victims, schools and local authorities to ensure there is support in place for anyone affected.

“Anyone who wants to report an offence or has any information on this investigation can still call 0161 856 1737 where you can speak to specially trained officers, via 101 or Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 quoting Operation Pomerie.”

News.title: Former DUP leader Donaldson sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sex abuse
News.content:
Jeffrey Donaldson has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences, including one count of rape.

The former DUP leader stood with his hands clasped in front of him in the dock of Newry Crown Court as his sentence was handed down.

Judge Paul Ramsey said Donaldson's crimes, which took place between 1985 and 2008, had led to a "catastrophic descent into disgrace".

He was sentenced to 11 years for his crimes against Victim B and four years for offences against Victim A.

The 63-year-old, who was convicted in June, is seeking to appeal his convictions.

Both sentences will run consecutively.

But Donaldson will spend only half his 15-year sentence behind bars.

Because the offences were committed before the Criminal Justice (Northern Ireland) Order 2008 came into effect, he qualifies for 50% remission.

Should his attempt to appeal his convictions fail, it means he will be released from prison at the end of 2033.

The remainder of his sentence will be under supervision in the community on licence.

News.title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says
News.content:
Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.

It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.

The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.

Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.

That meant that a trans woman â a biological male who identifies as a woman â could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man â a biological female who identifies as a man â could have opted for a men's ward.

That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.

The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.

Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.

But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met.

It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.

In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.

Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.

The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.

Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.

NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.

The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.

Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters has welcomed the guidance as a "momentous shift back to reality", but is concerned about how it will be applied.

"NHS patient data is a mess, with potentially thousands of trans-identifying people recorded as the opposite sex," CEO Maya Forstater said.

Trans rights organisations TransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance have said they are concerned NHS staff will be unclear on how to safely look after trans patients.

"This guidance will not survive contact with reality in resource-strapped hospitals and will create unworkable operational challenges," they said.

The NHS has been at the centre of a number of high-profile arguments over the interpretation of equality law and workplace regulations.

In January 2026, Darlington Memorial Hospital was found to have violated the dignity of a group of nurses who complained about a transgender colleague - a biological male who identified as a woman - being allowed to use the female changing rooms. The nurses were told they should change somewhere else if they objected.

The tribunal concluded that the trust had indirectly discriminated against them.

The nurses are currently seeking Â£400,000 from the NHS to cover their legal costs.

One of the nurses who brought the action, Bethany Hutchison, who is now president of the Darlington Nurses Union, says they welcome the "clear and necessary guidance" from NHSE, but the test will be whether trusts follow it.

"The Darlington nurses should never have had to take their own employer to court to secure privacy, dignity and lawful single-sex facilities," she said.

"Enforcement cannot continue to depend on the courage and personal sacrifice of individual nurses."

In Scotland, another employment tribunal found, in December 2025, that a nurse, Sandie Peggie, had been harassed by NHS Fife over its interpretation of rules on single sex spaces.

Peggie had complained about a doctor, who was a trans woman, using the female changing rooms.

She was suspended after raising concerns. The tribunal dismissed her other claims of discrimination and victimisation.

An appeal is under way and expected to reach the courts next year.

News.title: Russell Brand accuser says he turned 'monster-like' before alleged rape
News.content:
Under cross-examination Brand's barrister, Ian Winter KC put it to the complainant that when she first met Brand she welcomed his attention.

"I welcomed his company, not what followed," the woman replied.

He then suggested that she fell under his spell and that she wanted to spend more time with him.

The woman replied: "That's incorrect. I did not fall under his spell and I did not find him attractive. "

Asked by the defence why she agreed to go back to the hotel room with Brand, she responded: "I'm telling you... I thought he was a gay man, very softly spoken, very effeminate.

"I felt safe â I felt sexually safe with him. He was very intelligent and that appealed to me, not in a sexual sense. "

The woman became tearful a number of times while giving her evidence from the witness box.

At one point the judge told the witness to "take a moment, catch your breath", after she became emotional.

Brand's barrister later challenged the complainant about why she did not run back into the bathroom or leave the room when she realised Brand had removed some of his clothes.

She replied: "What was I supposed to do? Hide in bathroom? Walk out the room? Walk past him? I had no phone, no reception, no idea where I was. Run into the night with him following me?"

Referring to photographs she had taken of Brand, she said: "I took those photographs, he told me to take them, he was showing off, he was prancing around... I was scared... I couldn't fight him.

"I blame myself for allowing him back into my room," the woman said.

She was also challenged by the defence barrister about why she didn't report her allegation about Brand to the police in Bournemouth.

She said: "I didn't report it as I didn't want anyone to know. I didn't think anyone would believe me."

The woman told the jury that after she says she was raped by Brand she blamed herself "in that moment".

"I hate that I blamed myself, I shouldn't have to blame myself."

She also told jurors: "I regret to this day the error in judgment thinking this man would not rape me.

News.title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits
News.content:
Senior banking executives have told the BBC they expect the sector to be "on the menu" when the chancellor announces his Budget in two weeks' time.

John Healey has described the banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, yet has refused to rule out a raid on the sector.

The biggest four banks collectively made around Â£15bn profit in the first six months of this year, leading to calls from trade unions and others for additional taxes.

However, the banking sector trade body, UK Finance, warned that "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".

The UK's biggest banks and building societies currently pay a surcharge of 3% on top of the baseline 25% rate of corporation tax, plus a levy on the assets held on their balance sheets.

The sector contributed nearly Â£40bn to the Treasury last year, if income tax on employees is factored in.

The bank levy generated Â£1.4bn last year and the surcharge a further Â£1.2bn.

There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.

The 3% surcharge was reduced from 8% under Rishi Sunak, at the same time as he raised corporation tax from 19% to 25%. Returning the surcharge to its previous level could raise around Â£2bn a year.

The bank levy currently charges 0.1% on outstanding short-term loans and 0.05% on longer-dated loans, although mortgages are excluded from the calculation.

In the past banks have successfully argued that higher taxes would risk making the UK uncompetitive with other jurisdictions and would reduce their ability to lend, and therefore be anti-growth.

In truth, banks were pleasantly surprised they were not hit at the last Budget, given the large profits they have been making in recent years. Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which they lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.

There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials. Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year. Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.

Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra Â£1bn per year for the Treasury. That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.

It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world. He warned that adding further sector-specific taxes could discourage investment and damage competitiveness.

However, industry leaders say any form of tax rise that hits UK banks and exempts foreign banks' operations in the UK would be hard to square with the government's push to back British business.

Whatever form it takes, banks believe the chancellor now has much more of an appetite to take a larger slice of their pie.

News.title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM
News.content:
Swimmer Archie Goodburn has been successful in his efforts to improve brain cancer care for patients as the UK government announce new measures.

The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, met Prime Minister Andy Burnham after making an emotional plea on BBC Breakfast for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.

After the meeting, Burnham announced a new national brain cancer clinical lead and promised a review of brain cancer progress and action to get patients treatment sooner.

Goodburn, 25, thanked the prime minister and said all three of his requests have been "promised to some extent" but "fleshing out" needs to be done on the details.

The prime minister described the swimmer an "inspiration to us all" and said he was "delighted" to welcome him to Downing Street.

News.title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
News.content:
South East Water's operations director Douglas Whitfield said standpipes remained part of the company's drought plan but were unlikely to be needed.

Whitfield said a wet winter had been forecast but timings were not clear and the firm was making any adjustments it could to protect supplies.

Whitfield said South East Water, which supplies more than two million customers, said 92 repair crews were out across Sussex and Kent tackling leaks to minimise loss from the network.

In an email sent to customers South East Water said it was optimising water pressure across the county and had more than doubled the number of teams tackling leaks in the region, increasing from seven to 16.

It said the number of leaks in the affected area had fallen from 181 to 97 and that more than 1,300 leaks had been repaired since 1 April.

Wessex Water, which supplies customers from Wimbleball, introduced its first hosepipe ban in 50 years in August and said the restrictions would remain in place for the foreseeable future.

The water company said it had increased leak repairs, moved water into the area from more resilient sources and adjusted water pressure in some communities to conserve supplies and urged customers to continue using water carefully.

Will Willoughby, director of water supply at Wessex Water, said: "We saw record levels of demand through the network - and it sustained above the 400 million litres a day for 48 days, which is far and away the toughest year that we've seen in terms of that height in demand."

He said customer impact "should be none" but encouraged customers to continue to be mindful about water usage.

Paul Tompkins, deputy president of The National Farmers' Union (NFU) said it had been a "torrid year for farmers", where the conditions proved "very difficult" to harvest crops, provide water for livestock, and a "potential dry winter could have implications for next year's crops".

News.title: Man killed by tiger climbed two fences before suffering multiple injuries, inquest hears
News.content:
Brookes told the hearing: "He was approached by the tiger and the ensuing physical contact between the tiger and Mr Chapman led to him sustaining multiple traumatic injuries which rapidly led to his death."

Park staff secured the tiger and paramedics attended but confirmed his death at the scene.

The senior coroner said her office was awaiting a more substantial report as to the extent of his injuries.

South Yorkshire Police provided a number of witness statements from the public and staff who were at the wildlife park at the time, the hearing was told.

Mundy instructed staff to contact Yorkshire Wildlife Park to ask them to keep any relevant CCTV and inform the coroner of any previous visits by Chapman to the park.

After opening the inquest, which Chapman's family chose not to attend, on Thursday morning, Mundy adjourned proceedings until 18 March 2027.

Speaking after the hearing, a neighbour of Chapman told the BBC he was "very polite and well-spoken" and a "lovely man".

Josh, 24, who lived in the same building as Chapman, said: "He'd always have a laugh and a joke. He was quite well kept, he'd look after himself physically. He loved his F1, he'd talk for hours about his F1 if he could."

Discussing the online comments and speculation in the aftermath of the incident, he said: "People didn't know him. If you don't know him, don't make a comment."

News.title: Meghan makes first official public appearance since moving back to UK
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has made her first official public appearance since moving back to the UK, telling well-wishers "it's great to be back".

Meghan arrived at a youth charity in Nottingham alongside her husband, the Duke of Sussex, on Thursday morning. The pair, who are also expected to visit a food bank later, hugged and posed for selfies with the public.

The duchess spoke to a number of people in the crowd, telling one "we got lucky" as they chatted about the weather.

She has shared glimpses of her life back in the UK on social media, but this is the first time she has attended any public events since the family returned from California.

News.title: Fifty arrests in crime probe after fatal A66 crash
News.content:
A total of 50 people have now been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime following a fatal crash.

The arrests have been made after the head-on smash on the A66 on Teesside which killed seven people, including two police officers.

Ten of the 50 arrested are alleged to be linked to the Volvo reportedly involved in driving into two properties in the early hours of 22 August, police said.

Det Ch Sup Helen Barker of Cleveland Police, said: "Over the last two months, we have identified 50 people who we believe are associated within criminal networks that seek to cause serious violence and harm within the community through the supply of drugs."

The force said shotguns, hand guns, machetes and ammunition had also been seized, as well as Â£60,000 worth of class A and B drugs and more than Â£30,000 in cash.

Barker said: "Our pursuit of this criminality will continue, and I want to take this opportunity to thank the community for their support and patience but also for the information that we keep receiving.

"I want to encourage you to keep on reporting behaviour that is related to drugs or organised crime - no matter how small - and be assured we will act."

News.title: Farage defends Reform's vetting after councillors filmed making racist comments
News.content:
On a different day in the ITV broadcast, Feeney is joined by two other Reform candidates, Jamie Campbell and Chris Whelan, who discuss speculation of a mosque being built in the local area.

"There's got to be a way of stopping them - like, go and buy some pork chops; we'll bury it in the ground," Campbell is heard saying in the film.

Whelan says "we'll take pictures of it", prompting Feeney to add: "I was gonna say, 'Unfortunately, this is a pig cemetery, mate'."

Discussing a female Reform candidate from Birmingham, Feeney is heard saying, "I didn't know where to look", before Whelan adds: "I'd have been sniffing that seat as soon as she got up."

The BBC has tried to contact Feeney for a response. ITV has reported that on Monday evening he had "mutually agreed" to resign from Reform UK, citing "personal reasons" and would be continuing as an independent councillor.

The BBC has contacted Campbell and Whelan, who has resigned as a councillor, for a response.

A Reform UK Solihull spokesman condemned Feeney and Whelan's "misogynistic and offensive comments" and confirmed they were no longer Reform councillors.

The spokesman said Campbell's comment "was a joke in poor taste but with no malicious intent", adding: "It's something that he deeply regrets, and the party will not be taking any further action."

Elsewhere in the film, Dean Miller, a councillor in the south London borough of Bromley, is shown campaigning for Reform in the Makerfield by-election.

"We've been ethnically cleansed out of London because you never used to get any blacks over in Bromley," he tells an ITV undercover reporter. "And now, you know, Bromley's like massive Nigerian communities there."

Miller says he is "not racist", before later adding: "The Muslim thing, that is going to be that thing that takes over everything and then everyone just has one religion. Because, apparently, King Charles is a [expletive] Muslim... I think that's [expletive] traitorous."

ITV reported that Miller would now sit as an independent councillor having resigned from Reform and had told them in a statement that he was heavily medicated due to a chronic pain condition when he made the comments.

The BBC has contacted him for comment.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Reform should take "immediate and firm action against those who've been revealed to be making these abhorrent comments".

He added: "There is no place for any form of racism, antisemitism, discrimination in British politics, and we all should be relentless in repeating that and taking the firmest possible action."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "We should be asking why there's so many stories like this of people in Reform who are making these appalling comments."

Asked about one of the individuals being a former Tory councillor, she said: "It's not my problem anymore."

Badenoch added: "I don't want people like that in the Conservative Party. I'm glad they have gone."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "This is chilling. I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community."

A Green Party spokesman said: "Vilifying migrants and Muslims is Reform's main focus, and these racist comments reflect party policy."

News.title: King Charles praises Welsh 'sense of belonging' as he opens Senedd
News.content:
King Charles III has praised Welsh people's "sense of belonging", as he and Queen Camilla officially opened the Senedd's seventh term.

The visit marked the King's first official meeting with First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth following the election victory of Plaid Cymru - a party rooted in a strong republican tradition.

In his speech to the Senedd, with most of its 96 members in attendance, including opposition parties Reform, Labour and the Tories, the King also expressed concern for the impact of climate change on the Welsh countryside.

About 30 protesters by the steps of the Senedd were vocal throughout the royal visit, and one was arrested on suspicion of breaching the Public Order Act.

Chants of "not my King" and "down, down, down with the crown" could be heard from protesters during the visit.

Wales' national poet did not take part in the ceremony as had been planned, after Senedd officials rejected the poem she had written for the event and cancelled her performance.

The King used his visit to the Senedd to say he would return to Wales next week to visit Aberfan - scene of the 1966 coal tip disaster and meet a survivor who had been pulled from the rubble aged six.

A 21-gun salute in Cardiff Bay marked the King's arrival in the city, and Plaid leader ap Iorwerth greeted the King on the Senedd steps, together with Presiding Officer Huw Irranca-Davies and Labour Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock, who represented the UK government.

News.title: Tributes paid to crew of fishing boat missing off Lewis
News.content:
Isles MP Torcuil Crichton said Craigie's devastated family were now planning his funeral, and the islands would miss the "sparkle" of his wit and charm.

Crichton told BBC Radio Scotland's Drivetime programme: "These men were part of their own community as well as the fishing community of the islands.

"I last came across Douglas Craigie at the Western Isles Fisherman Association Conference last year in Uist, which will no longer sparkle with his wit and charm this year.

"Today would have been his 50th birthday and his family are devastated planning a funeral instead of a party."

Crichton said Murray is a well-respected member of the community of Ness in the north of Lewis, and is one of the Men of Ness who harvest young gannet known as guga.

The MP said Morrison, who is also a guga hunter, is the "kind of young person we try to encourage to go to sea to keep on this age old tradition of fishing".

News.title: Taxi driver given fake cash drove customer to police
News.content:
A man was arrested after a taxi driver who was given fake cash drove the suspect straight to a police station.

Nottinghamshire Police said the driver picked up the suspect from Nottingham Road at 23:30 BST on Tuesday.

When the customer continued to change his route, the taxi driver asked how he would be paying, which is when he was handed a counterfeit Â£20 note, the force added.

After questioning the customer and being given further fake notes, the driver took him straight to Radford Road police station.

The force said officers also carried out a search of a man's address, where they discovered a "Rambo knife" under his mattress.

It added no further counterfeit cash was recovered, but a cannabis cultivation kit was seized from the address.

A 23-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of using counterfeit currency and possessing an offensive weapon in a private place.

News.title: Another man admits raping woman drugged by husband over 20 years
News.content:
Another man has pleaded guilty to raping a woman who was drugged and abused by her husband without her knowledge for over 20 years.

Graham Brougham, 74, is the oldest of 13 men who were charged with sexual offences against the victim after being allegedly invited into her home, in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, to abuse her by her husband.

The husband, in his sixties, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife - including rape - and has given a witness statement detailing "what he says happened".

Brougham, from Northwich, was told by a judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that he "should be under no illusion his sentence will be custody and a long time in custody."

The victim, who held hands with a family member, watched on from the public gallery as Brougham answered "guilty" in the dock to a charge of raping her in September 2024.

News.title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has threatened to ban all Eritreans from entering the UK if the east African country's government does not accept more returns of small boat migrants and foreign national offenders.

From Thursday, Eritrean diplomats will face restrictions on their movement outside London. Fast-track visas will also be stopped for VIPs.

Ministers have previously pressured other countries into accepting returns by threatening visa bans.

Eritrea branded the move a "perfunctory political gimmick", saying the UK had not issued a single visa to an Eritrean official since 2023.

The country's embassy in London also accused the UK of refusing to engage in "meaningful and appropriate dialogue".

It said the UK had failed to disclose the return of criminals still serving prison terms and that the UK had claimed returns were voluntary "when clearly, they were not".

Human Rights Watch has accused Eritrea's government of widespread repression - including forced labour, conscription and restrictions on freedom of expression.

Eritreans were the most common nationality among small boats migrants in the 12 months to June - accounting for 18% of arrivals, external, according to figures from the House of Commons Library.

Mahmood said: "Eritrea has had every chance to accept the return of criminals and those with no right to be in the UK. Unlike other countries, it has refused."

She said she would not hesitate "to impose further measures on other countries refusing to co-operate".

The UK government accused the Eritrean authorities of "abruptly" withdrawing co-operation earlier this year.

The restrictions mean diplomats are banned from travelling 60km outside London without permission.

The Home Office said this mirrored restrictions on British officials in Eritrea's capital Asmara.

In the 12 months to June only seven people from Eritrea were returned there from the UK, according to Home Office figures. A further 244 Eritreans were returned to other countries.

Over the same period, more than 5,800 Eritreans arrived in the UK via small boats. A further 1,300 were given visas, mostly to join people already settled in the UK.

Dr Madeleine Sumption, director of the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, said targeting Eritrea would have little impact.

"Eritrea is one of the major countries of origin for asylum seekers coming to the UK - we had roughly 7,000 asylum applications in the last year of data, roughly 8% of the total," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

"Most Eritreans who come and claim asylum are not removable at all - the government would never be in negotiations to remove them because 84% are successful at initial decision; more will be successful on appeal."

She added that about 1,400 people were initially refused asylum, but that this number would reduce after appeals.

Many young Eritreans try to leave the country - which is a one-party state - to avoid military conscription, which can last for decades.

News.title: Nandy 'minded to intervene' in Sky's £1.6bn takeover of ITV entertainment arm
News.content:
But Nandy has told Sky and ITV that she is considering issuing a public interest intervention notice (PIIN) to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and regulator Ofcom, forcing an investigation into the tie-up.

In a letter to both companies, she said she was minded to order the probe to address public interest considerations including:

The need for free expression of opinion in news media

The need for a range of views in news media across the UK

The need for a range of people controlling the media across the UK

The need for a wide range of programmes to be offered across the UK

The letter said Nandy recognised Sky News and ITV News were two of the most prominent sources of television news in the UK, with a joint 26% share of those viewing news on linear TV.

Consumers would still have access to other sources of news such as the BBC and Channel 4, it added.

But Nandy believes that, over time, the tie-up could undermine the range of views available to viewers, with 86% of the linear TV news market controlled by the BBC and Sky/ITV.

The North of England could be particularly hard hit as well as nations of the UK other than England and those from lower socio-economic backgrounds, the letter argued.

This is because their main source of news is broadcast news, it added.

Sky and ITV have been given until 20 October to respond to the culture secretary's concerns.

A Sky spokesperson said: "We have already made clear commitments to protect ITV's identity, its free-to-air services and public service broadcasting obligations, and to ensure ITV News and Sky News remain distinct editorial voices."

An ITV spokesperson said: "We welcome the publication of the secretary of state's 'minded to' issue a public interest intervention notice letter as was expected and look forward to fully co-operating in the process.

"This is another important milestone in the regulatory review process towards creating a UK player with the scale and resources to better compete with global streaming platforms, benefiting viewers, advertisers and the UK creative industries."

Nandy's intervention would be made under a new public interest consideration.

This would need legislation to be brought forward, given that current laws do not cover the effect of a merger on streaming or on-demand programmes.

She said: "If I decide to intervene on the basis of this new public interest consideration, I will bring forward legislation... to extend the application of the public interest consideration relating to the availability of a wide range of broadcasting to on-demand programmes."
