News.title: Trump admits ‘I have some very severe problems’ in Biden-like ramble at White House
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nine hours after he’d landed at the new helipad on the South Lawn that he can’t stop gushing about —after a multi-day campaign swing through mostly safe Republican states that he should not have to rally support in — Donald Trump told a hand-picked group of first responders gathered in the Rose Garden that he was “supposed to be sleeping now.”

The attendees had come to the luncheon with the expectation of seeing Trump speak, but both they and he might have been better off if he’d decided to shut his eyes and stay in bed.

Instead of a cogent, topical set of remarks from the leader of the free world (at least that's what the POTUS is supposed to be anyway), what they got was nearly an hour of rambling from an exhausted octogenarian rushing headlong towards a midterm election his party is on course to lose.

“If my voice holds out, we’re going to be in great shape,” Trump said early on, after listing the states still on his schedule at his pace of a rally-and-a-half a day. “You know, it is one voice after all. You could maybe get one of those beautiful robots that they make nowadays and make them look just like me, and you wouldn’t know the difference. Send them out on the trail. I can sit home and watch them on television.”

For those of us who covered the last year of Joe Biden’s presidency, the 80-year-old’s demeanor elicited a sharp sense of deja vu — watching a past-his-prime, soon-to-be lame duck shrug off dismal polling and rising unaffordability while pivoting to talking about what happens after he is gone.

open image in gallery Instead of a cogent, topical set of remarks from the leader of the free world, Trump delivered nearly an hour of rambling from an exhausted octogenarian rushing headlong towards a midterm election his party is on course to lose ( AFP/Getty )

The bravado that led him to spend months trolling the press and public about a third term appeared to be completely gone, leading him to tacitly acknowledge the limitations of his time in office — in the middle of a boast about the $22 trillion in investment he claims his unpopular tariffs have brought in.

“You’re going to have a president someday that’s not me, and they’re going to be standing right here, ladies and gentlemen. I’d like to report the greatest growth in the history of our country. I’ve done such a good job,” Trump said, sounding more defeatedly wistful than boastful.

Trump then turned to the head of the Border Patrol union at a nearby table. “Remember, I did it. They didn’t do it. So just remember that,” he said.

He claimed to be the victim of a similar phenomenon when he remarked that drug-pricing reforms from his first term “kicked in in Biden’s second year,” leading his successor (and predecessor, given his split terms) to announce the results as his own.

“I remember Biden standing up and saying, ‘Ladies and gentlemen, I want to announce some great numbers here or there.’ And I’d say, ‘I did that.’”

Trump said the same thing a different way when he talked about the brass plaques of the “presidential walk of fame” now mounted along the colonnade. The entries get “a little bit more personal as we get closer to my year,” he said, “about what we’ve had to put up with. So who knows? They’ll probably change that as soon as they get in. But all I do is write the truth.”

open image in gallery Chairman of the National Volunteer Fire Council Chief Steve Hirsch presents a fire helmet to Trump at the Rose Garden lunch ( Reuters )

With less than a month until voters cast their ballots in the midterms, Trump appears caught in the same polling bubble that trapped Biden until a come-to-Jesus meeting with then-Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) convinced him that he no longer had enough support from his party to continue as the Democratic presidential nominee.

For most of that summer leading up to his shockingly bad debate performance against Trump, Biden told anyone who asked that the polls were wrong, that his crowds proved it and that the press would not report it.

Trump’s refrain in the paved-over space that was once the Rose Garden was similar: “The Democrats are saying there’s something bad happening, and the fake news doesn’t want to talk about it. But these are rallies that nobody’s ever seen.”

It was unclear what he was talking about, though Trump has remarked multiple times in recent days that he has boosted GOP candidates simply by appearing in their states for a 2024-style rally.

He was more candid about individual races than about the national picture. The Montana congressman he flew out to help is in “a little bit of a tight race.” Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who Trump allowed is “a little bit controversial,” has “pulled pretty even now” with James Talarico in Texas — yes, let it sink in, the Trump backed Republican in ruby-red Texas has pulled even with a trans-rights supporting, left-leaning Democrat, and the president is noting that as a plus. Oh, and Trump said he’d “go back if it’s necessary because “we got to win these races.”

On Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed leads Mike Rogers, he said, “I can’t imagine he won.” He called El-Sayed, a physician born in Michigan to Egyptian parents, “a Muslim Brotherhood guy, 100 percent,” and said, “I call him Mohammed Abdul Al-Sayyed.”

open image in gallery Trump performed his signature YMCA ‘dance’ for attendees after meandering remarks in the White House Rose Garden ( AP )

The admission (as in the headline above) came while Trump was explaining why fentanyl has never tempted him: he does not drink, smoke or take drugs.

“I have other problems. I have some very severe problems, but those are not one of them. I don’t want to add them to the list. Do you understand that, Todd?” he strangely said to Attorney General Todd Blanche, who is also his former personal lawyer. “Because if I did, I guarantee I wouldn’t be here right now.”

He caught it immediately. “Now the press is going to say, ‘What problem does he have? Let’s figure it out.’ I probably set myself up for that one, Todd. Todd’s going to have to try and defend me because they’re going to say, he said he’s got some serious problems. What are they? Which I actually don’t know. I was just having fun.”

Also, Todd is not your lawyer anymore, he is the American people’s, so why would he be defending you, Mr. President?

The bizarre remark was reminiscent of the madcap stories and gaffes that came from Biden at this point in his term, from the uncle supposedly eaten by cannibals to talk about “President Putin” of Ukraine and “Vice President Trump” at that year’s NATO summit.

Trump does his own explaining, on the spot, and did here. But in 2024, the clips were the news and they were widely and regularly promoted by conservative outlets and Trump’s social media allies. This year, they share the page with gasoline at $4.40, a war in its eighth month, and an approval rating Pew measured at 30 percent this month, the lowest of either of Trump’s divisive terms. Democrats lead the generic ballot by nine points and are ahead in 10 of the 12 competitive Senate races.

He still got laughs.

Navy missile strikes on drug boats, Trump said, have “killed the fishing industry,” because “nobody wants to go boating anymore.” He wants the death penalty for anyone who shoots a firefighter on a ladder. When a volunteer fire chief handed him a helmet and said he hoped God would use it to protect him, Trump said, “I could have used this in Butler.” Everyone would get a challenge coin, he said, and “they have a choice of the coin or meeting Trump. They say, ‘We’ll take the coin, please.’”

He told the guests to eat, suggested some music because “some of you don’t like each other,” and went inside.

Michigan, Iowa and Kansas are still on the list. Trump has just one voice to get through them with.

News.title: Car registered to man accused of planning mass shooting was at Hindu temple he targeted, police say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Illinois authorities believe a 19-year-old man charged with planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in suburban Chicago entered the building’s parking lot on Sunday, hours before police arrested him near his home after receiving a tip about the alleged attack plan.

Authorities announced Wednesday that they had arrested Alexandros Paporakis and provided the additional detail about his suspected movement during a news conference Thursday. The leaders of Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in a statement said a security threat had “targeted our Temple” and announced an increased security presence.

Palatine Police Chief William Nord said a red Acura RDX registered to Paporakis entered a temple parking lot on Sunday around 12:25 p.m. and left less than 15 minutes later. He was seen alone inside the car around 2 p.m., driving near his home in another suburb about 40 miles away.

Paporakis faces felony charges of making a terrorist threat and unlawfully possessing a rifle. Prosecutors have said his co-workers at a Taco Bell location called 911 after Paporakis told them he “couldn't wait to kill Indian people” and said Sunday would be the “special day.”

Temple adds security after threat

Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in Aurora, around 40 miles west of downtown Chicago, said leaders were in contact with police.

“Please know that the safety of our devotees, employees and volunteers is our highest priority, and we have implemented additional security measures effective immediately, including increased armed security presence at the Temple,” a statement said.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, who represents Illinois' 8th congressional district, said he was at the Hindu temple on Sunday.

“I visited not knowing that there was an attacker lying in wait with a sinister motive to commit a mass shooting, and only because his AR-15 weapon jammed was he not able to commit a massacre that day," Rep. Krishnamoorthi told The Associated Press on Thursday.

Rep. Krishnamoorthi said he had increased his security in response to the alleged planned attack. He called on the FBI to “investigate and prosecute this particular matter as a hate crime,” and the Trump administration to release federal nonprofit security grants to bolster security at religious institutions.

“People are really shaken up,” he added.

Court records detail the accused attacker's words

Paporakis told a coworker on Sunday afternoon that his gun jammed and he left quickly, but promised to “retry,” according to prosecutors. He sent the coworker a video showing an AR-style rifle and a photo of himself wearing a tactical vest, they added.

Paporakis also sent the coworker an eight-page manifesto called “Why I fought: A.K.A. (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto)" in which he described non-white people as “subhumans” and expressed a plan to “sacrifice myself to take revenge on the world," according to prosecutors. In the document, he described himself as a “sociopathic white supremacist Neo Nazi," they say.

Police arrested Paporakis later that day. Detectives who searched his home found an AR-style rifle without a serial number, loaded magazines and “hundreds of rounds” of ammunition, a gas canister labeled with a slur referring to South Asians, a tactical vest and a patch depicting Nazi symbolism, authorities say.

Paporakis' mother was questioned, but she is not cooperating with the investigation, police said on Thursday.

At a Wednesday court appearance, a judge ordered Paporakis to remain in detention. His next court hearing is scheduled for Oct. 30.

“This case is in the earliest stage of what will likely be a lengthy process,” the office of the Cook County Public Defender, which is representing Paporakis, said in a statement emailed to The AP. "We would remind the public that statements made by police and prosecutors are only allegations and that cases can change significantly as they continue to be investigated.”

The targeting of the Hindu temple is another example of heightened threats in the last few years against South Asians in the U.S., according to Stop AAPI Hate, the national reporting center for anti-Asian hate incidents. Online slurs and threats have risen significantly, co-founder Manjusha Kulkarni said in a statement.

“We are grateful this violent plot was thwarted and that no one was hurt – but it doesn’t erase the fear Hindu, Indian, and South Asian people feel after years of escalating hate,” Kulkarni said. “Violence against South Asian people is not inevitable. It is fueled when leaders stoke fear of immigrants and people of color for political gain.”

She attributed some of the anti-South Asian sentiment to the Trump administration’s rhetoric around Indian immigrants who hold work visas. She also pointed to a Texas Republican last month posting a social media video of South Asian students cheering at a University of Texas football game and referring to them as “foreigners.”

The temple, like other Hindu temples and households around the country, has been celebrating Navratri, a Hindu festival that lasts nine days. It “should be a time for celebration and unity, not terror and hate,” Kulkarni said.

___

Associated Press writer Terry Tang in Phoenix contributed to this report.

___

Mayes-Osterman is a corps member for The Associated Press/Report for America Statehouse News Initiative. Report for America is a nonprofit national service program that places journalists in local newsrooms to report on undercovered issues.

News.title: Is it safe to travel to Turkey? Deadly flooding prompts Foreign Office update
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Two people have died in Istanbul after heavy rain caused severe flooding, while nearly 600 people needed to be rescued after being stranded.

A 14-year-old was electrocuted after stepping in a puddle at a park in the Fatih district, and a 34-year-old slipped on a sidewalk in the Sariyer district and hit their head.

Residents have been advised to stay home unless travel is absolutely necessary. Homes and buildings have been flooded, schools have shut, and roads have become inaccessible due to the high water levels.

Images from Istanbul show vehicles stranded in floodwaters, with debris piling up on submerged streets.

The rain also appears to have affected flights in and out of the city, with at least 53 cancelled on Thursday across both Istanbul’s main airports.

Istanbul is a popular city for tourists, attracting visitors with its historic bazaars, traditional Turkish hamams, and a blend of Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman architecture.

If you are planning a trip to Istanbul, or are already in the city, here is the latest travel advice.

What does the UK government say?

The UK’s Foreign Office (FCDO) has warned travellers of heavy rainfall that has caused flooding.

It says people should monitor local media and follow the instructions of local authorities, including evacuation orders.

What do Turkish authorities say?

Residents were advised by Istanbul Governor Davut Gül to remain indoors.

“Avoid going outside unless absolutely necessary, and refrain from driving your private vehicles,” he said.

“Do not stay in basement levels or areas at risk of flooding; stay away from puddles, stream beds, and underpasses prone to flooding. Keep away from areas at risk of landslides and buildings in those areas.

open image in gallery A man walks over damaged vehicles piled up in a flooded residential neighbourhood after heavy rains in Istanbul ( Reuters )

“In emergencies, call the 112 Emergency Call Centre. Please follow official announcements.”

Nuri Aslan, the city's deputy mayor, said that the rainfall has been among the heaviest in recent years.

He added that normal operations have been restored on the M9 metro line and the T1, T3, and T5 tram lines, and that roads are currently being cleared.

“Although the rainfall has largely subsided, our work continues. I kindly ask all our citizens to stay away from risky areas, puddles of water, and roads that have been closed to traffic,” Mr Aslan said on Thursday, 15 October.

Will the rain and flooding continue?

The Turkish State Meteorological Service said on Thursday that the heavy rainfall affecting the eastern part of the Marmara region is expected to subside by tonight, but is then forecast to start again on Friday.

It said: “Rainfall is expected to resume in the region from Friday morning, and is predicted to be particularly heavy in Istanbul, especially the northern districts on the European side, and in eastern Kırklareli. The rainfall is expected to intensify from Friday night and continue strongly across Istanbul and the surrounding areas of Kırklareli on Saturday, 17 October.

“Given that the adverse conditions caused by the heavy rainfall on 14 October are still ongoing, authorities and citizens should be cautious and take precautions against the new rain system, which carries risks of floods, water inundation, lightning, and landslides.”

Is the rain impacting flights?

Data from Flightradar says that 41 flights have been cancelled at Istanbul airport as of 3.15pm local time Thursday, with over 556 delays.

The city’s secondary hub, Sabiha Gökçen International airport, has seen 12 cancellations and 272 delays.

The situation was worse on Wednesday, 14 October, with a collective 89 cancellations and more than 1,000 delays.

open image in gallery A drone view shows partially submerged lorries on a flooded street after heavy rains in Istanbul ( Reuters )

As a passenger, you are covered by UK law if you are departing from an airport in the UK on any airline, arriving at an airport in the UK on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline.

Airlines must provide you with care and assistance if your flight is cancelled.

Can I cancel my trip to Istanbul?

As the FCDO has not warned against non-essential travel to Turkey, there will be no special circumstances in place to be able to cancel a trip for a full refund.

The conditions for cancelling your trip depend on your holiday provider, so it’s best to contact them if you’re looking to postpone.

There is no obligation for companies to refund bookings if you want to cancel, and you will not be able to claim on your travel insurance due to safety concerns unless government advice changes.

If you do have travel insurance, some policies include natural disaster cover for an event that prevents you from reaching your holiday destination. Check your insurance policies and speak to your insurer to see where you stand.

News.title: Greece’s President snubs Kimberly Guilfoyle of traditional honor as she leaves ambassador role
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Greek President Konstantinos Tasoulas snubbed Kimberly Guilfoyle of a traditional farewell as she leaves her ambassadorship after a bombshell report alleged she begged a Trump donor to pay off her six-figure credit card bill.

Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece, resigned Tuesday after the White House asked her to step aside following a series of troublesome reports that have raised questions about her conduct in office.

Had the 57-year-old former Fox News host’s tenure ended under normal circumstances, she would’ve received a sendoff by top officials, according to a report.

“Protocol has it that with every outgoing ambassador a courtesy call is placed with the head of state, the prime minister and the foreign minister,” a source at the Athens embassy told the Daily Mail. “However, because of her sudden ousting she will not be allowed to say goodbye.”

Tasoulas's office confirmed to the outlet that there are no current plans for Guilfoyle to to receive the formal farewell.

open image in gallery Kimberly Guilfoyle will not have a ceremonial farewell as she leaves her role as the US ambassador to Greece, according to a report ( Getty )

However, a top aide for the Greek leader speculated that Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to Donald Trump Jr., may try to force an official goodbye.

“She is so brazen that no one is discounting she might show up anyway to try to force a grand farewell despite her current ignominy,” the aide told the Mail. “Anyone would be enormously embarrassed to do that, but this is Kimberly.”

Staffers at the U.S. Embassy in Athens said her departure is “unprecedented.”

“We have never seen such a violent beheading of the mission. Usually, these push-outs happen quietly. This was abrupt,” a staffer told the outlet.

“There is no semblance of shock, rather relief that she’s been fired. She was horrible and mean and spoke down to just about everybody,” another staffer said. “She simply wouldn’t listen to anyone, even the most experienced career diplomats surrounding her.”

Guilfoyle’s resignation came nearly a week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she begged wealthy MAGA donor Eric Deters for $100,000 to pay off her American Express bill.

In exchange for the funds, she offered Deters help getting the Trump administration to look into his personal tax and legal issues. However, a lawyer for Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of the messages to the outlet.

open image in gallery Greece’s President Konstantinos Tasoulas will not give Guilfoyle a traditional send off as she leaves her post, according to a report ( AFP/Getty )

Deters, a retired Kentucky lawyer, has filed a defamation lawsuit against Guilfoyle.

Guilfoyle faced further trouble after The Wall Street Journal published another report claiming that she was caught on an audio recording raging about not being invited to a dinner party with the Trump family.

News of Guilfoyle leaving her post came Tuesday, when the new White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia revealed that President Donald Trump had asked her to resign.

“She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well,” Zacharia told reporters.

On social media, Guilfoyle thanked Trump for the opportunity to serve and vowed to “vigorously” fight the “false” allegations against her.

“Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime,” she wrote. “From my first day as Ambassador, I have worked tirelessly to advance President Trump’s America First agenda, strengthen our strategic alliance with Greece, and deliver meaningful victories for the American people.”

News.title: Breaking Bad actor’s barbecue restaurant files for bankruptcy
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A “Breaking Bad” has filed for bankruptcy to help save the historic California restaurant he owns.

Dean Norris and his wife, Bridget, have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy for the Swing Inn Cafe on September 25 through its business entity, Main Street Eeeatery LLC, according to court documents reviewed by Patch. The filing lists nearly $1.8 million in liabilities and just $147,810 in assets.

Norris, 63, who played DEA agent Hank Schrader on the hit crime drama starring Bryan Cranston, and his attorney wife, Bridget, took over the 99-year-old Temecula, California, restaurant in August 2022. They transformed the longtime eatery into a barbecue restaurant that also serves breakfast, hoping to give back to the city they had called home for more than 20 years.

The filing does not necessarily mean the restaurant will close permanently. Chapter 11 allows businesses to restructure their debts while continuing to operate.

open image in gallery 'Breaking Bad' star Dean Norris and his wife, Bridget, who took over the historic Temecula restaurant Swing Inn Cafe in 2022, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 25 through their business entity, Main Street Eeeatery LLC ( Google Maps )

The filing lists $1.57 million in secured debt owed to Byline Bank, making it the restaurant’s largest reported obligation, The U.S. Sun reports. The business also cited what it described as a “predatory loan” structure as a reason for seeking bankruptcy protection.

The restaurant has a history dating back nearly a century. It opened in 1927 as Mother’s Cafe and underwent several name changes over the decades before becoming Swing Inn Cafe. It remains a fixture in Temecula’s Old Town district, attracting fans hoping to meet Norris, who appears to visit regularly, according to the restaurant’s social media.

The financial troubles come as Norris also mourns the death of his former “Breaking Bad” co-star RJ Mitte, who died by suicide Monday. Mitte’s character was Norris’ nephew on the show.

open image in gallery Dean Norris and his wife, Bridget, bought the 99-year-old Swing Inn Cafe in August 2022 ( Getty )

“Oh my God! Was working just found out about RJ I am heartbroken,” Norris wrote online. “Though RJ didn’t play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set.”

“He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed. This is so heartbreaking, I can’t believe it. Thinking of him and his family,” Norris added.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

News.title: A one-night US hotel stay has never been more expensive
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hotel rates in the U.S. hit an all-time high of $179.43 per night at the end of September - but don’t worry, there are simple hacks to find a discount.

For the tens of millions of people planning to travel in the coming months for holidays - even a two- or three-night hotel stay could be cost-prohibitive, especially if travelers have to pay for airfare, too.

But experts say there are multiple methods consumers can use to find affordable hotel rates even during the busiest seasons of the year.

That’s because hotel prices change constantly based on a few main factors, said Tim Gunstone, chief communications officer at travel tech firm HotelPlanner.

open image in gallery The average US price for a hotel room has hit a new side. But finding an affordable room doesn’t have to be a hassle as there are helpful online tools paired with basic travel knowledge can simplify a traveler’s search ( Getty Images )

“Hotel pricing is highly dynamic and based entirely on supply and demand,” Gunstone said in an email to The Independent. “Rates fluctuate based on the time of year, the day of the week, and how busy the destination is expected to be.”

Flexibility is an important baseline, he said - if your dates aren’t set, you can increase your chances of booking cheaper hotel reservations.

Blind buying

Travel sites Priceline and Hotwire sell discounted rooms to travelers willing to pay for their stay without knowing the hotel name or location at checkout. Once the reservation is made and paid for, the site reveals the hotel.

While risky, the method can save travelers a considerable amount of cash - up to 31 percent for a four-night stay in New York City from November 25 to November 29:

Priceline Express Deal: A four-star hotel in the World Trade Center-Wall Street area goes for 26 percent off its usual price

Hotwire: A four-star hotel in the World Trade Center-Wall Street area goes for 31 percent off its usual price

Travelers should note that blind buys are often nonrefundable. If the traveler doesn’t like their hotel, they cannot get their money back if they cancel.

Sunday funday

Popular destinations often see a rush of travelers come in for the weekend, which means that Fridays and Saturdays can be expensive nights for hotel stays.

But once those travelers leave, demand usually dies down and hotels are more likely to offer better rates.

“Look at city center hotels on a Sunday night,” Gunstone said. “The weekend travelers have left, which often results in great rates.”

Travelers can save as much as 15 percent by checking-in on Sundays, according to Hotel.com’s 2026 Hotel Price Index study.

Google’s surprising travel tools

The average person spends about five hours researching flights and hotels and viewing 141 web pages in the 45 days before they book, according to a 2023 study by travel site Expedia.

Travelers looking for a hotel room can skip their five-hour search by typing the name of the destination and “hotels” into Google’s search bar, said travel site Nomadic Matt.

Google’s search results provide a comprehensive and easy-to-filter list of hotels it pulls from travel booking and hotel websites. It provides an interactive map with the hotel results, too.

open image in gallery ‘Look at city center hotels on a Sunday night. The weekend travelers have left, which often results in great rates’ one expert said ( AFP via Getty Images )

The site provides three tabs across the top of the hotel results list:

Where to stay: Provides a list of neighborhoods at the destination accompanied by a score based on visitor reviews, average hotel rates, a description of the neighborhood, and what it’s known for

When to visit: Tells travelers the average weather, crowd sizes and average hotel prices for each month of the year

What you’ll pay: Details average prices for hotel star levels from one to five.

Travelers get a quick overview of the destination and its hotel prices in a few seconds, making it easy to find the lowest rates.

“That’s why it’s the best booking site - because, rather than searching every website individually, you can just go to Google, find which website has the cheapest rate, and book there,” Nomadic Matt wrote.

News.title: Economy slows before Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
The Chancellor said banks are too often seen as “distant financial institutions”, in a sign he will not raise taxes on the industry in the Budget.

John Healey has faced pressure to impose a windfall tax on bank profits to help rebuild an expected decline in his wiggle room in the public finances.

John Healey said: “My observations on the banks are just that people too often see them as a big distant financial institutions when they are hardwired into the economic fabric of this country and our future prospects.

“That said, you know I’ve got decisions to take in the Budget, and I will. I’ll set those out in two weeks’ time.

“And my special responsibility as Chancellor is to protect the resilience of the British economy for the future. That the resilience that the IMF has reported on this week by upgrading our growth figures in the UK this week, that the welcome monthly growth figures published this morning reinforce, and importantly, alongside that, the IMF reports said that Britain stands out for our deficit reduction plans, and will have his forecast actually a reflection not just on forecast plans but performance over the last couple of years. You know, a consolidation plan in place and underway.

“I’ve said from day one and week one, and I’ve had Andy Burnham in lockstep alongside me, I will meet those fiscal rules in full.

“That will be part of the Budget that I set out in two weeks’ time, and I think the IMF report reinforces that that is not just a not just a reinforcing the strength of Britain’s position, but something that they say they want to see other countries doing as well.”

News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

Sports.title: Torreense 1 Sunderland 2: Sadiki snatches 93rd-minute winner to seal from-behind win as Black Cats maintain 100% record
Sports.content:
Next

NOAH SADIKI’S rocket got Sunderland out of jail as they escaped Europa League embarrassment in Torreense.

The DR Congo star’s unstoppable injury time drive sealed a 2-1 win after the Black Cats were forced to come from behind.



Torreense, currently 15th in the second tier, shocked everyone by defeating giants Sporting Lisbon to lift the Portuguese Cup last season.

And they looked set for another huge giantkilling when centre-half Volnei Feltes unleashed a 25-yard screamer straight past Robin Roefs just before the break.



But Sunderland’s midfield duo of Jules Ahoka and Sadiki got them out of jail late on to maintain Regis Le Bris’ side’s 100 per cent start after last month’s win over AZ Alkmaar.

Le Bris, on the back of three-straight defeats in the top-flight, made seven changes from the side that lost 2-0 to Brighton on Sunday with only the goalscorers, ‘keeper Roefs and Trai Hume remaining.

Stand-in skipper Luke O’Nien should have scored from a backpost header early on before Ukrainian forward Timur Tutierov had an effort chalked off.

But they went in trailing at the break thanks to Feltes’ thunderstrike and it was not until a quadruple change on the hour that Sunderland sprang into life.

But Parker believes United should prioritise strengthening their backline rather than chasing the Norwegian, with Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly topping his list.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez’s outburst seems straight out of the Cristian Romero playbook – divorce from Man Utd feels inevitable
Sports.content:
Next

THE Lisandro Martinez furore at Manchester United feels eerily reminiscent of his Argentine pal Cristian Romero at Tottenham last season.

And just like with Romero, there are suspicions that Martinez’s barbs towards the higher-ups may be motivated more by self-interest than first thought, despite them striking a chord with a frustrated fanbase.



Martinez, nicknamed “The Butcher”, stuck the knife into the powers-that-be – specifically director of football Jason Wilcox – in an explosive post-match interview following Tuesday’s 2-0 defeat to Romero’s Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The tough-tackling centre-back gave those running the club a kicking over what he felt was underinvestment in the team in the summer following last season’s “fantastic season”.



Singling out Wilcox, he told Amazon Prime: “We have to bring in more players to compete. I expect more from our technical director, I have to be honest.”

His comments sent shockwaves through United, who were already reeling from a bad start to the season.



They have put Wilcox in a tough spot where his authority has been undermined.

While former captain Roy Keane has branded the club “a circus” following the storm.

Martinez’s jibes were not without foundation – United’s summer transfer business has certainly looked questionable so far – albeit a little rich given his own poor form.

Indeed, it was his substandard defending that allowed Dominic Solanke to head home an injury-time leveller for ten-man Spurs at United on Saturday. He also scored a comical own-goal in the 1-1 draw at Fulham.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Yet on further inspection, they have raised eyebrows even more because of his contractual situation.

Martinez is in the final year of his deal but is said not to want to extend and would ideally like a move to Spain.

United have a one-year option they can trigger on his terms should they want to.

Martinez’s angry rant would likely make that extra 12 months far less appealing.

Speaking to The Athletic, sources close to Martinez have rejected the notion that his outburst was part of a strategy to force his way out or to convince United not to take up his option. That he would have said it anyway even if he was contracted for another half a decade to the club.



Yet would anyone be surprised if this was now part of the end-game for Martinez at Old Trafford?

That is certainly how it played out with Romero at Spurs last season.

Tottenham’s World Cup winner had seemingly pushed for a move the previous term, including doing an interview he set up himself where he spoke of his desire to play in La Liga.

But when it did not happen, Romero stunned the fanbase by signing a new four-year deal and was named captain by then-boss Thomas Frank.

He turned out to be an unreliable skipper for many reasons, chiefly through the SEVEN games he missed via suspension in the Premier League as Spurs floundered.



But Romero also went to war with the board through one particularly incendiary Instagram post.

Following January’s 3-2 loss at Bournemouth, he accused the Spurs hierarchy of lying.

Romero wrote at the time: “Apologies to all fans of you who follow us everywhere, who are always there and will continue to be.

“We are responsible, there’s no doubt about that. I am the first.



“But we will keep facing up to it and trying to turn the situation around, for ourselves and for the club.

“At times like this, it should be other people coming out to speak, but they don’t – as has been happening for several years now.

“They only show up when things are going well, to tell a few lies.”

He later removed the “tell a few lies” comment from the post, but his point had been made and long-term future was thrown into doubt.

Many Spurs fans applauded Romero for telling it like it is after years of underachievement in the Premier League.



Yet it paved the way for what felt like an inevitable exit in the summer, when Romero finally got his dream move to Atletico in a £34.2million deal – which was less than half what Spurs had hoped to get just a year prior.

Tellingly, Atleti boss Diego Simeone revealed after signing Romero that the centre-back had “wanted to come here for two years”.

Martinez and Romero would surely both argue they were just speaking their mind out of frustration and passion for the club they proudly represent failing to live up to expectations.

Some supporters certainly appreciated their candour and felt it spoke for their own indignation against those running their respective clubs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But there will be other fans who will see Martinez as following the same exit-strategy playbook Romero was accused of using at Spurs.



That is to call out the club’s hierarchy in public to such an extent that a departure feels like the natural, perhaps even only, consequence.

"Our independence is absolute and my independence personally is absolute. I made it very clear last year that if have any form of Government interference on the way we operate is going to result in me resigning from this role and I stand by that completely.

"I should say, to be crystal clear, we've come under absolutely no political pressure on this or any other topic and I don't expect to in the future. Ministers know full well that we are going to act completely independently."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes 'deserves respect' after 'carrying history of Man Utd on his shoulders'
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes 'deserves respect' after 'carrying history of Man Utd on his shoulders'

Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes has been defended by former player Ander Herrara, who has hit out at the criticism levelled at the Portuguese playmaker

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has not been at his best this term as Man Utd struggle for form (Image: Getty Images)

Ander Herrera has told the critics to stop hammering Bruno Fernandes and show the Manchester United captain more respect. Fernandes has faced some flak following a mediocre start to the new season.

‌



‌



The midfielder has been nowhere near his best, with United winning just two of their opening nine games in all competitions.

‌



But former United star Herrera has leapt to the defence of Fernandes - and insisted he deserves huge gratitude for carrying the team on his back in recent seasons.

‌



Appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, Herrera said: "For me, he's a leader. He has had Manchester United on his back a lot of years, a lot of seasons. Sometimes playing, I'm not going to say alone, but carrying the history of the club on his shoulders.

‌



"In difficult times he was there, always putting his face there, asking for the ball, scoring goals, assisting. After defeats, going to the media to talk. I have huge respect for him, for what he has done for the club. And he could have left the club and he's still there, putting his face in difficult moments and he deserves credit. A lot of credit. How can Bruno be the problem? He has been a solution a lot of times."

Michael Carrick is feeling the heat, following a woeful run of six games without a win. But Herrera remains convinced Carrick is the right man for the job - and will bring success back to the fallen giants.

He said: "We have to give him time because, as I told you before, the Premier League that I found was not the same Premier League that you found. And Michael, when he got in charge, the Premier League now is not top four, top five. It's almost top eight.

‌



View 2 Images Ander Herrera insists Michael Carrick is the right man to lead the club (Image: Getty)

"So I think we have to give time to the coaches, to the managers, to build something, to create something. And I think Carrick is the man. I want him to be the man, but I also believe he is the man to bring trophies to the club. I don't know if he will win the Premier League in two or three years, but he is going to be there. He's going to be competing. I'm sure of that."

Herrera spent five years at United, winning four trophies, including the FA Cup and he was left heartbroken when United bosses failed to give him a new and improved deal. Instead, the club wrote him a letter informing him of a 12 month extension, which left him so fuming he decided to join Paris Saint Germain.

‌



Herrera added: "After my third season, when I won the 'Player of the Year' award, I expected the club to come to me. I said to my agent, 'whatever they offer is going to be OK. I'm going to sign because I want to stay at United. I'm so happy.

"They didn't come, so I started to feel sad. And I remember what killed me is when they sent me that letter saying we are going to renew automatically your fifth season at the club. They didn't even call me to say, 'Ander, we want you to stay'. They sent me a letter. When I received that letter I thought, 'I'm done'. My heart was already a little bit broken."

Sports.title: Man City misdemeanours will not impact on football's integrity - only the Premier League's
Sports.content:
Right, a confession. I’m not spectacularly bothered by Manchester City’s cheating. Of course, in a professional capacity, I’m obliged to find it outrageous, abhorrent even.

In a professional capacity, I’m compelled to portray the proprietors of the club as pariahs and be sickened by the sight of its current stars carrying on with life as normal.

Personally, though, I’m not dramatically fussed. That’s the truth. Their years of impropriety had no significant impact on my club - if it had, my feelings would certainly be different - and I quite enjoyed watching their brand of football. That’s the truth.

Like anyone who values fairness in sport, I deplore and condemn City’s deception but I haven’t lost a wink of sleep over it. Of course, they should be punished severely. I hope they are. What they did was fundamentally wrong. If the punishment includes removing all the honours won during the period when the offences took place, then fine.

‌



They probably won’t have the appetite for it, but the Premier League should be scrutinising City’s accounts from the most recent eight years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

City absolutely deserve all that is coming to them. But the bottom line is that a competition that has prided itself on its financial might has been undermined by one of its mightiest financial institutions breaking its financial rules. There is an irony in there somewhere.

‌



Who do we feel sorry for in this saga? The players and fans of the clubs who might have won the league had it not been for City’s fiscal chicanery. Obviously. But it doesn’t necessarily work that way. And there is no way I’m dabbing away tears for John W Henry and the owners of Liverpool, or the Glazer family and the owners of Manchester United.

We should all be outraged, the argument goes, because City’s scandalous behaviour has threatened the integrity of the game. Only it hasn’t. It has threatened the integrity of the Premier League. That is different. And for some, the Premier League is becoming hard to love. Take the champions, for instance.

Arsenal have always been a club that is easy to like. Great traditions. Do things the right way. Now, they have told staff that 60 jobs could be under threat at a time when the fanfare over Mikel Arteta’s new £20million-a-year contract has barely died down. Explain it how you like, that is a dreadful look.

View 2 Images Arsenal's recent redundancy announcement has not painted them in a good light (Image: Getty Images)

‌



So, when supporters of clubs outside the Premier League are asked about Manchester City’s misdemeanours, there is often little more than a shrug. The EFL is great, the non-league scene is great. There are wonderful storylines throughout the pyramid - and none of them involve VAR.

Last season, just under 24 million supporters went to an EFL match. And that figure will be matched or bettered this season, that is for sure.

The Premier League is also sensationally popular, there is no denying that. But the demographic status of the match-going Premier League fan is probably changing. Outside the Premier League, support comes overwhelmingly from local communities.

Sure, the State of the Game report from the Independent Regulator - published this week - paints a picture of a pyramid that is in dire financial trouble, with so many clubs on the brink of disaster. But that has always been the case. From my viewpoint, the love of the game has never been stronger on these shores.

‌



And Manchester City’s grave misdemeanours will not change that. Of course, there will be ramifications in the Premier League. But the game will go on and will be enjoyed up and down the land, regardless.

Sports.title: Mikel Merino opens up on Arsenal’s secret meeting that ‘won the Premier League’
Sports.content:
Mikel Merino opens up on Arsenal’s secret meeting that ‘won the Premier League’

Arsenal ended their long wait for a Premier League title last season, with Mikel Arteta’s side beating Manchester City to the trophy but there were moments where their title push was in doubt

View 2 Images Mikel Merino in action for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Merino believes that a players-only meeting after last season’s draw with Wolves pushed Arsenal towards the Premier League title. The Gunners finally ended their long wait for the crown, with Mikel Arteta finally leading his side to the trophy.

‌



‌



There were some moments where it was in doubt. Arsenal blew a 2-0 lead to draw with relegation-bound Wolves in January, while they also lost back-to-back games to Bournemouth and Manchester City in April.

‌



Merino has revealed that the squad got together after the draw with Wolves and believes that was a huge driving force behind their eventual success.

‌



Writing in the Players Tribune, the Spanish midfielder said: “One slip, and all we heard was ‘same old Arsenal’. To be honest, there were doubts inside the team too. Giving away a 2–0 lead should never happen. But the day after the game, the players had a meeting inside the dressing room, without the boss. Everyone spoke up.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“Nobody talked about tactics. This was about how a group of human beings handle adversity together. I spoke about how I saw the team from the outside, and I said that this was something we as players had to handle, because the boss couldn’t do everything for us.

“When one person has so many tasks at one club, you need leaders who can figure things out on their own. Well, at this club, we do.

“In my view, that was the day we won the title. Even when we lost to Bournemouth and City, that meeting kept us together. We decided to use all the criticism as fuel, and thanks to social media we saw everything.

‌



“We were bottlers. Runners-up. Second, second, second. Boring. Set-piece team. Couldn’t score from open play. Couldn’t handle the pressure. When they questioned our professionalism, we grew even closer.

View 2 Images Mikel Merino helped Arsenal to the Premier League title last season (Image: Getty Images)

“The guy with the bottle on TV? We just laughed. ‘Bantah,’ like the English say.

Article continues below

“The boss was on fire. Every team talk, he reached into our hearts. He spoke about looking out for one another, like a family. The culture we have is thanks to him. Even when the world expected us to collapse, I felt confident that the title would be ours.”

In the end, Arsenal won their last five games of the season and were officially crowned as champions with a match to spare after Manchester City were held by Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Roy Keane tears into Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire as Lisandro Martinez fine demanded
Sports.content:
Roy Keane tears into Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire as Lisandro Martinez fine demanded

Roy Keane has slammed the Manchester United dressing room leaders following Lisandro Martinez's explosive post-match outburst

View Image Roy Keane has singled out two Man United players for criticism amid Martinez's outburst

Roy Keane has criticised Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire for failing to maintain discipline in the Manchester United dressing room, following Lisandro Martinez's outspoken comments about the club's hierarchy after Tuesday night's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid. The Argentine defender questioned United's lack of investment during the summer transfer window and singled out Jason Wilcox for criticism.

‌



‌



He also voiced concerns over the quality of the squad and that is thought to have sparked a clash with a United teammate on the flight back to Manchester. Martinez's remarks have sparked debate among pundits, with Keane now turning his attention to Fernandes and Maguire.

‌



The former United captain believes the pair should be doing more to set an example, but instead has suggested they are too 'busy podcasting.' The Red Devils' captain, Fernandes, appeared on Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast in the summer, where he appeared to take a dig at Keane.

‌



Man Utd told to suspend Lisandro Martinez immediately despite new public statement READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Meanwhile, Maguire, who was left out of Thomas Tuchel's England World Cup squad, appeared on The Rest Is Football podcast in New York.

Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast, Keane said: "Bruno, Maguire... They're probably busy doing podcasts, I can't imagine them pulling him [Martinez]. Bruno's body language, he doesn't seem a happy lad at the moment.

‌



"They're pulling nobody. This reflects where Manchester United are and where this dressing room is. Maguire gets left out of the England squad - he's all upset with that. Instead of rolling his sleeves up during the summer, 'I'm going to go to New York and do a podcast for a few weeks.'

"That's his mindset. I made a mistake with Bruno on this programme. Bruno goes on a podcast with [Steven Bartlett] this is the Man United captain, he goes on there, has a little dig at me, no problem, he's entitled to respond.

"That's the mindset of a Man United player, I'm going to start doing these little gigs instead of getting Man United competing at the very top. So this idea, when I see a player have a little b**** the last few days, I'd be more annoyed at Maguire and Bruno for getting things off their chests on podcasts. You get your priorities in place as a footballer.

‌



Keane continued: "Back in our day it was more magazines than podcasts, but if a player went off and said something, even silly, he'd come in the dressing room, and lads would say: "What are you talking about?" You'd put him in his place in that sense - not a big bust-up.

"Man United is a circus. If you can, try and do your talking on the pitch. If you have to let off a bit of steam, ok, but try and do it on the back of some victories, or when you've won a league title or something like that.

"These players have done nothing for the last few years at Man United. Two years ago we were finishing 13th (15th) or whatever, getting knocked out by Grimsby, and they're coming up with all these comments."

‌



The Stick to Football panel, featuring Keane, Gary Neville, Steven Gerrard, Ian Wright and Jill Scott, agreed that Martinez's criticism of the club's recruitment could cause friction within the dressing room.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

However, it remains unclear which player challenged Martinez over his comments, although his outburst is understood to have angered several members of the squad.

‌



At the time, a fuming Martinez told Amazon Prime: "Really poor performance, really poor. I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it is the reflection, the mirror, for our club at the moment. A fantastic season last season, but now we are far from the top. We have to bring in more players to compete.

"Look at Atletico, they had an amazing team, they deserved to win. I expect more, from everyone. More investment? Yes, 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director, I have to be honest. As players, we have to do more, but it’s also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this sort of night.

"Last season we created a base to build an amazing team, but this is something to be honest. It’s annoying to come here with my team and not trying to get an amazing result."

‌



When asked if Michael Carrick was at fault, Martinez added: "I don’t think so. He does his best, but every season is different. Teams know how you play, every detail. If you don’t change each season, it’s a big problem.

"Changing, changing, changing manager? What about other areas? I can’t say more. It’s easy to blame the coach, it’s easy to blame the players, but what about other areas?"

On Wednesday, Martinez wrote a statement on Instagram, explaining his comments and his reaction. He admitted speaking 'out in anger and frustration.'

‌



"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club," he wrote. "To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top. I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment."

United are currently 13th place in the Premier League table and return to league action on Sunday afternoon, when they travel to Elland Road to face rivals Leeds United. Kick-off is scheduled for 2pm.

Article continues below

It remains unclear whether Martinez will feature against Leeds and whether United will take disciplinary action against the defender.

Sports.title: Serbian tennis player handed 24-year ban for match-fixing
Sports.content:
A Serbian tennis player has been handed a massive 24-year ban for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800).

The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Milicevic's suspension will officially come to an end on October 8, 2050, by which time he would be 53 years old.

The ITIA added: "While suspended, Milicevic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association."

Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Spain, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad and said he expected more from "upstairs" after he singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

Sky Sports News understands Martinez met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, on Thursday. Head coach Michael Carrick was also present at the meeting.

In a statement released on Thursday night, the defender said: "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager.

Sports.title: Garcia set to face Lopez next after emphatic Benn win
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez in his next fight after his emphatic victory over Conor Benn last month.

Garcia defended his WBC welterweight title with a second-round stoppage of British contender Benn in Las Vegas and is now holding talks for a fight against Lopez, Sky Sports News understands.

Fellow American Lopez also holds a world title in the same division after he sealed a majority decision win over Rolando Romero to claim the WBA belt in August.

Image: Teofimo Lopez became a world champion again after a win over Rolando Romero

Lopez has been ordered to defend his WBA title against Lancashire fighter Jack Catterall, but is pressing ahead with a fight against Garcia instead.

Benn is yet to confirm his next move after the second loss of his professional career against Garcia.

His long-term trainer Tony Sims has confirmed that Benn will never fight again at welterweight.

The 30-year-old announced on social media that he will spend some time away of the ring, although he continues to be linked with a trilogy fight against Chris Eubank Jr.

Sports.title: Itauma could be one win away from another world title shot
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma could be one victory away from another world title shot.

Itauma, a highly regarded 21-year-old prospect, took on Filip Hrgovic for the IBF belt in August.

It was Itauma's first world championship fight. After starting very strongly, he tired, unravelled and was halted by Hrgovic in nine rounds.

Promoter Frank Warren, however, plans to bring Itauma back in a good level fight in January to set him up for another world title tilt.

"It'll be a decent fight. He's got to be in with somebody who's going to give him a test," Warren told Sky Sports.

"When you're coming off a loss any comeback fight is a risky fight. He'll be wanting to go out there with something to prove. We want to see him in with someone reasonable for the comeback fight and he wants to get back into the mix.

"He's going to have to come back and show what he's all about."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Delicious Orie, Barry Jones and Sam Noakes reflect on Moses Itauma's defeat to Filip Hrgovic.

After that Itauma will be targeting a world champion. As well as promoting Itauma, Warren represents new IBF champion Hrgovic, WBC heavyweight titlist Agit Kabayel, as well as WBO champion Daniel Dubois.

"He wants to be back in the mix so he's going to be very active next year," Warren said of Itauma. "Straight in, no messing about.

"He could fight any of them. Because if he wins he'll be straight back into, I think, the top half of the rankings."

Warren added of Itauma's defeat: "Hrgovic managed to absorb the punishment. Even when [Itauma] was blowing he was still throwing shots, even when he got caught he was still trying to fight back. He did tick some other boxes as far as I was concerned."

Hrgovic is due to face his mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez next. That could be a homecoming fight for Hrgovic in Croatia.

"We're looking at putting him on in Croatia, we're working hard to make that happen, that's his dream," Warren said.

Mike Borao, Sanchez's manager, told Sky Sports: "Looking to make it happen in the first quarter of 2027.

"Everything is tracking well so far. Frank [Sanchez] is confident he'll win and is eager for his chance to become world champion.

"Hrgovic is elite and won't be an easy opponent, but I fully expect Frank to get the job done."

Sports.title: Kane agrees new deal in principle with Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has agreed a new deal in principle with Bayern Munich until the summer of 2029.

The England captain and his family are said to be enjoying life in Munich.

It's understood the Bundesliga club are now finalising the paperwork on his contract extension.

Kane has scored a phenomenal 154 goals in 156 matches since moving from Tottenham to Bayern in 2023. His 73 goals for club and country last season - including the World Cup with England - have put him in strong contention for the men's Ballon d'Or.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane said it would be amazing to win the Ballon d'Or and agrees it's his best chance so far in his career.

During his time at Bayern, he has won two Bundesliga titles - the first in 2025 acting as the first major trophy of his career - as well as last season's German Cup and the German Super Cup in the last two years.

In the last three years, Kane has also won the European Golden Shoe twice - given to the top scorer on the continent - and has won the Bundesliga Golden Boot in each of his three seasons at Bayern.

Kane also took England to the Euro 2024 final during his time with the German giants, as well as leading the Three Lions to their best World Cup finish since 1966 earlier this summer.

Earlier this month, he equalled Peter Shilton's England appearance record by winning his 125th cap, which he will hope to beat in next month's Nations League matches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at all Harry Kane's goals for Bayern Munich from the 2025/2026 Bundesliga season

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

Kane set the record to become the fastest player to 100 goals in the history of the Bundesliga earlier this month.

He didn't just set it, he smashed it, reaching his ton in 98 games - 31 faster than the previous holder, Dieter Muller, whose record had stood for almost half a century.

That was underpinned by the most prolific scoring season of his entire career in 2025/26, netting 36 goals in 31 Bundesliga matches as well as 14 in 13 Champions League matches and, if that wasn't enough, a further 12 strikes for England including six at the World Cup.

Already the best No 9 in the world, Kane has somehow found a way to hit new heights even in his 30s.

Scoring 73 goals in 65 games is, simply, mindblowing. And a fitting reward for maintaining his fitness better than he ever has before - having arrived at previous international tournaments already clearly burnt out.

Others may have picked up bigger team honours but for an individual award, there has been no player in better form on the planet. And what better time to pick up the award than in his home town when the winner is crowned at the London Palladium later this month?

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
Sports.content:
Alex Scott, the former Football Focus host, has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+.

It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

Scott had fronted the streaming platform’s coverage of the elite women’s European club competition since it obtained the rights in 2025. However, Disney’s production levels were criticised after the opening round following a series of technical problems. These included an unscheduled advert break that interrupted the second half of Arsenal’s 1-0 win over HB Køge for more than three minutes.

A spokesperson for Disney+ told the Guardian: “We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women’s Champions League on Disney+. Her passion for the women’s game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success.”

Scott, a former England and Arsenal defender and former contestant on the BBC’s Strictly Come Dancing and ITV’s I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, has also presented major sports shows for the BBC, including coverage of the 2020 Olympics. Scott’s representatives said: “Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future.”

Scott presented the BBC’s Football Focus show for five seasons before its closure this year. At the start of this season’s Women’s Super League campaign she launched One More Word through her own production company, First Cap Productions, and has previously explained that show was createdin response to the BBC cancelling its weekly WSL highlights show.

Scott, who turned 42 on Wednesday, told the Observer, this month: “I feel like there’s always an excuse about women’s football shows not working because of the viewership or needing to save money. Whereas I think if they are done right, they can work, if things are given a fresh idea or a fresh format, they can work.”

In the same interview, discussing some of the criticism aimed at Disney’s Women’s Champions League coverage this term, Scott said: “Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.
