“But nobody sees the conversations, the fights I have behind the scenes. But I can hold my head up and know that I’ve always tried my best for the greater good of women’s sport.”

Sources have told the Guardian the presenter’s relationship with Disney remains positive. Disney, whose coverage is produced by ESPN, secured an exclusive five-year deal to broadcast the Women’s Champions League across European broadcast territories in 2025. It is understood its presenting team will continue to include Shebahn Aherne, Nedum Onuoha and Lianne Sanderson. The lineup includes commentators such as Vicki Sparks and Jacqui Oatley. The competition resumes on 28 October.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
Sports.content:
CITY’S BILLION-POUND BENNY HILL SHOW

It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby!

Not just because Désiré Doué was unplayable or that Vitinha put on an absolute clinic or that Luis Enrique was more forward-thinking than Magnus Carlsen reading a horoscope in playing his right-back as a striker, but also because the camera kept cutting – deliciously – to the faces of glum City fans as they watched their expensively assembled squad spin into such a dizzy mess that £125m Enzo Fernández and £116m Elliott Anderson appeared in Manchester to be auditioning as a double act for next year’s Strictly.

Although PSG eased off in the second half as City rallied to a brave 4-2 home defeat, it was a miserable outing for all of those dressed in sky blue or trendy flatcaps sitting in the stands. Pep Guardiola was – we think – not one of the City fans that had spent the weekend chanting “we’re Man City, we’ll cheat when we want” at Anfield – but the former manager returned to Manchester for a well-timed visit on Wednesday to support City’s beleaguered owners, backing up last month’s statement that he remains “behind my club”.

While we did not hear from Pep on the night as he sloped off from his heated seat back to his sabbatical – with British TV viewers instead treated to the valuable and impartial TNT Sports pundit and literal on-the-payroll City ambassador Joleon Lescott, who “broke his silence on the guilty verdicts” in predictable fashion – we did also enjoy some relatively stain-free football on Wednesday. Aston Villa romped to a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce, Bradley Barcola notched his first Liverpool goals (a hatty) in the 6-3 win at Lask and Real Madrid secured a last-gasp 4-3 win at Roma. In a fast-changing world, it was heartening to feel the warm embrace of familiarity with Madrid manager José Mourinho using his post-match press conference to speak, not of his side’s remarkable comeback (three corners in the final 10 minutes, naturally) or even of his emotional return to the Italian capital after his Tin Pot triumph with Roma in 2022, but as an opportunity to deliver a monologue against Spain’s football authorities. Football is healing.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Michael Butler from 5.45pm for red-hot Bigger Vase updates from the early kick-offs, including Torreense 1-3 Sunderland and Lyon 2-1 Crystal Palace before Simon Burnton takes you through the 8pm starts, including Benfica 2-1 Celtic and Bournemouth 4-1 Sturm Graz.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinícius has a four-match suspension? They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag. A Spanish team that has earned three points for Spanish football, for the rankings, for the prestige of Spanish football. You want to kill a player two hours before the match? It doesn’t seem normal to me.” – José Mourinho laments the timing of the Spanish Football Federation’s announcement that Vinícius Júnior will receive a four-match ban, including ​El ​Clásico, after ​being sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair against Villarreal last Saturday. The announcement came hours before ​Mourinho​’s R​eal Madrid side – featuring Vinícius – faced Roma in the ​B​ig Cup​ last night, coming from behind to earn a 4-3 win.

View image in fullscreen Vinícius Júnior found out about his suspension only a couple hours before kick-off in the Big Cup. Photograph: Matteo Ciambelli/Reuters

double quotation mark I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt.

double quotation mark My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes.

Sports.title: Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meeting
Sports.content:
European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, with the heads of the English and German football associations questioning his fitness to govern after a three-and-a-half-hour council meeting.

Infantino began the long-awaited gathering of Fifa’s 37-strong executive board by apologising for failing to consult them over his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan but failed to provide answers to dozens of questions posed by the European FAs on a range of subjects including the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, Donald Trump’s Fifa peace prize and the Folarin Balogun affair, when the USA striker’s World Cup suspension was overturned after lobbying from the US president.

Infantino’s apology was followed by a 30-minute presentation on FFE from two American lawyers, who described the $20bn (£15.1bn) valuation and proposed sale of a 20% stake to Thrive Capital as a good deal for Fifa. At the insistence of some attenders, the lawyers were asked to leave the meeting after they had presented. When questioned, one of them confirmed he had been commissioned and paid by Fifa to produce a review of FFE.

Quick Guide How do I 

“The main objective for Gianni was to survive this meeting and nothing more,” one council member told the Guardian.

Council members succeeded in deferring, until they receive more information on Balogun, a Fifa proposal to amend its disciplinary regulations by removing the scope for players shown a straight red card to have it rescinded. Infantino pledged to provide that information by their next meeting in Doha on 16 December, after nominations close on 18 November for March’s presidential election.

The issue of whether the Fifa peace prize will be revived this year or Trump left as a standalone winner has been referred to Fifa’s social responsibility committee, and the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, has been appointed to chair a new committee examining governance reform. But otherwise the meeting broke up without tangible answers, to the frustration of the English FA’s chair, Debbie Hewitt.

“We didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested,” Hewitt said. “I think the man [Infantino] has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, he’s not fit to be Fifa president. That was what was shared in the meeting.”

The German FA’s president, Bernd Neuendorf, went further by calling for wholesale reforms of Fifa’s administration, which he hopes will fall within the purview of Sheikh Salman’s governance committee.

“The whole administration has to be reformed and the whole governance has to be reformed,” Neuendorf said. “But I’m pretty clear here that this is not possible with Gianni as the responsible person at Fifa. So we need a complete restart, I think, a political restart of persons who represent Fifa.

“Yes he apologised, but I didn’t have the feeling that this apology was because of the FFE project in total. My impression was it was just because it wasn’t brought forward to the council and no one was involved.”

Neuendorf also said he was “very confident” that an alternative candidate would be found to stand against Infantino, a view shared by senior figures at Uefa, who expect a late declaration to limit the amount of time for Fifa to scupper the nomination.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The respective presidents of the three continental confederations who have called for Infantino to go – Aleksander Ceferin of Uefa, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf and Sheikh Salman – have ruled themselves out and suggestions that high-profile figures such as Arsène Wenger or Michele Kang could put themselves forward have been dismissed.

A proposal to distribute $3.5bn (£2.6bn) from Fifa’s financial reserves, which would involve each national association receiving $25m over the next four-year cycle, was approved by council.

Montagliani is also understood to have been critical of Infantino, but Fifa’s president received strong support from council members from Asia and Africa.

“I am certain that Gianni Infantino is the right president,” Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritania Football Federation said. “The majority want Gianni Infantino to stay. After finally withdrawing this proposal, president Gianni Infantino apologised to the members of the executive committee. This was followed by a responsible debate, during which this issue was more or less shelved.

“In the interests of football, the executive committee is looking ahead and seeking solutions, by focusing on the good aspects that football has to offer and trying to move forward.”

Sports.title: Vinícius claims he is targeted by referees and says flair players need protection
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is not happy with how he is being treated by referees and wants more protection for talented players such as himself, Lamine Yamal and Julián Álvarez.

Vinícius spoke out after Real Madrid’s 4-3 come-from-behind win at Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday. The Brazil forward also acknowledged he was going through a slump, but said he had “no doubt” he would regain his best form soon.

The match against Roma came hours after he was handed a four-game suspension in the Spanish league after being sent off for pulling the hair of an opponent and for protesting against the referee. “I don’t recall any other player receiving a four-match suspension,” he said. “I tried to move the player in front of me out of the way, and I ended up getting caught in his hair.

“That was it – a red card – which is why I was so surprised. I didn’t say a single offensive word to the referee that would warrant a four-match ban. But when it comes to Vini, it’s all too easy. The opposing team will always say it’s justified, and the press will say the same. I understand that. I’m here to keep evolving and improving, because I know where I’ve come from and what I’m capable of achieving.

View image in fullscreen Vinícius Júnior leaves the pitch after his red card against Villarreal. Photograph: Alejandro Martinez Velez/Reuters

“It’s understandable for the opposing fans to jeer me, because my job is to score goals against their team, but I don’t get the referees. I’ve seen the stats: I’ve been on the receiving end of 500 fouls, yet that has only resulted in five red cards. In the end, the yellow cards always seem to go to Vini, to the attacking players. We need to protect the players who bring something different to the game, like Lamine at Barcelona or Julián at Atleti. Defenders are allowed to foul me the entire match but in the end it’s me who gets the card.”

José Mourinho complained about the timing of the announcement of the suspension. “Do you think it’s normal for a player from a Spanish team, preparing for an important match that’s also crucial for Spanish football, to find out about his four-match suspension just two hours before kickoff?” Madrid’s manager said. “We were on the bus about to arrive at the stadium when we found out … they’ve started doing things without any shame.”

Vinícius, who hasn’t scored for Madrid since August, was replaced in the 59th minute of Madrid’s victory before the team rallied from 3-1 down. “I’m working to get back to my best as soon as possible,” Vinícius said. “I know I’m not at my peak right now, but I’ve been through worse, and even when people have doubted me, I’ve always stood up for this club. That’s why I signed a six-year contract extension. The good run of form will return, and the goals will come back, too. I’m certain of that. I have no doubt. I’m here to help the team.”

The 26-year-old downplayed his frustration after Mourinho substituted him. “It’s natural for me to get upset when I’m substituted because I always want to play every single match,” he said. “I’m well aware of my current form and how I’m playing. I’m here to help the team, and sometimes you have to come off so that other players can get on and change the dynamic.

“Mourinho and I have a great relationship. He’s always straight with me. Of course I got a little annoyed when I came off today, but that’s normal. In the end he was right, the team improved, and that’s what matters most.” Vinícius was replaced by Endrick, who scored an 85th-minute equaliser before Antonio Rüdiger gave Madrid the win in the 90th.

Among the games Vinícius will miss because of his suspension is the clásico at Barcelona on 25 October.

Sports.title: Giovanni Leoni’s return from injury delayed in fresh blow to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Giovanni Leoni’s Liverpool return has been delayed because of the severity of the knee injury sustained on his debut, Andoni Iraola has revealed.

The central defender had been expected to resume team training during the recent international break but that schedule has been put back by about a month.

Leoni, a £26m signing from Parma in 2025, sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury against Southampton 13 months ago. Iraola has disclosed the damage extended beyond the ACL and Liverpool must tread carefully with the 19-year-old’s rehabilitation as a consequence.

“It is taking more time than we wanted,” the head coach said. “With Gio, the plan was to train with the team in this past international break. It is probably now going to be the next international break [which starts on 9 November], so we have lost one month in the process.

“With Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department it wasn’t just an ACL. It was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL. I think he has to be very confident in the rehab and the process has to be very careful with him.

“We want to make sure once he comes to the team he stays there in a good place. It’s true we’ve had a little bit of not a setback but a delay, if you want. The plan now is he starts in the next break. It’s not that far off, but a little bit later than we expected.”

Sports.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
Sports.content:
Watching Chelsea this season ought to come with a health warning. Goals arrive in abundance, leads are established before spectators have settled into their seats and clean sheets have become an alien concept. Xabi Alonso has transformed Chelsea into one of the Premier League’s most thrilling spectacles. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 13. That’s 4.7 goals per game in six matches. Chelsea are a neutral’s dream, but is it sustainable?

They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. An 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. The five goals against Bournemouth last weekend came from an xG of just 0.75.

Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers complement each other’s qualities. Palmer’s instinct to drift into pockets of space and dictate attacks gives Chelsea a creative focal point; Rogers provides the direct running and ball-carrying to unsettle defences; and João Pedro offers the movement to stretch opponents in behind and the composure to finish when chances arrive. They rotate roles too, giving defenders a constant headache – they can’t crowd out one of the trio without giving another space.

Their forwards deserve credit for their clinical finishing but Chelsea’s attacking numbers will surely revert to the mean at some point, so they need to improve defensively. They have conceded 13 goals, the joint most in the league, and have not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since January – a run of 22 games. It is a far more volatile position than a serious European contender would want. Alonso’s structure is built to commit players forward; that high-risk, high-reward approach helped his Bayer Leverkusen team win the Bundesliga but Chelsea are not yet set up to protect against the risk.

When they are in possession, both wing-backs, their two attacking midfielders and João Pedro push on. That leaves the back three and two midfielders covering, and one of the central pair often gets pulled forward too. The result is that they lack the protection to deal with turnovers. The midfield is left covering a huge area, the wing-backs leave space in behind, and the back three are left scrambling to defend the gaps.

Chelsea’s 3-0 defeat by Brentford before the international break was a wake-up call for Alonso. Andrews’ side repeatedly targeted the space behind Chelsea’s advanced wing-backs, forcing the midfield to choose between tracking runners out wide and exposing the centre, or holding position and allowing Brentford to progress down the flanks. All three goals exposed Chelsea’s defensive vulnerabilities: the first followed a corner won through pressure down the flank; the second saw Kevin Schade break behind Chelsea’s defence before Thiago converted the rebound; and the third came after Schade was given time and space out wide to cross for a back-post finish.

As Chelsea pushed forward in search of a response, the defence became increasingly stretched. It exposed the central dilemma in Alonso’s system: committing players forward increases their attacking threat but leaves space for opponents to exploit.

The good news for Chelsea fans is that there were encouraging signs in their 5-1 victory over Bournemouth that suggest Alonso used the long international break to find a solution. On first inspection it had all the hallmarks of a standard Chelsea game this season: a two-goal lead inside three minutes, ruthless finishing that defied the xG statistics, a six-goal thriller, and no clean sheet. But look a little deeper and it appears Chelsea may be beginning to find a better balance.

The most significant change was a move to a 4-4-2 shape out of possession, defending in a back four rather than a back three. Josh Acheampong played more like a right-back; Levi Colwill and Maxence Lacroix moved closer together; and Pep Chavarría held back on the left while Neto pushed on the right.

They defended with a more recognisable shape, and the space between the lines was more manageable. The return of Moisés Caicedo was another boost. It provided the team with a vital source of energy, ball-winning and protection in front of the defence – he won seven duels, made the joint-most tackles in the game (four), and the second most defensive contributions (11). Jordan Henderson brought leadership and organisation to the midfield, organising the press with regimented efficiency.

View image in fullscreen Moisés Caicedo’s return from injury made a big difference for Chelsea against Bournemouth. Photograph: David Cliff/EPA

It was by no means a complete solution; they still committed players forward and took risks. Bournemouth managed to exploit lapses and find space behind a number of times; they had 67 entries into Chelsea’s final third compared with Chelsea’s 39. Alonso’s next goal will be to develop a shared understanding among the players. They need to recognise the same triggers, move at the right moment and trust their teammates to cover the spaces they leave behind.

Chelsea are perhaps the Premier League’s most entertaining side, but entertainment does not secure European football. Their finishing is unlikely to stay this ruthless so the defence needs to step up. The performance against Bournemouth offered encouraging evidence that the defence can improve their organisation without sacrificing their threat going forward, and the return of Caicedo gives the midfield the legs and authority it has lacked. If Alonso can turn these positive signs into consistency, Chelsea may become a side capable of thrilling their supporters without putting them through quite so much stress.

This is an article by WhoScored

Sports.title: Southgate ‘hardly watches’ football and does not envisage Premier League return
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate has all but ruled out a return to Premier League management and revealed he “didn’t even enjoy the wins” for more than a couple of minutes towards the end of his time in charge of England.

Southgate, who has moved away from football since stepping down as the manager of the England men’s team after defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final, said he had not attended a game since watching his boyhood club Crystal Palace beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final last year.

The 56-year-old’s only taste of club management came when he spent almost three-and-a-half years at Middlesbrough after replacing Steve McClaren in 2006. Southgate was unable to keep Middlesbrough in the Premier League in 2009 and he indicated during an appearance on the Amol Rajan Connection podcast that he had no interest in seeking a return to top-flight management.

Quick Guide How do I 

“I don’t see a scenario where I do that,” he said. “Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying … at the very least for a period, the wins keep you going. By the end, I didn’t even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I’ve hardly watched football.

“I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I’ve not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed.”

Southgate managed England for almost eight years and came close to ending their hunt for a first men’s trophy since the 1966 World Cup. But he has sought different opportunities since leaving the role. He has launched a podcast and fronted a BBC documentary this year in which he travelled across the UK to understand the challenges facing young men and boys.

“I’ve loved the last 18 months of my life,” Southgate said. “I’ve had 37 years where my sense of self depended on did I win or lose on Saturday. And actually I’ve loved having different experiences.

“I’ve met politicians, I’ve met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I’ve travelled around the world learning things. I’ve just enjoyed playing a different film in my life.”

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits job months after Football Focus cancelled
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has left her role as Women's Champions League presenter on Disney+.

The former England international, who won 140 Lionesses caps, was announced as part of their line-up in September 2025.

2 Scott has left her role as a presenter for the Women's Champions League a year after taking it Credit: Getty

However, as per The Guardian, Scott has made the decision to vacate the role.

"We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women's Champions League on Disney+," a Disney+ spokesperson told the outlet.

"Her passion for the women's game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success."

Scott's representatives added: "Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future."

What will Scott work on next?

Formerly of Arsenal Women, Scott is said to be shifting focus onto separate projects, such as her newly-launched One More Word WSL.

Alongside other ex-England stars in Anita Asante and Fara Williams, the show discusses news from the Women's Super League.

One More Word was launched by First Cap Productions Limited, where Scott is listed as a director on the Companies House website.

Since starting her media career after professional football, the 42-year-old has been best-known for presenting Football Focus.

It was announced in May 2021 that she would succeed Dan Walker, who had fronted the Saturday lunchtime football show for 12 years.

However, the BBC confirmed in April that Football Focus, which first aired in 1974, would not run beyond the 2025/26 season.

2 Scott presented Football Focus for five years before the BBC ended the show earlier this year Credit: Getty

Scott briefly mentioned the decision to end the programme during her opening words on the first episode back since the news broke.

talkSPORT's Martin Keown was a long-term pundit on Football Focus and called it 'an iconic programme'.

He also claimed that Scott was doing an 'exceptional job' as presenter and that its conclusion did not reflect on her.

Scott won five Women's Premier League titles with Arsenal, and then a sixth after it became the Women's Super League in 2010.

She also won the Women's Champions League and was awarded an OBE in 2017 for her 'outstanding contribution to Women's Football'.

Sports.title: Billy Sharp eyes up new job days after retiring from professional football
Sports.content:
Billy Sharp eyes up new job days after retiring from professional football

Former Sheffield United and Leeds striker Billy Sharp has revealed he wants to go into management having hung up his boots.

The 40-year-old, who was the Championship's all-time top scorer, officially announced that he had called time on his career on Sunday.



2 Sharp called time on his career last weekend, having been without a club since leaving Doncaster earlier this year Credit: Getty

Sharp, who scored 299 career goals across a 22-year career, has been without a club since leaving Doncaster Rovers at the end of the season.

He joined Hawksbee & Baker on Thursday to discuss his future plans, where he outlined his intention to move into management.

What did Sharp say?

"I want to be a football manager. Definitely not going to shy away from that," the former striker said live on talkSPORT.



"I know I've got a lot of work to do and a lot of people to influence. And I'm going to watch loads of football.

"I'm passionate about football. I love the game."

Sharp went on to name-check a number of managers he has been studying as he looks to transition into management.



"Whenever I've been sat on the bench the last 10 years, I've always been watching the managers' body language, the way they handle themselves under pressure and how they deal with tactics when something happens with the red card or stuff like that," he continued.

"And I've been learning that side of the game.

"I've been very fortunate to have Chris Wilder, Grant McCann, Liam Rosenior, all people who I could learn off and let me into their environment, which has been helping me as well."



2 Wilder is one of the managers Sharp spoke highly of as he considers a career in management

Potential Blades return?

The experienced hitman did admit that if current Blades boss Wilder did ask him to come out of retirement in order to bag the elusive 300th career goal, he'd happily jump at the chance.

"All Chris [Wilder] has to do is ask me to play," Sharp added. "I'll play for free for Sheffield United, no problem. I probably need to go and do a couple of fitness sessions

"I might come out of retirement. I might miss it in a year, but I'm satisfied. I'm happy."



Sheffield United currently sit 15th in the Championship following their midweek 3-2 loss to Portsmouth.

The result means the Yorkshire side have collected 12 points from the opening 10 games of the season.

Sports.title: Arsenal given renewed hope of Vinicius Jr move after summer ‘regrets’
Sports.content:
Arsenal should not give up hope of signing Vinicius Jr next summer.

That’s the verdict of European football expert Andy Brassell, who says Real Madrid could look to rebuild their team if they fail to win any silverware.

4 Vinicius Jr faces a three game ban - which would see him miss El Clasico Credit: Getty



Arsenal attempted to lure the Brazil international to the Emirates this summer amid a stand off over his contract.

talkSPORT reported the Premier League champions were weighing up an approach for Vinicius Jr.

However, the Gunners always viewed him as an option rather than their top target.

The 26-year-old ended speculation by signing a new contract until 2032.



However, all is not well at the Bernabeu for Vinicius Jr under new manager Jose Mourinho.

He has scored just one goal in 10 games in all competitions this season.



Vinicius Jr came off the bench and put the ball in the back of the net against Villarreal on Saturday, only for the referee to rule it out.

He was adjudged to have pulled the hair of an opponent and was given a red card.



The forward is now on course to miss the first Clasico of the season.

Boss Mourinho has backed him to rediscover his form for Madrid.

4 Mourinho has backed Vinicius Jr to rediscover his form this season - but started him on the bench to face Villarreal Credit: Getty

"He is going to emerge," Mourinho said of Vinicius on Tuesday to TNT Sports. "It's just a question of when."

No longer Vinicius Jr’s team

Madrid spent £120m bringing in Yan Diomande this summer. He and Arda Guler started on the wings for Madrid’s most recent game.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, Brassell said: “When you consider he's signed this new contract, a lot of this season so far has made you think well did they need to? There were definitely people at Real Madrid who would have been happier and would have felt it was cleaner for him to go to Arsenal.



“They could move forward with Mbappe and Diomande, who has really grown into Real Madrid in recent weeks.

“He [Diomande] has done really well on both sides of the international break. Scoring the winner for his first goal for the club against Villarreal, and I think it's not obvious how the front part of Real Madrid fits together anymore. From Vinicius' perspective it's really unfair.

“It’s a real shame because in 2024 this was his team and he was maybe the best player in the world. If not he was really close. They were the best team in Europe or certainly the European champions at least after that win against Dortmund in the final at Wembley.

4 Vinicius Jr has played 385 times for Real Madrid Credit: Getty



“So everything that's happened since has been stuff that's been out of his control and it's diminished his power to be impactful on the field. Most of that has nothing to do with him. They're all decisions that are out of his hands.

“I wonder in that context would it have been better if he went to Arsenal where there's a whole new enthusiasm for him.

“He would get to be a star player on an excellent collective team that, with all due respect to Gabriel and Declan Rice and David Raya, maybe doesn't have that wow factor world superstar in it even though obviously they're clearly one of the very best teams in Europe.

“I would have loved to see that. I think in terms of the discipline of what Arteta wants to do, Vinicius has shown in the past that he can be very very useful without the ball. Not so much recently.



“I think it's fair to say Arteta would have made him into the two way player that he's always destined to be because he's a great athlete, he's super explosive. You make him be as good as he can be off the ball as well.

“We're talking about the best player in the world all over again. I know people have had their theories that Arsenal will use some sort of Trojan horse to make sure his contract was seen over the line. I think he's a little bit more than that. I think there was a genuine possibility of him going there.”

4 Arteta and Arsenal explored the signing of Vinicius Jr in the summer Credit: Getty

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal still on?

Madrid have surprisingly been trophyless for the last two seasons and are facing that prospect for a third.



Barcelona have already won all eight of their LaLiga games this season and look set to defend their title.

Brassell argued this could force Madrid to reshape their team in the summer, possibly opening the door once again for Vinicius Jr’s exit.

He said: “I wonder if we get to the end of this season and Real Madrid have won nothing again for the third straight season. They're faced with some sort of decision. Do you sell Vinicius? Do you sell Mbappe?

“You've got to do something, you can't just leave it as it is. All the time the guy who's probably your best player Jude Bellingham is thinking come on, build a team around me then.



“So whether it's with or without Mourinho if they don't win this season, and I think there's a decent possibility they win nothing this season. They're going to have to have a bit of a rethink

“Maybe that turns out to be the best thing for Vinicius if he goes.”

Sports.title: Graeme Souness: Goal machine Harry Kane is a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but there is one catch
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness: Goal machine Harry Kane is a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but there is one catch

Harry Kane is deserving of winning the Ballon d'Or because he can do the 'hardest thing in football'.

That is according to Graeme Souness, who has hailed the England captain's ability to score goals.

3 Kane has been warned one factor could stop him winning the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

However, he has questioned whether playing in the Bundesliga for Bayern Munich could impact Kane's hopes of glory.

The 33-year-old is amongst the favourites to win the prestigious award later this month.

A ceremony at the London Palladium on Monday, October 2026 will see the latest recipient announced.

Kane is fresh from scoring 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions for Bayern last season.

His strikes helped Vincent Kompany's side win a domestic double as Kane clinched the Bundesliga golden boot and the European Golden Shoe.

He then went on to score six goals in seven matches for England at the World Cup as they finished third in North America.

Can Kane win the Ballon d'Or?

Those numbers can be the difference when it comes to securing the Ballon d'Or, says Souness.

Speaking to Alan Brazil and Tony Cascarino on Thursday's Breakfast show, he was asked if Kane would be his choice to win this year's award.

The three-time European Cup winner replied: "The hardest thing to do in football is score goals. He scores goals for fun.

"I’d have to factor in this, the Bundesliga is not the greatest league. It’s not got the intensity that the Premier League has.

3 Kane's goal-scoring ability is enough to win him the Ballon d'Or, says Souness Credit: Getty

"I’d have to say that, but he’s a goal machine and the single biggest reason he’s a goal machine is (because) he’s a lovely, lovely striker of the ball.

"He gets his shots off accurately from anywhere within 25 yards. He’s a proper player and he’s got a football brain. He can see a picture and deliver on it as well.

"I think that would be a good shot because generally it is strikers that win it.

"I know Rodri won it recently, (Luka) Modric a couple of years ago, but it’s generally the guys that put the ball in the back of the net.

"I suppose that's very deservedly so because that is the hardest thing to do in the game of football."

Bundesliga Ballon d'Or winners

Kane is amongst the 30 nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or alongside fellow internationals Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.

Last 10 Ballon d'Or winners 2025: Ousmane Dembele - PSG and France 2024: Rodri - Manchester City and Spain 2023: Lionel Messi - Inter Miami/PSG and Argentina 2022: Karim Benzema - Real Madrid and France 2021: Lionel Messi - PSG/Barcelona and Argentina 2019: Lionel Messi - Barcelona and Argentina 2018: Luka Modric - Real Madrid and Croatia 2017: Cristiano Ronaldo - Real Madrid and Portugal 2016: Cristiano Ronaldo - Real Madrid and Portugal 2015: Lionel Messi - Barcelona and Argentina

Meanwhile, three of his Bayern team-mates have also been nominated in Luis Diaz, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano.

They are the only current Bundesliga players in the running for the award.

If Kane is victorious, he would become the first German-based player to win the Ballon d'Or since Matthias Sammer in 1996.

The former Borussia Dortmund captain is one of six players to do so whilst plying their trade in the Bundesliga.

Others include Hamburg legend Kevin Keegan in 1978 and 1979 as well as Borussia Monchengladbach's Allan Simonsen in 1977.

As for Bayern, they have had three separate winners, with the most recent coming 45 years ago.

3 Sammer is the last Bundesliga-based player to win the Ballon d'Or Credit: Alamy

Karl-Heinz Rummenigge won the Ballon d'Or two years in a row in 1980 and 1981.

The only other Bayern players to receive the award were Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer.

Sports.title: The eight players who have run the furthest in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
The eight players who have run the furthest in the Premier League this season

Every Premier League team needs a workhorse - someone to do all the dirty work for their side and give their all for the cause.

Certain teams have more of those stars than others, but there are some standouts so far this season for total distance covered.



5 Gross has covered the most distance in the Premier League so far this season amid his incredible start with Brighton Credit: Getty

Here are the top flight players who have run the most...

1. Pascal Gross - 72.5km

Brighton's star of the campaign so far is surely Pascal Gross.

And at 35 years old, Gross has covered the most distance of all players in the Premier League, running 72.5km in six games.

That's an average of 12.1km per 90 minutes for the veteran, who has four assists and three goals to his name already.

2. Anton Stach - 70.9km

Anton Stach comes next, with the Leeds midfielder clocking just under 71km covered across six outings.



The German has averaged 11.9km per 90 minutes.

He has played all but two minutes of Daniel Farke's side's impressive start to the Premier League season.

3. Vitaly Janelt - 70.8km

Another midfielder. Another German.

Brentford's Vitaly Janelt is also one of the leading runners in the league, totting up 70.8km in total distance covered.



Janelt is currently averaging 11.8km per 90 minutes.

5 Leeds' Stach is a workhorse in the Leeds midfield and the numbers back his efforts up Credit: Getty

5 Armstrong has secured a starting spot for Everton and is making sure that he keeps it Credit: Getty



4. Harrison Armstrong - 70.3km

Also above the 70km mark is Everton's Harrison Armstrong.

19-year-old Armstrong, who has started every game for the Toffees so far this season, has covered 70.3km altogether.

The ex-Preston and Derby loanee averages 12.1km per 90.

5. Ethan Ampadu - 69km

Ethan Ampadu rounds out the top five, as the Leeds captain leads by example when it comes to effort on the pitch.

The Wales international has covered 69km so far this season, averaging 11.5km per game.

Ampadu has played every minute for the Whites, with their midfield full of workhorses, as he joins Stach in the list.



5 Sunderland skipper Xhaka is also one of the leading runners, with the 34-year-old leading by example Credit: Getty

6. Granit Xhaka - 68km

Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka is also one of the furthest runners in the Premier League this season.

He has covered 68km altogether, averaging 11.3km per 90.

At 34 years old, Xhaka, who has recently been punished for obtaining a fake COVID certificate, has played every minute this term.

7. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall - 67.5km

Averaging 11.3km per 90 minutes, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is another of the leading runners in the Premier League.



The ex-Chelsea midfielder has run a total of 67.5km so far.

And as a reward for his effort on the pitch, Dewsbury-Hall has also scored two goals and provided one assist.

5 Dewsbury-Hall is the second Everton midfielder sitting among the Premier League's running leaders Credit: Getty

8. James Justin - 67.1km

Farke clearly has Leeds working hard for their results.

James Justin is the third Leeds player in the top eight players who have covered the most distance so far this season.

Justin has run 67.1km in six Premier League games.

Sports.title: UEFA continue plot to oppose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president after $15million move
Sports.content:
Senior figures within UEFA continue to work on a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, talkSPORT understands.

Infantino is currently face-to-face with several of his critics at the FIFA Council meeting in Zurich and has promised to address his failed and controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise plans, which intended to part-privatise FIFA.



2 Infantino is struggling to drum up support ahead of his re-election vote next year Credit: Getty

Ahead of the FIFA Congress on Thursday, Infantino pledged $15million in additional funding to each of FIFA's 2011 members, taking their total for the 2027-2030 cycle to $25million.

The move comes off the back of calls from UEFA and CONCACAF to use more of FIFA's reserves to fund members.

Infantino has also put forward an amendment stopping automatic one-match bans being suspended at FIFA tournaments. This follows US striker Folarin Balogun being allowed to play against Belgium in the last sixteen of the World Cup despite being sent off in the round before against Bosnia.



Infantino has insisted he played no role in making the call, yet he was asked to review the incident by US President Donald Trump, as talkSPORT revealed.

Several key members within UEFA are not satisfied with extra funding or even reforms.



UEFA's comments

"There has to be a challenger to Infantino because he will certainly, as he already said, be a candidate in the election unless something dramatic happens in the coming weeks," UEFA VP Laura McAllister told talkSPORT. "Of course, it could do, but legal processes [including UEFA putting together a criminal case against Infantino and FIFA] take a long time, so let's not hold our breath over that.

"There has to be a candidate who, first of all, can command the support of all modernisers beyond just Europe. Football doesn't belong to Europe. Yes, we [UEFA] are a very powerful confederation and, yes, we generate a lot of funds, but football belongs to every single federation and club across the world. On this, I agree with Infantino that football doesn't belong to anyone in any geographical location.



"We have to unite people around a candidate, or maybe more than one candidate, and that candidate, whoever he or she is, has to stand on a manifesto of agreed reform: of greater transparency or greater accountability, of less political interference and must recognise the role of the FIFA President should be to run football, and not [like Infantino] to involve himself in other ventures, whether that's via the private or political sectors.

2 Infantino's decisions throughout the summer have put him under serious pressure to keep his job Credit: Getty

"I hope very much there will be a candidate [to rival Infantino] and I think that's where we are at the moment. Lots of work is happening behind the scenes. But we need a candidate with an ethos of credibility and modernisation showing why they should win the election next March."

Who could challenge Infantino?

UEFA, with strong support from CONCACAF, are still determining who to put forward on the ballot. So far, former Spurs defender Ramon Vega is the only name to come forward. He does not yet have the five federations required to officially stand, and it is uncertain if he even meets the eligibility criteria of working for two-years in football within the last five years.



talkSPORT understands there is firm support for Arsene Wenger, the former Arsenal boss who is now FIFA's head of football development. It is unclear whether Wenger has an appetite to stand, but his name has been brought up at multiple UEFA meetings, including last week in Berlin.

Luis Figo is another name who would draw considerable support. The ex-Barcelona and Real Madrid footballer has been a vocal critic of Infantino. He has also been earmarked as a potential replacement for Aleksander Ceferin, but the UEFA President is seeking another term next year.

Victor Montagliani was viewed as a leading contender but has decided to seek a new term with CONCACAF.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi would be well capable of challenging Infantino, and winning support in key battleground Asia, but the PSG President insists he doesn't want to stand.



"I have zero ambition," Al-Khelaifi told talkSPORT at the EFC General Assembly in Copenhagen earlier this month. "I don't think I am the right guy. I don't want to go [to FIFA]. I am enjoying what I am doing. I am having fun."

EFC vice-chair Dariusz Mioduski is another name who has been discussed and is highly-regarded within the game.

The head of the Norwegian FA, Lise Klaveness, AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, former FIFA presidential candidate Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein and London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang are other contenders that executives within UEFA or CONCACAF have suggested.

Senior UEFA sources say they want only one name so as not to fragment the vote.



The expectation, should a candidate emerge, is their unveiling could run close to the November 18 deadline so as to give Infantino the least possible time to prepare for a challenge.

Even if someone can't be found to beat Infantino, several sources within football, spoken to by talkSPORT, feel it's important not to let him get re-elected unopposed, and to use the four-month campaign period as means to fuel genuine debate.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez says SORRY! Argentine apologises for angry interview calling out Man United's hierarchy - as he concedes his words 'did not help' after showdown talks with bosses
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez says SORRY! Argentine apologises for angry interview calling out Man United's hierarchy - as he concedes his words 'did not help' after showdown talks with bosses

Lisandro Martinez on Thursday night apologised for his withering takedown of Manchester United’s hierarchy after ‘positive’ clear-the-air talks with director of football Jason Wilcox and other key figures.

A fuming Martinez publicly criticised Wilcox and United’s top executives after defeat to Atletico Madrid for not backing manager Michael Carrick in the summer transfer window and for not fronting up to criticism after a miserable start to the campaign.

Martinez looked to clarify his remarks with a statement on Instagram on Wednesday – the squad’s allocated day off following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid – before releasing a fresh statement after talks with Wilcox and the board.

He is also understood to have accepted a fine.

‘It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after the game,’ Martinez said.

‘Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

‘The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.’

Lisandro Martinez has released another statement after meeting with Man United chiefs

While Martinez has for the first time apologised for the timing of his remarks, made just moments after the match concluded in Spain on Tuesday, it is not clear whether he apologised privately for the nature of his blistering critique, particularly of Wilcox.

Club sources stressed that Martinez alone made the decision to apologise publicly for his comments. The matter, in the eyes of United’s hierarchy, is seen as closed.

‘Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that,’ he added in his latest statement.

‘I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.

‘With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.’

Carrick, who was also present in Thursday’s crunch meeting at Carrington, is going to need Martinez on Sunday when United travel to Elland Road to face Leeds United, not least with Noussair Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu and Luke Shaw all already sidelined at the back.

Martinez’s long-term future is more uncertain, however. He is out of contract at the end of June, although United can extend it by another year.

If there is no resolution in the coming weeks, Martinez is free to negotiate with clubs outside of England for a pre-contract agreement.

United are unlikely to let a 28-year-old World Cup winner leave as a free agent five years after his £57million move from Ajax, but could trigger the extension so they can demand a transfer fee for him.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace's John Textor nightmare: BOBBY MANZI reveals the blazing rows with Steve Parish, his crumbling football empire and why Lyon can't stand him either
Sports.content:
When the full-time whistle went at Wembley and Crystal Palace had defied all the odds to win the FA Cup, John Textor leaned over a row of Royal Box seats to embrace Steve Parish.

After Eberechi Eze's goal won them the first trophy in their 120-year history, the image depicted an ownership group that was united and jubilant. In reality, their relationship was anything but.

On Thursday, Palace will reopen old wounds when they travel to Lyon for the Textor Derby. The disgraced former owner of both clubs will be nowhere to be seen and that's probably for the best, given the acrimony towards him in both France and south London.

Without his cross-Channel multi-club network, Palace may well have been playing in the Europa League last season. Instead they were demoted by virtue of no two clubs being able to play in the same UEFA competition and Nottingham Forest - now Public Enemy No1 in Croydon - took Palace's place. And the animosity extends beyond the supporters.

Textor arrived at Palace in August 2021, acquiring the largest minority stake in the club for £87.5million before increasing his shareholding to 43 per cent three years later. Yet, despite his attempts, Textor failed to convert his equity into control. On several occasions, he tried to purchase a majority stake but was consistently blocked.

That irked him. Chairman Parish, the club's ultimate decision-maker despite owning significantly less of it than Textor, angered him. Textor deemed Parish risk-averse, while Parish viewed Textor as a risk to the club. But Parish had the measure of him, using the Missouri-born former competitive skateboarder's capital to pay off debt during Covid, develop the academy site and strengthen the playing squad without giving him decision-making power.

Former Crystal Palace director John Textor (left) had regular slanging matches with fellow part-owner Steve Parish (right)

Textor's ownership of Lyon meant that Palace were kicked out of the Europa League last season, as no two teams in the same competition can have the same controlling partner

Meanwhile, Textor wanted Palace to be the cornerstone of his multi-club ownership group, Eagle Football, which owned Lyon, Brazilian top-flight side Botafogo and the now-defunct RWD Molenbeek of Belgium. Given that Textor has since lost all the clubs amid financial mismanagement, Parish's wariness has been vindicated.

Textor wanted Parish to prioritise the playing squad and was aggrieved by ring-fencing cash for Selhurst Park's new Main Stand. Some believe Textor never supported the development, with the issue often prompting bust-ups.

Publicly, Parish and Textor mostly put on a united front, though Textor made some snide digs about the 'red Ferrari driving chairman' in an interview with talkSPORT. Behind the scenes, however, the pair never hid their dislike or the tension between them – and Textor eventually lost much of his interest in Palace after realising his sway was limited and he could not further his multi-club network ambitions.

The most disruptive period came during Textor's exit. He had been looking to sell for some time but the process was accelerated after the FA Cup win granted Palace entry into the Europa League for the following campaign, where the Lyon problem reared its head.

There was perhaps another reason for Textor's expediency. Lyon had problems of their own - the seven-times French champions were in the process of being kicked out of Ligue 1 by the French football authorities (DNCG).

But when Textor's money came in from selling his Palace stake to Woody Johnson, the former US Ambassador to the UK and owner of the NFL's New York Jets, they satisfied the DNCG's demands and were reinstated not just to the French top flight but also the Europa League.

So in the end, selling Palace and releasing them from the multi-club network resulted in Lyon taking their Europa League place. Palace were demoted to the Conference League - which they went on to win to again qualify for the Europa League - because Textor still had 'decisive influence' on the March 1, 2025 deadline for ownership conflicts to be resolved for the following season.

Palace fans had voiced their distrust of Textor long before the multi-club ownership issue hit them hard - with this banner in January 2023

Textor (centre) owned around 40 per cent of Palace from August 2021 to July 2025, when he sold his stake to New York Jets owner and former US Ambassador to the UK Woody Johnson

To this day, Textor is one of three parties Palace supporters blame for their expulsion, alongside Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis and UEFA.

'F*** UEFA, f*** John Textor, f*** Marinakis' has become a staple chant at matches and will almost certainly be heard throughout the match at the Groupama Stadium on Thursday night.

Textor has both publicly and privately suggested that supporters are naive for blaming him. Of course, the Europa League demotion is the emotional source of their frustration. However, the Textor resentment originated in concerns over his ambition to put Eagle Football Holdings on the stock market and fears over whether he had suitable funding.

Having previously held stakes in four clubs, Textor now has none.

Palace and Lyon are under new management, Botafogo voted him off their board this summer a few months after the club were hit with a three-window transfer ban for non-payment of a transfer fee, and Molenbeek lost their Belgian football league licence in August over financial difficulties. At the top of it all, Eagle Football Holdings went into administration in March.

It should be said that Palace had not planned well enough for the possibility of playing European football. Had they done so, Textor's shares could have been placed in a blind trust before the deadline and the situation avoided. Whether Textor would have agreed to that while trying to sell up, though, is another matter.

Intriguingly, one Palace source defended Textor when speaking to Daily Mail Sport. The source argued that Textor was the driving force behind Palace appointing Oliver Glasner two years ago and that the investment he made helped to pay for the signings of Marc Guehi and Michael Olise, suggesting that none of Palace's three trophies in the last 18 months would have been possible without the American. That is an unpopular opinion among fans to say the least, though.

Even after his exit, there remained a tenuous link to the club. John Textor's son, Addison, was until this summer employed by Velocity Capital – an American private equity firm owned by minority Palace shareholder David Abrams. The firm invested more than £75m in leading football agency Unique Sports Group, which represents past and present Palace players Dean Henderson, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi and Dwight McNeil.

Under Textor's ownership, Botafogo won the Copa Libertadores in 2024 but he was voted off the club's board in July this year

One source argued that Textor was the driving force behind Palace appointing Oliver Glasner, and as such none of Palace's three trophies in the last 18 months would have been possible

It was Textor who appointed now-Palace boss Pierre Sage as Lyon head coach in 2023. He led them to the French Cup final in his first season but was sacked the following January

Palace fans will use their trip to Lyon to lambast Textor once again and the home crowd is likely to join in. Although Lyon's involvement prevented Palace from competing in the Europa League, there is no bitterness between the two clubs – both equally disdain Textor.

Lyon endured persistent battles with the DNCG thanks to Textor building up debt, the provisional relegation last summer and being forced to sell key players because of their financial situation. Ironically, supporters also fumed over his decision to sack now-Palace boss Pierre Sage, a decision Textor admits he now regrets.

When Palace won the Conference League to qualify for the Europa League last season, they were almost destined to face Lyon.

This is the final chapter in their Textor debacle and, unless it's in their favourite chant, everyone at Palace will hope Thursday night is the last time he enters their thoughts.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk insists 'introverted' Bradley Barcola's Champions League hat-trick will 'help him so much' - as Liverpool captain reveals advice for dealing with big price tag
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk has hailed 'introverted' Bradley Barcola after the Frenchman expressed himself with a ruthless hat-trick on Wednesday evening. The Reds winger scored three in Liverpool's rout of Austrian champions LASK in the city of Linz to help Andoni Iraola's side keep up their perfect European record. And van Dijk, who spent most of the game as a substitute, said: 'It's massive for Bradley. He's very introverted anyway. 'He won't express his feelings too much but everyone knows that will help him so much. Hopefully there are many more hat-tricks to come. 'It's about creating the environment where he can express himself on the pitch. 'As a footballer, you always want to be out there, showing what you can do. For him, scoring goals is a big part of his game. To get a hat-trick in the Champions League is a great thing for him and for us.' Virgil van Dijk (right) has said Bradley Barcola's (left) Champions League hat-trick will 'help him so much' Asked about how Barcola can deal with the sky-high price-tag, an issue that van Dijk experienced, he said: 'You can share experiences for sure. It's about helping each other to succeed. We're in it together. Bradley is getting into it now. He'll be absolutely fine.' Van Dijk came on around the hour mark – and Liverpool ended up conceding three goals, which he joked about, before revealing he is carrying a knock. 'Obviously Joe (Gomez) and I made it interesting after we came on after 60 minutes but sometimes these things happen,' he added. 'I didn't expect to come on whatsoever. It was a surprise. I'm still recovering a bit (after getting a kick to the calf against Manchester City). It had been a long time since I did not start a game like that. 'I still did everything I could off the pitch to help the team. It was unusual for me (not starting) but it's part of life. I think I'll be fine for Saturday.'
