Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Sports.title: Social Media: Mekies extends contract to lead Red Bull until 2031 | Brief
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence in its team principal Laurent Mekies by extending his contract to run the team until 2031.

Mekies took over from Christian Horner in charge of the team last year. Horner had run Red Bull since it entered F1 in 2005.

Under Mekies, Red Bull rebounded from a poor start to last season. From over 100 points behind, Max Verstappen came within two points of retaining his drivers’ championship title in one of the closest ever finishes to a world championship.

This year, in the team’s first season with its own power units designed in conjunction with Ford, Red Bull has won the last two grands prix.

Sports.title: Verstappen says Red Bull’s car was “scary” to drive early in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has made huge progress with a car which felt “scary” to drive early in the season, says Max Verstappen.

The four-times world champion has won the last two grands prix in a row and also took victory in the sprint race in Singapore last week. The team’s form has improved significantly since the beginning of the season, when Verstappen only reached the podium once in the first seven rounds.

Verstappen spun out of the British Grand Prix suffered costly spins in qualifying at the Red Bull Ring and Hungaroring as the team struggled to get on top of its car. However their most recent upgrades have transformed its performance.

“The car definitely felt a lot nicer from Baku onwards,” said Verstappen. “It’s just been a lot more balanced. Then naturally, of course, when you can compete a bit further up front without having too many issues with the car compared to the beginning of the year, where it was actually sometimes a bit scary to drive, that makes it a lot nicer.”

Verstappen finished a close second behind George Russell in Baku. He qualified only eighth but was in contention for pole position until his final lap was compromised by a yellow flag.

He has been undefeated since then and expects to remain competitive over the final rounds. “We’re not in a championship fight, and that’s why I think ’til the end we’ll just try to have a good time and try to add more podiums and hopefully a few wins.”

It is the second time in as many years that Red Bull has made a breakthrough with a troublesome car in the second half of a season. “Two completely different cars as well, with the regulations,” Verstappen noted. “Also two completely different problems.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We had to find lap time. Plus, of course, also this year with the engine side of things, I think for everyone it’s been sometimes a bit complicated to get the most out of it.”

Red Bull needs to ensure they begin next year in better shape, said Verstappen.

“From race one to now, I think we’ve gained a lot of experience. Of course, we’re still not where we want to be, but I guess everyone will say the same thing.

“But we have learned so much and definitely also on the car side have fixed a lot of our weaknesses. We just need to keep improving, keep learning this year that so we can apply that also into next year.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: Cadillac already has better facilities than Mercedes, says Bottas | Brief
Sports.content:
Cadillac remain yet to score a point in their first season in Formula 1 but Valtteri Bottas says their progress is clear to see.

“We are definitely seeing an improvement somewhere every weekend,” he told the Financial Times. “It’s not necessarily in the results yet, but it’s in how we operate as a team in different areas.”

Bottas scored all 10 of his grand prix victories for Mercedes. He drove for the world champions between 2017 and 2021.

Cadillac is based partly at Silverstone, a short distance from Mercedes’ Brackley factory. Asked whether his new team’s facilities are better than the world champions’, Bottas replied: “I would say so.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 teams need decision ‘by mid-October’ on whether final races will go ahead | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses say they need to know by the middle of this month whether the series’ final two races will go ahead as planned.

Qatar and Abu Dhabi are due to hold the final two races of the season in November and December. However the war in Iran, which forced the cancellation of races in nearby Bahrain and Saudi Arabia six months ago, put those plans in jeopardy.

F1 has a back-up plan to hold an alternative event at Imola. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali previously said a decision would be made by mid-September. Teams say they need to know one way or the other soon.

“I believe Stefano was targeting to tell us in mid-October,” said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu in Azerbaijan. “So, we all know what the situation is.

“I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it. I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etcetera. All those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that.

“But I’m sure we all, as a family, community, will make sure if we have to do that, that will happen. But hopefully, as a baseline, we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That would be really good.”

Drivers have pointed out the conditions could be very cold if the series races in Imola in December. However Audi team principal Mattia Binotto believes it would be no cooler than some other venues the series visits.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The main challenges are more organisation and logistics,” he said. “I would think, from a technical point, often we may say wintertime and snow tyres, but at the end, as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than Las Vegas.

“So I don’t think that’s a true concern. It’s more from the organisation and the logistics, really. And again, mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision.”

Domenicali told the Financial Times the “decision is done” but also admitted “Imola is the place that eventually, in case of a force majeure before a certain date, would be ready to host it.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: F1’s sportswashing roster grows with addition of race in Rwanda | Briefs
Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. [caption id="attachment_530322" align="alignright" width="470"] The 2025 Formula 1 season started in Australia[/caption]A world drivers’ champion has been crowned every year since the series began. Since 1958 a world constructors’ championship title has also been awarded. The most successful F1 drivers in history are seven-times world champions Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. In 2021 the former became the first and so far only driver to date to win 100 grands prix. While Schumacher retired from F1 at the end of 2012, Hamilton continues to race. His rival world champions in the series are Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso. There are 10 teams active in the championship, each of which field cars for two drivers. Each team is required to design and build the majority of its cars but may source some parts including engines, gearboxes and certain other components. Ferrari has won the F1 constructors’ championship more times than any other team, with 16 titles. It is also the only team which has competed in every championship since the first…

Sports.title: Formula 1 announces it will race in Rwanda from “early 2030s” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced it will return to race in Africa for the first time since 1993.

The series has agreed a 10-year deal to race in Rwanda, which has never previously held a round of the world championship. Unusually, no year for the inaugural race has been confirmed, with F1 saying only that it will “join the calendar in the early 2030s”.

A new circuit will be constructed in Bugesera, in the Eastern province of Rwanda. The track will be located 40 kilometres south of Rwanda’s capital Kigali, which hosted the FIA’s General Assembly and award ceremony in 2024.

F1 published an image of the planned RISE Motordrome circuit, which was created by Tilke Gmbh and Wurz Design, but gave no details of its specifications.

“Further details regarding the inaugural race date, circuit development milestones and race weekend plans will be announced in due course,” said F1.

According to Rwanda’s president Paul Kagame the race will be called the “Formula 1 African Grand Prix”.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali called the announcement “a landmark moment for Formula 1.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.”

F1 first raced in Africa in 1958, when Morocco’s Aib-Diab circuit held the final round of the season. However the series never returned to the northern African state.

The series found a longer-term home in South Africa, first at a track in East London, then at the popular Kyalami circuit near Johannesburg. South Africa held 23 grands prix, though the series faced growing criticism for holding events under the country’s racist apartheid regime, which led some teams to boycott the 1985 race.

Following a seven-year absence, F1 returned to a heavily revised Kyalami circuit for two races in the nineties.

By the time Rwanda hosts its first grand prix, up to 40 years may have passed since F1’s last race in Africa.

Sports.title: Devin Haney-Shakur Stevenson Purse Clash Could Sink Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson finally agreed on 145 pounds, but dividing the revenue could scuttle their bout before either man steps into the ring.

Talks have reached a critical point, putting the targeted November 28 date in Atlanta in real jeopardy. Settling on a catchweight gave both camps a clear target. Splitting the revenue creates a deeper rift because it hinges entirely on personal market valuation.

Haney’s November 28 date allows almost no room for further haggling. Just over six weeks remain on the calendar, meaning both boxers require signed contracts right now to launch proper training camps. Every day squandered bickering over percentages pushes that target closer to collapse.

Haney has every right to challenge an even split. He already proved his drawing power as a headline attraction. Agreeing to parity would concede commercial ground that his team believes Shakur has yet to earn.

Backing from Turki Alalshikh changes the financial landscape. Deep financial support guarantees a massive overall purse, but funding a guarantee is not the same as generating revenue through paying customers. Haney’s side will almost certainly demand terms that honor that distinction.

“A potential fight between Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson is facing obstacles,” Mike Coppinger reported, adding that negotiations were “reaching a critical stage to keep this fight alive.

Coppinger did not reveal the figures being discussed, but if Shakur wants an equal or larger share, that could be where the talks are getting stuck.

Haney holds the cards here. Devin has options, commercial value, and a willing audience. Shakur cannot afford another inactive stretch where he sits around polishing belts while the division moves on without him. If he lets his ego dictate both the scale and the purse split, Haney will simply walk, leaving Shakur with an empty calendar and nobody to blame but himself.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia-Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

“Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are now in advanced talks to fight in the first quarter of 2027, sources tell. Expect this welterweight title fight to happen next. And it’s a big one,” said Coppinger on X. “I believe the Garcia-Teo fight will happen regardless of the WBA’s ruling here. Catterall could end up being elevated.”

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Sports.title: Agility Drills Cannot Mask Canelo Alvarez’s Fading Gas Tank
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is putting his feet through plenty of work ahead of Christian Mbilli, but a movement-heavy approach could leave him short of energy before their October 31 fight reaches its toughest rounds.

Alvarez trying to reinvent himself as a nimble mover at age 36 looks like a recipe for disaster. The math simply does not add up when looking at his gas tank and output history.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo was barely working, averaging just 28 punches a round while trying to plant his feet, load up on single power shots, and conserve energy. Even with that rock-bottom volume and virtually zero ring traversal, he was visibly gassing by round six. His body has shown clear signs of mileage for several fights now, and stamina has always been his primary limitation whenever opponents force him to work at a sustained clip.

Now his camp is circulating clips of him running agility ladders, doing cone drills, and practicing lateral movement to stay off the ropes against Christian Mbilli. While it makes for good social media optics, applying that in a real fight is completely detached from reality. Moving your feet constantly under pressure takes far more conditioning than standing your ground and picking spots.

The work doesn’t stop for Canelo! 💯 🎥: @Canelo 🎟️ Buy #CaneloMbilli NOW at https://t.co/yxybEeoyF5 | Oct 31 | Mexico vs The World | Live on DAZN | @RingMagazine https://t.co/zDOn7OR9xH — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 15, 2026

Mbilli is a pure volume puncher who thrives on throwing 70 to 80 punches a round, pressing forward with reckless abandon. If Canelo’s tactical adjustment is to skip around the ring, make short escapes, and play keep-away, he is volunteering to burn the exact energy reserve he does not have. Avoiding shots on the move still costs cardio, and Mbilli will not politely hit pause between drills to let him recover.

Canelo has never been an elusive ring mechanic. He built his career on upper-body slips, tight high-guard defense, and brutal counter-punching off a solid base. The only way he beats a swarmer like Mbilli is by doing what he has always done best: planting both feet and landing shots hard enough to break Mbilli’s spirit and stop the forward march. If he spends the first four rounds burning his legs on lateral movement, Mbilli is going to drown him in volume before the second half of the fight even gets started.

That script is practically already written. If Canelo gasses out trying to play Willie Pep at 36 and drops the belt to Mbilli, the post-fight press conference will be a masterclass in deflection.

Fighters with that level of clout rarely say, “I cooked up a terrible game plan in camp, convinced myself I could turn the clock back eight years, and completely misjudged my own gas tank.” Instead, the narrative instantly shifts into passive corporate speak. It becomes “we made tactical adjustments that didn’t materialize on the night,” or Eddy Reynoso will quietly take the heat to protect the brand, talking about camp fatigue or lingering elbow issues that allegedly flared up in the dressing room.

The irony is that Canelo’s entire late career identity has been built on stubborn pride. He genuinely believes his ring IQ can outsmart the physiological clock. Attempting to dance and pivot away from an engine like Mbilli is purely an ego-driven attempt to prove he still possesses the agility of his prime 154- and 160-pound runs.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Puts Rematch Pressure on Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois faces the greater pressure in their rematch, with the champion needing to repeat his victory against a challenger who believes he has corrected the mistakes that cost him their first fight.

Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to win. Wardley admits he became overconfident after that success, giving the champion an opportunity to recover. If Wardley avoids those mistakes, Dubois could face a different task this time.

“I think that for me, like again, it’s something Daniel’s gone through, but now he’s got three losses on his record,” Wardley told Fight Wire. “Two of those to Oleksandr Usyk, so you chalk them up a bit differently.”

Wardley argues that another defeat would put Dubois in a difficult position, while he views his own first loss as something he can repair.

“It just frees me up. It’s okay, we had a loss. Things didn’t go too great. Not the end of the world,” he said.

The pressure on Dubois goes beyond the number of defeats. He needs to demonstrate that his previous victory was repeatable, rather than a result that depended on Wardley getting careless after putting him down twice.

Wardley believes he has identified how he let that opportunity slip. Better decisions could leave Dubois with fewer chances to recover, although maintaining pressure without wasting energy or walking into punches will require more than determination.

“There’s a few adjustments to be made, a few things we need to capitalize on better, and then the fight’s ours,” Wardley said.

Dubois proved he could beat Wardley that night. Whether he can handle a more disciplined version remains unanswered. Wardley still has to deliver those improvements under fire, but the champion cannot assume the same openings will appear again.

Wardley also questioned Dubois’s conflicting comments about his punching power, suggesting some of his opponent’s remarks sound rehearsed.

“Especially when the camera comes out, some of the lines you can very much tell are forced, or they’ve at least been told to him to put in there,” he said.

The verbal sparring adds to Wardley’s portrayal of himself as the more relaxed fighter. Dubois’s harder task is showing that he has answers for the changes Wardley brings into the ring.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls Sebastian Fundora A Cheat Code
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga can’t understand how Sebastian Fundora fits into the 154-pound division. Looking at a workout photo of the WBC champion, he compared Fundora to a video game character and suggested he should be making his money in the NBA.

Fundora’s long legs and arms dominate the picture. Berlanga fights two divisions above him at super middleweight, yet even he sounds taken aback by the sight of someone that tall competing at light middleweight.

How do they allow him to box at 154lb he’s a cheat code character from GTA WTF 🤣🤣🤣 listen he would have been a 200 million dollar NBA player. This is unacceptable he looks like a building https://t.co/AYW3y9aSuM — Edgar Berlanga Jr (@EdgarBerlangaJr) October 15, 2026

Berlanga isn’t the first fighter to reach for a video game comparison. After Fundora stopped Erickson Lubin in April 2022, Terence Crawford called him “a cheat code,” comparing him to a created Fight Night boxer with the height turned up in a smaller weight class.

It’s an understandable reaction. Finding sparring partners who can prepare an opponent for Fundora is difficult enough. Then comes the task of getting past those long arms and landing on a head that sits well above the usual target.

The odd thing is that Fundora often gives opponents a chance by coming to them. He likes fighting up close, throwing short punches rather than spending every round keeping shorter men at the end of his jab. They don’t always have to chase him to get their shots off.

That makes him entertaining, even if Berlanga thinks his dimensions look unfair. Fundora can make 154. The men across from him have to figure out the rest.

His WBC title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj this Saturday is a harder sell. Hadribeaj is the mandatory challenger, but most fans know little about him. They’re waiting to see Fundora against the bigger names in a division with plenty to offer.

Hadribeaj gets his chance to make himself known once the fight starts. Until then, Fundora’s unusual frame is likely to draw more conversation than the matchup itself.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Faces Long Wait For Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Liam Paro booking another defense puts more distance between him and Ryan Garcia, though Garcia’s alternative choices present a far bigger hurdle. Matchups with Teofimo Lopez or Devin Haney carry massive commercial appeal, which could strand Paro well past his ideal timeline.

“We’re not going to sit on the sideline,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia.

Staying active is the smartest move Paro can make. Continuing to take bouts keeps him sharp instead of burning months chasing an opponent who sees little urgency to fight him.

Teofimo gives Garcia an established American audience. A return bout with Haney carries built-in personal drama. Paro holds a world championship belt, yet hardware alone might not outweigh the bigger paydays Garcia could chase instead.

The calendar for Ryan creates another headache. If Garcia sits out until May, that single appearance eats up the first half of 2027. Another high-profile date could easily swallow the remaining months, leaving Paro on the outside looking in despite handling his business in the ring.

Teofimo’s mandatory duty against Jack Catterall adds some problems, but it will not kill a potential Garcia meeting. The WBA might grant Teofimo an exception so he can keep the strap. Teofimo could also surrender the belt outright to lock down the more lucrative bout.

That situation does not assure Teofimo gets the nod. Still, Paro cannot count on sanctioning body politics to eliminate a popular name from contention.

Title dynamics bring further chaos. If Garcia meets Teofimo first, Paro must hope Garcia wins so the WBC unification prize remains intact. A Garcia loss instantly ruins that scenario before Paro ever secures a signed contract.

Paro holds the power to defend his title and keep his phone line open. He cannot dictate Garcia’s opponent, dictate fight results, or force Garcia to pursue undisputed status.

Taking another bout makes complete sense. Chasing Garcia is worth the ambition, but Paro must build an active calendar that keeps rolling even if Garcia never calls. Paro landing that fight in 2027 makes zero sense from Ryan’s financial perspective.

Ryan operates purely on box office scale. A return match with Devin Haney already has massive public heat, personal grudge, and built-in history that sells pay-per-view buys effortlessly. A fight with Teofimo Lopez brings two huge American fanbases together for an absolute blockbuster. Those two events generate monster gates. Paro simply cannot generate that kind of revenue in the United States.

On top of the financial gap, Paro presents a terrible risk profile for Ryan. Paro is a tough southpaw with an awkward style who makes life miserable inside the ring. Taking on that kind of stylistic headache for a fraction of the money Ryan can make elsewhere is bad business. Fighters in Ryan’s tax bracket do not volunteer for difficult nights unless huge checks back it up.

Then you have the calendar reality. Ryan is not fighting four times a year. If he takes a marquee date in the spring, that eats up the first half of 2027. A massive fall date takes care of the rest. Between Teofimo, Haney, or other lucrative names floating around, 2027 fills up instantly.

Paro holding a title belt does not move the needle for Ryan either. Ryan transcended the need for sanctioning body belts long ago because his name alone drives the promotion.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Approval Leaves Meiirim Nursultanov Waiting
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames got the green light to take an interim bout before dealing with mandatory challenger Meiirim Nursultanov. The WBC approved a November 17 date above 160 pounds, but it includes a massive catch. If Adames loses, he loses his middleweight world title on the spot, even with the belt not officially on the line.

The WBC confirmed the ruling in an October 14 update. They left out the opponent, the venue, plus the exact weight limit. Because of that, nobody knows how tough this assignment will actually be.

Meiirim Nursultanov gets stuck waiting again. Holding the mandatory slot didn’t lock down his crack at the belt. Now he has to sit back, hoping Adames survives this detour so their scheduled clash can take place.

It puts Nursultanov in a weird spot. If Adames wins, Nursultanov still gets his shot at the active champion. If Adames stumbles, the title gets stripped, which leaves the top contender waiting on fresh orders for a vacant belt.

The WBC laid out clear terms. An Adames win routes him directly into the Nursultanov defense. Whoever walks away with the victory there has to face interim titlist Jesús Ramos Jr next.

There is a road map to clean up the division, but getting there takes three separate bouts. Every detour before the mandatory introduces the threat of an injury or an upset that blows up the entire schedule.

NEWS: Per sources, Carlos Adames’ @Zuffa_Boxing debut in a nontitle bout OK’d by the WBC is planned for November in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Zuffa is planning a show in November & one in December (obviously depends on status of the war & unrest in the region). #boxing — Dan Rafael (@DanRafael1) October 15, 2026

That vacant title rule also creates a bizarre setup for whoever steps into the ring on November 17. If the opponent beats the middleweight champ, Adames loses the belt, yet the winner walks away empty-handed without claiming it. Anyone signing that contract needs to realize what a victory actually delivers.

Adames lands the flexibility he wanted, while Nursultanov collects yet another promise about future dates. Until the promotion names a foe, nobody can tell if Adames is taking a dangerous test or just booking a tune-up above middleweight. Either way, Nursultanov stays on the sidelines waiting for his turn.

It sends a terrible message when a sanctioning body lets a champion put their mandatory obligations on ice just to chase an untitle bout above the weight class.

The whole point of a mandatory challenger is that you earn the number one spot through actual ring results, not politics. Nursultanov did the work, secured the position, and now he is forced to sit on the shelf watching the champion go hunt for bigger money elsewhere.

Nursultanov is not getting compensated while Adames takes this detour. Time away from the ring burns prime years, brings zero purse money, and creates ring rust. If Adames gets hurt on November 17, the layoff stretches out even longer. If Adames loses, Nursultanov does not even get the satisfaction or the profile boost of taking down the sitting champion. He gets stuck in a vacant title match that generates far less fanfare and a smaller check.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Rules Out Saudi Arabia For Boots Fight
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the winner of Jaron Ennis against Josh Kelly next, but the WBC junior middleweight champion insists Saudi Arabia will not host it. Fundora aims for spring 2027 to stage a unification bout, making it clear that facing Boots will not convince him to travel abroad to Riyadh.

That stance sets a firm condition on his future plans before his title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj on Saturday. Fundora expects Ennis to defeat Kelly, calling Boots the premier matchup at 154 pounds.

“I think the winner of Boots and Kelly should be the opponent for our next fight,” Fundora said to Ariel Helwani. “I think that’s early, early maybe springtime of next year, 2027.” Asked whether that reflected discussions or simply his preference, Fundora clarified: “That’s what I want. I think that’s what I’ll get as well.”

His preferred schedule remains a target rather than a signed contract, yet his refusal regarding Saudi Arabia sounded absolute.

“There’s a reason why I haven’t fought in Saudi Arabia,” Fundora said. “I wouldn’t feel comfortable, me being an American and everything like that.”

Asked directly if he would turn down an Ennis bout in the Gulf nation, Fundora confirmed he would walk away because that option feels unrealistic to him.

Securing an Ennis encounter would require common ground on location alongside purses. If promoters propose Saudi Arabia, Fundora makes it obvious that organizers must secure an alternate venue to get his signature.

He has not turned down an active offer to box Ennis. The scenario remains hypothetical right now, even while his desire to face the Ennis vs. Kelly victor is genuine.

Fundora must handle business against Hadribeaj first. Once Saturday concludes, his focus centers on collecting the remaining belts at 154 pounds in an arena he can accept. His stance puts him in a tricky spot financially. Crossing Riyadh off the list immediately shrinks the money pool, because nobody in the United States or the UK is writing those blank checks right now.

“My mother being a veteran and all the politics and that. It’s bigger than boxing. It’s way bigger than boxing,” said Fundora.

If PBC or another promoter has to finance an Ennis against Fundora unification on regular domestic pay-per-view, the numbers have to make sense organically, and that means significantly smaller paydays for both men.

Boots wants the belts, but he also wants to get paid like an elite fighter. If Fundora demands the bout take place in Vegas or Los Angeles, Ennis might look at the revenue split and decide the headache is not worth the discount, especially when other opportunities exist.

None of it matters if he looks past Saturday, either. Hadribeaj is not flying in just to collect a check and hand over the belt. If Fundora gets sloppy or gets caught while daydreaming about spring 2027, the whole discussion vanishes overnight. He will have priced himself out of an imaginary payday while holding empty hands.

Ghana News.title: From Campaign Propaganda to Gov’t Accountability: When the message-makers demand a seat at the table
Ghana News.content:
AI-generated illustration.

The campaign is over, the votes have been counted, and power has changed hands. But what happens when the very voices that helped sell a political message begin demanding answers from the government they helped bring to power? Ghana may be witnessing one of the most fascinating consequences of modern political communication: the struggle between those who shape the message and those who must ultimately govern.

THE THEATRE OF GHANA’S 2024 ELECTIONS

Ghana’s 2024 general elections now belong to history, but the dramatic scenes that defined the campaign remain memorable.

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, John Dramani Mahama, popularised the emphatic slogan, “NDC, no turning back,” while the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, used the metaphor of a driver seeking the keys to lead Ghana forward.

These campaign performances were more than political entertainment. They were communication strategies designed to make messages memorable, build emotional connections and persuade voters.

Both candidates and their supporters made extensive use of social media to reach eligible voters. The Electoral Commission declared Mahama the winner of the December 2024 presidential election, with Bawumia conceding defeat. The electorate had made its choice. Reuters’ election report.

But the end of a campaign does not necessarily end the influence of those who helped shape it.

BERNAYS AND THE POWER BEHIND PUBLIC OPINION

In his 1928 book Propaganda, public relations pioneer Edward L. Bernays made a provocative observation about the power of persuasion in democratic society.

He wrote: “The conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organised habits and opinions of the masses is an important element in democratic society.”

Bernays went further, arguing that those who influence public opinion can constitute an “invisible government” because they help shape how people think, what they value and how they respond to public issues. Bernays, 1928, p. 9

This idea offers a useful lens through which to examine modern political campaigns in Ghana.

Political communication is not simply about presenting policies. It is also about deciding which issues receive attention, how problems are framed, which emotions are activated and which political narratives become dominant.

During the 2024 campaign, NDC communicators and activists repeatedly criticised the record of the then governing NPP. Their messaging formed part of a wider contest over economic hardship, public confidence, accountability and the direction of the country.

In my view, the effectiveness of the NDC’s campaign communication deserves examination. However, it would be simplistic to attribute the election result to propaganda alone. Economic conditions, voters’ experiences, policy choices, party organisation and many other factors also shaped the outcome.

The important question is what happens when the campaign machinery continues operating after the election.

WHEN THE CAMPAIGN PROMISES BECOME THE PUBLIC’S SCORECARD

Among the commitments Mahama made during the campaign was a proposal to drill boreholes on cocoa farms and provide water-storage facilities to help farmers irrigate their farms during dry periods. MyJoyOnline reported the proposal in November 2024

The NDC also campaigned on a 24-hour economy, built around three eight-hour shifts intended to increase productivity and create employment.

These were campaign commitments, not merely slogans. They created expectations among citizens who hoped to see tangible improvements in employment, agriculture and living standards.

Whether individual promises have been fulfilled, partially implemented, delayed or remain outstanding must be assessed through current evidence, official implementation records and the experiences of the intended beneficiaries.

But one principle is beyond dispute: “a campaign promise does not become a government achievement simply because it was repeated convincingly during an election.”

It must be measured against what is actually delivered.

This is where citizen journalists, bloggers and content creators become particularly important. They can visit communities, interview farmers, speak to unemployed young people, document unfinished projects and ask questions that may not receive sustained attention in traditional newsrooms.

Their work can help transform campaign rhetoric into public scrutiny.

THE PROPAGANDIST IS NOT THE PRESIDENT

Here lies the central dilemma.

When political activists spend months promoting a candidate, defending campaign messages and challenging opponents, some may come to regard themselves as indispensable to the political victory. They may expect access, influence or recognition once their preferred candidate takes office.

That possibility deserves attention, but it should not be assumed that every supporter expects a position or that every online critic once served as a campaign propagandist.

The broader question is whether political communication can create expectations that become difficult to manage after an election.

A campaign requires persuasion. Government requires administration, evidence, negotiation, public accountability and decisions that must be judged by their results.

Those are different responsibilities.

The people who helped communicate a party’s message do not automatically acquire authority over government decisions. Equally, winning an election does not give a president the right to disregard citizens who helped build public support or who now question the administration’s performance.

The citizen is not a campaign prop, and the content creator is not a permanent public-relations officer for the party he or she supported.

Once the votes are counted, the relationship must change. Supporters, critics and undecided citizens all retain the right to demand answers.

FROM PROPAGANDA TO ACCOUNTABILITY

I do not believe Bernays’s argument means that the public is powerless or that a small group can control every political outcome. People can question messages, compare competing accounts, reject political claims and change their minds when presented with evidence.

That is why the rise of citizen journalism matters.

A viral video is not automatically proof. A trending allegation is not a verified fact. Bloggers and content creators must distinguish evidence from speculation, correct errors and give people accused of wrongdoing a fair opportunity to respond.

Governments, meanwhile, should not dismiss legitimate criticism merely because it arrives through Facebook, TikTok, YouTube or WhatsApp.

Where allegations concern public spending, campaign promises or possible wrongdoing, the appropriate response is to examine the evidence, provide clear explanations and allow lawful accountability processes to operate.

The media’s responsibility is to investigate. The citizen’s responsibility is to question. The government’s responsibility is to account for its decisions.

GHANA MUST MOVE BEYOND CAMPAIGN THEATRE

The 2024 election demonstrated the importance of political storytelling and digital communication. But the real test of democracy begins after the rallies, slogans, campaign videos and victory celebrations have ended.

Bernays helps us understand how public opinion can be shaped. Ghana’s democratic experience must also remind us that public opinion can change, and those who once helped promote a political message can later become among its most determined questioners.

The lesson is not that propaganda alone wins elections or that every campaign activist seeks to control government. It is that political communication creates expectations, and those expectations must eventually confront reality.

President Mahama’s administration should be assessed by its documented actions and results, not simply by the strength of its campaign messaging. The same standard should apply to every government.

And citizen journalists, bloggers and content creators should understand that their greatest public service is not to protect a political party from embarrassment, but to help citizens establish what is true, what remains unfulfilled and what must be done.

The campaign may end on election day, but accountability has no closing date.

In Ghana’s democracy, the microphone belongs to the people. Those who once used it to help a candidate win must remain free to use it to ask what happens next.

That is not betrayal. It is part of the democratic responsibility that begins when the campaign ends.

Ghana News.title: Ashanti Region Security Coordinator warns sand winners to stay off Accra–Kumasi Expressway site
Ghana News.content:
Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator, Captain John Kwame Jabari, has warned sand winners operating along the Accra–Kumasi Expressway project site to stop their activities or face severe consequences.

He said security personnel had been deployed to the area to prevent further illegal sand winning and protect the planned infrastructure project from disruptions.

Speaking on Accra-based Channel One on Thursday, October 15, 2026, Captain Jabari said preliminary investigations suggested that the alleged activities had been ongoing for about two weeks, with operators reportedly entering the area at night with trucks to load sand.

“A team has been set up to conduct patrols along the expressway to prevent future incidents or any other offences that may occur along that route.

"So, I would like to tell Ghanaians, particularly sand winners, to stay off the expressway. It is a big project that this government wants to embark on, and we are not going to entertain anybody who wants to disrupt the progress of that work,” he said.

The warning follows the arrest of 15 men suspected of engaging in sand-winning activities along the expressway project site.

The suspects were arrested on Wednesday, October 14, during a security operation in the Sewua–Donyina–Appiadu enclave in the Ashanti Region.

Six vehicles, including a wheel loader, were also impounded during the operation.

Assistant Liaison Officer Ivan Bilson Yeboah said the suspects had been transported to the National Security headquarters in Accra for custody and further investigations.

Captain Jabari said security personnel would maintain a strong presence along the route to prevent a recurrence and ensure that the project proceeded without interference.

“We are going to pay key attention to that route over there. So I like to tell Ghanaians or sand winners that they should stay off the expressway,” he cautioned.

He reiterated that authorities would not tolerate activities that could undermine the progress of the expressway project and assured the public that security teams would take action against anyone found engaging in unlawful activities in the area.

Ghana News.title: PZ Cussons Ghana promotes hand washing among schoolchildren through Camel campaign
Ghana News.content:
PZ Cussons Ghana Limited is promoting hand-washing education among schoolchildren, saying habits developed early in life can help prevent infections and improve public health.

The company used its Camel brand to educate pupils at Christ the King School on proper hand-washing techniques as part of activities marking Global Handwashing Day.

The engagement featured practical demonstrations and interactive sessions aimed at helping pupils understand the importance of washing their hands with soap and making the practice part of their daily routines.

Head of Marketing at PZ Cussons Ghana Limited, Bright Anomah, said the focus on children was deliberate, as lessons learnt at an early age could influence their hygiene practices throughout their lives.

He said educating pupils on when and how to wash their hands could help protect them from infections while enabling them to share the knowledge with their families and communities.

Mr Anomah also called for greater private-sector involvement in public health education, arguing that the responsibility should not rest solely with government.

“Public health shouldn’t be the responsibility of the government alone. It is the responsibility of also the private sector and businesses like us, PZ Cussons, to help the country in terms of social development,” he said.

He said businesses should complement their commercial activities with initiatives that promote health awareness and support community development.

Brand Ambassador for Camel, Matilda Adu Boateng, encouraged consumers to incorporate hand washing into their daily hygiene routines.

She highlighted the benefits of Camel Antibacterial Soap, which the company says offers protection against germs, moisturises the skin and helps eliminate odour.

“Washing your hand with Camel Antibacterial Soap, it gives you that triple defence, which is killing germs 99.9 per cent, it moisturises your skin, and it eliminates odour,” she said.

The product's advertised germ-killing claim was not independently verified for this report.

Pupils who participated in the engagement demonstrated their understanding of the importance of hand washing and identified key moments when the practice is necessary, including before eating and after using the toilet.

One pupil said the session had helped them understand how hand washing could protect against germs and infections.

“Today I learnt about how hand washing is important and how it saves us from germs and infections. Thank you to Camel Ghana,” the pupil said.

This year's Global Handwashing Day is being marked under the theme “Be a Handwashing Hero,” which encourages individuals, families, schools, communities and businesses to make hand washing with soap a consistent part of everyday life.

PZ Cussons said the campaign forms part of its broader efforts to promote hygiene awareness and encourage practices that contribute to healthier communities.

The initiative highlights the importance of reinforcing hand-washing lessons beyond special campaigns, so children can practise proper hygiene consistently at school and at home.

Ghana News.title: 30 NDC aspirants file nominations in Upper West as regional election approaches
Ghana News.content:
Thirty aspirants have filed nomination forms at the Upper West Regional office of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Wa to contest various regional executive positions ahead of the party’s internal election.

The filing attracted constituency executives and grassroots members seeking regional leadership roles, with aspirants highlighting grassroots empowerment, party reorganisation and efforts to retain the party’s parliamentary seats in the region.

A total of 60 aspirants picked nomination forms, with all applicants expected to undergo vetting on Friday ahead of the regional delegates conference scheduled for next month.

Chairmanship contest

Among those contesting the regional chairmanship is Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency Chairman Sombawiere Samba, popularly known as Sankara. He faces incumbent chairman Abdul Nasir Saani, who also filed his nomination on Thursday, and businessman Alhassan Aadam Randy.

Speaking after filing, Mr Samba highlighted his progression through the party’s ranks, from polling agent and branch chairman to ward chairman, before serving eight years as Deputy Regional Treasurer and becoming constituency chairman.

“I started as a grassroots person... If I succeed, everybody who wants to lead the party in the region must start from the grassroots,” he said.

He cited his contributions to development in Nadowli-Kaleo, including the provision of 1,400 chairs distributed across 114 polling stations and the initiation of a permanent constituency office project.

Mr Samba pledged to extend similar infrastructure development across the region by helping all constituencies acquire furnished offices and securing a permanent regional headquarters for the party.

On the NDC’s parliamentary performance in the region, he argued that credit for winning seats should be shared with constituencies, Members of Parliament and branch executives rather than attributed solely to regional executives.

Mr Saani, who filed earlier in the day, urged delegates to retain him as regional chairman.

Vice-chairmanship and deputy secretary races

Daffiama-Bussie-Issa Constituency Chairman and Dean of Constituency Chairmen, Boniface Tienaah, has filed to contest the regional vice-chairmanship.

He said his priority would be to support whoever emerged as regional chairman through advice and practical assistance.

“As a vice chairman, you don’t really have the direct mandate. The best you can do is to make sure that you give the best ideas to your regional chairman and support him vividly,” Mr Tienaah said.

He stressed the need for regional leadership to remain responsive to branch executives to prevent grassroots members from feeling neglected after elections.

The contest for Deputy Regional Secretary has attracted Dr Angsongna Banangmwine Claudius, popularly known as Dr ABC, and former Regional Elections and IT Directorate member Cornelius Naasoa Wuobar.

Dr Claudius cited his administrative experience as a former two-time president of the Graduate Students’ Associations of Ghana (GRASAG) at the University of Ghana and the University for Development Studies.

He pledged to lobby for 44 tertiary scholarships across the region’s 11 constituencies during a four-year term and to modernise party secretariats through improved IT infrastructure, internet access and dedicated office managers.

He also called for fair distribution of opportunities and warned against sidelining branch executives in post-election welfare and programme allocations.

Mr Wuobar, who resigned from the Regional Elections and IT Directorate to contest, said his experience as a former Deputy Youth Organiser and Constituency Secretary in Nandom had prepared him for the role.

He expressed confidence in the NDC’s structures in the Upper West Region and dismissed the New Patriotic Party (NPP) as a threat to the party’s standing.

“We are not going to leave an inch for them... We don't have boys; we have men. Proper men,” he said.

“This time we are going to do shoe-to-shoe; we have already dealt with the boot-to-boot,” he added, suggesting that the party was prepared to match its political opponents at every level.

One woman files on opening day

Gladys Sufuyani was the only woman to file on the opening day, seeking the position of Deputy Regional Women’s Organiser.

The regional vetting committee is scheduled to vet all applicants on Friday, ahead of the regional delegates conference next month.

Ghana News.title: UPSA launches laptop assembly plant, requiring new students to assemble their own devices
Ghana News.content:
The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), has taken a major step towards technology-enabled learning with the official launch of its laptop assembly plant at the AFOA ATA Building.

The plant, launched on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, is the university’s response to years of student complaints that teaching is too theoretical.

“The main idea behind the UPSA laptop assembly plant is not just about assembling laptops but also to expose our students to the basic things they need to know and, ultimately, to equip them with skills to be self-reliant,” management explained at the launch.

“We always teach them theoretical frameworks, but complete education requires that students practise what they learn.”

The university says IT education at UPSA is being redefined, moving from watching videos about motherboards to actually making them.

“Today, our students can walk to the lab and learn how to make motherboards, as well as assemble and dismantle a lot of gadgets,” the university stated.

The training also covers software, app development that interacts with hardware, and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI).

In what it describes as a first-of-its-kind model for Ghanaian public universities, UPSA announced that, from the next academic year, every newly admitted student will assemble their own laptop.

“Once you are admitted to our university, you assemble your own laptop and use it yourself, and pay for it over time,” management said.

“We have come up with a very simple and convenient financing stream. You cannot train a student without a laptop. It is like going to school without a book and a pen.”

The plant currently produces 1,000 laptops per week, or about 4,000 a month, with the capacity to produce more through overtime work. The first 25 laptops were assembled by students last Saturday after just three days of training.

The facility is also equipped with an S-ray machine to detect faults and will provide warranty and after-sales services.

The project is a partnership between UPSA and MDIT, alongside two other private investors. The university says it invested no money in the project, contributing student labour as its equity.

The consultant and acting chief executive officer of MDIT said UPSA was chosen because of its professionalism.

“MDIT partnered with UPSA because, when we talk about professionalism, you cannot go anywhere other than UPSA,” he said.

“Our role is not just to bring a product out but to give skills to our students so they can progress from the basics to the intermediate and advanced levels, where they can also conduct their own research and come up with their own designs and working boards before they graduate.”

He disclosed that the training would include short courses lasting between one month and one year in advanced AI, AI agent training, and basic and advanced printed circuit board (PCB) and motherboard training.

The courses will be open to all students, not just those studying IT, with a minimum entry qualification of the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) or an equivalent senior high school qualification.

“Some of them are into marketing, some are into different fields, but it all starts with the interest,” he said.

Beyond the classroom

As a business university, UPSA says it intends to commercialise its knowledge by serving as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) for Ghanaian businesses seeking to develop their own laptop, mobile phone and tablet brands locally.

“The average Ghanaian businessman knows that … I want to create my own brand. Let me go to UPSA and see how UPSA can create a brand for me. I don’t have to travel outside, pay customs duties and all that,” management said.

“Our prayer is that we will scale it up and then, if possible, go nationwide.”

Management described the launch as Phase One of the project, with Phase Two focusing on engaging the business community.

Ghana News.title: UCC sociologist calls for action on gender inequality to end child marriage
Ghana News.content:
The Head of the Department of Anthropology and Sociology at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), Prof. Georgina Yaa Oduro, has called for action to address gender inequality, warning that it exposes girls to child marriage and threatens their education and prospects.

Speaking at an event to mark the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child at Ekon in the Central Region, she said the practice reflected unequal treatment of boys and girls, with girls bearing a disproportionate burden.

“Because why is it that a boy child is not being given out into marriage, but it’s a girl child that is being given out into marriage? So, it is genuinely a gendered issue,” she said.

Prof. Oduro cautioned against using poverty and vulnerability to justify child marriage, saying the practice could deepen deprivation across generations, particularly when girls are unable to complete their education.

“So, if we are not careful and we argue on poverty and vulnerability, we end up compounding the situation, because then we sow and reap the rippling effects of poverty,” she said.

She described education as one way to break the cycle, explaining that it equips girls with knowledge and skills that can improve their prospects, including in entrepreneurship. She added that efforts to end child marriage must begin at home, with parents supporting their daughters’ education and protecting their rights.

Informal unions are also a concern

The celebration was held under the theme, “End Child Marriage and Invest in the Rights of Girls”.

The Central Regional Girl Child Coordinator, Priscilla Cristabel Eshun, warned that child marriage extends beyond formal ceremonies to include informal unions in which girls cohabit with boys and men who have the financial means to support them.

“We want to end child marriage, which is not necessarily giving your daughter in marriage, formal marriage. But also, the informal marriage, where children are cohabiting with boys and men who have the financial standing,” she said.

Ms Eshun urged parents, traditional authorities and other stakeholders to work together to prevent early unions that disrupt girls’ education.

Education Director calls for enforcement of community bylaws

The Central Regional Director of Education, Dr Juliette Dufie Otami, urged traditional authorities to enforce community bylaws aimed at ending child marriage and protecting girls.

Speaking to JoyNews on the sidelines of the event, she said chiefs had considerable influence and should use their authority to ensure that community directives intended to protect children were enforced.

“The challenge we throw to the chiefs is that this is the time their bylaws need to work in the communities. Because we notice that they are now relaxed. They have the power to give out whatever instructions they want our children and our parents to follow,” she said.

Dr Otami said Ekon was selected to host this year’s celebration because of its high incidence of teenage motherhood and low learning outcomes. She said the Directorate wanted to work with the community rather than blame it, stressing that the challenges could not be addressed by schools alone.

She urged parents and guardians to encourage their daughters to remain in school and called on chiefs, elders, religious leaders and other community figures to challenge practices that harm children. She also urged boys to become active partners in respecting and protecting girls.

Dr Otami further called on teachers, particularly male teachers, to act as protectors, mentors and role models. She appealed to stakeholders to keep girls in school, report and resist child marriage, support young mothers who wish to return to the classroom, and invest in children’s education and well-being.

Call to prioritise girls’ aspirations

The event brought together pupils from schools across Cape Coast and Elmina and featured an appeal from the 2026 National Sanitation Diplomat, Nabeeha Erasoung Sulemana Atiah, who urged parents to support girls’ ambitions.

“I want to tell every parent to let their girl child have dreams. Let them go to school to the highest levels to become whatever they want, so they can help their families and the nation at large,” she said.

The guest of honour, Tufohene of the Ekon Traditional Area, Nana Wiabo Kwamena V, also encouraged parents to take a greater interest in girls’ welfare and education.

The event was organised by the Girls Education Unit of the Central Regional Education Service as part of efforts to raise awareness of child marriage and promote girls’ rights.

Stakeholders called for coordinated action by parents, traditional authorities, schools and communities to prevent child marriage, address early cohabitation and ensure that girls can continue their education and pursue their aspirations.

Ghana News.title: LSN questions Ghana’s proposed five-year presidential term and DCE election reforms
Ghana News.content:
The Law Students’ Network (LSN) has questioned the government’s decision to support extending Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years, while warning that its proposed model for electing District Chief Executives (DCEs) could undermine local democracy by retaining presidential influence over candidate selection.

LSN President Abraham Kwaku Gyasi raised the concerns at a roundtable organised by the Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) in Accra on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The discussion examined the Constitution Review Committee’s report, led by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh, and the government’s position on proposed constitutional reforms.

In its position paper issued on July 28, 2026, the government accepted the recommendation to amend Article 66(1) of the 1992 Constitution to extend the presidential term to five years, arguing that the additional time would allow governments to implement policies more effectively.

The LSN acknowledged that frequent election cycles could encourage short-term decision-making but argued that a longer mandate alone would not resolve governance challenges. It cited institutional inefficiencies, corruption, weak planning and inadequate accountability, insisting that proponents of the change must provide convincing empirical and institutional evidence to justify it.

The network also challenged the government’s proposed approach to electing DCEs, which would allow the President to nominate candidates before they are shortlisted for election. It argued that retaining executive influence over who can contest would weaken the purpose of introducing elections at the local level.

“Local democracy requires more than allowing citizens to vote among candidates selected through an executive-controlled process,” the network said, citing Article 240 of the Constitution and noting the IEA’s call for open competition in local elections.

The LSN further criticised the government’s rejection of proposals to change the appointment process for the Chief Justice and Justices of the Superior Courts, arguing that judicial appointments are closely linked to the constitutional protection of judicial independence under Article 127.

It also questioned the government’s alternative to a proposed ban on MPs serving as Ministers, saying the removal of the requirement for a majority of Ministers to be appointed from Parliament would not eliminate concerns about divided loyalties if MPs could still join the Executive.

Despite its reservations, the network welcomed the government’s acceptance of other proposed reforms, including the establishment of an Independent Public Emoluments Commission and the abolition of the death penalty. Other panellists at the roundtable included Titus Owusu Darko, Secretary for Innovation and Entrepreneurship of the National Union of Ghana Students, and Sharif Ghali, President of the Ghana Youth Federation.

Former Speaker of Parliament and IEA Distinguished Fellow, Rt Hon. Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye, delivered the opening and closing remarks, while Dr William Kofi Osew moderated the discussion.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: Bjorkegren to lead Black Stars for Somalia doubleheader with Tanko and Attram as assistants
Ghana News.content:
Kim Lars Bjorkegren will take charge of the Black Stars for the November international break as the search for a new head coach continues.

The Black Queens gaffer will be in charge for the two games against Somalia next month in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Bjorkegren, who served as assistant of the Black Stars for a game, will return to the setup to lead the team as the interim boss for the doubleheader.

The Swedish trainer will be assisted by Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram for the two games as Ghana search their first win of the qualifying series.

Ghana lost the opening game of the qualifiers to Côte d’Ivoire before losing to Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Bjorkegren will look to steer the Black Stars to victory in the two games which will be played in Ghana.

The Swedish trainer will then turn attention to leading the Black Queens in the first phase of the 2027 Women’s World Cup qualifiers playoffs.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
