The June exercise followed a four-day mass trial in April, during which the government prosecuted 508 defendants. The exercise resulted in 386 convictions, eight discharges and two acquittals, while 112 cases were adjourned to a subsequent phase.

In both exercises, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, led the federal government’s prosecution team.

World.title: Court acquits Malabu Oil, Aliyu Abubakar of OPL 245 deal charges
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has discharged and acquitted Malabu Oil and Gas Limited, the Chairman of AA Oil Limited, Aliyu Abubakar, and six other defendants of money laundering charges relating to the OPL 245 deal.

Delivering judgement on Thursday, Judge Inyang Ekwo held that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) failed to prove the allegations against the defendants beyond reasonable doubt, as required by law.

The EFCC had charged Malabu Oil and Gas Limited, A-Group Construction Company Limited, Rocky Top Resources Limited, Mega Tech Engineering Limited, Novel Properties and Development Company Limited, Imperial Union Limited, Carlin International Nigeria Limited and Mr Abubakar as the first to the eighth defendants in the case.

The charges concerned alleged fraudulent dealings involving the controversial Oil Prospecting Licence 245 (OPL 245) oil block.

But in the judgement, Judge Ekwo faulted the EFCC’s investigation, finding that the investigative officer had not concluded the investigation before the charge was filed.

The judge said the court had a duty to examine how an investigation was conducted and determine whether it was satisfactory. He added that an investigating officer was expected to present evidence of actual investigative work rather than rely on assumptions.

He said where the investigative officer “fails to tender a document or findings made during the course of proceedings, there is something wrong with the investigation.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that it was established law that an investigation must be concluded before a charge is filed, noting that the case before him showed that this requirement had not been met.

Judge Ekwo also faulted the EFCC for proceeding with the prosecution despite a 2018 directive from the then Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, advising against prosecuting the defendants because of insufficient evidence.

The judge said the prosecution ought not to have filed the charges against the advice of the AGF, whom he said would have considered the available evidence before issuing the directive.

“No prosecuting agency is higher in law than the AGF,” he said, adding that a prosecuting agency should not act in a way that suggests it could disregard the attorney-general’s advice or directive and still expect the court to endorse its actions.

He said the court would not endorse a situation in which different arms of the prosecution acted against one another.

Judge Ekwo subsequently held that the prosecution had failed to prove the allegations in counts one to 43 against the defendants beyond reasonable doubt.

“I hereby make an order discharging and acquitting the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth defendants of the respective allegations against each of them in this case,” he declared.

The allegations against Malabu Oil

Among the allegations in the charge, the EFCC accused Malabu Oil and Gas Limited of taking control of funds transferred by the Federal Government into the company’s bank accounts, allegedly in collaboration with three individuals who are at large.

In count two, the commission alleged that Malabu Oil, alongside Seidougha Munamuna, Amaran Joseph and Dauzia Loya Etete, the petreleum minister during thel Sani Abacha regime, took control of $401.54 million transferred by the federal government into the company’s account with First Bank of Nigeria Limited.

In count three, the EFCC alleged that the same defendants took control of another $400 million transferred by the Federal Government into Malabu Oil’s account with Keystone Bank Limited.

The commission alleged that the funds formed part of the proceeds of unlawful activity, contrary to the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act 2011, as amended, and punishable under Section 15(4) of the Act.

The defendants pleaded not guilty to the charges during their arraignment.

Abubakar also acquitted in separate N300 million case

In a separate judgement, Judge Ekwo also discharged and acquitted Mr Abubakar of five counts in a money laundering case involving an alleged N300 million payment.

The judge held that the EFCC had failed to discharge the burden of proof placed on it, saying there was no evidence establishing that Mr Abubakar committed the offences for which he was charged.

“The allegations in counts five, six, seven, eight and nine cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt,” the judge said.

He subsequently ordered the defendant’s discharge.

The separate case arose from charges filed by the EFCC in 2017 against former Attorney-General of the Federation, Mohammed Bello Adoke, and Mr Abubakar, who were listed as the first and second defendants, respectively.

The commission accused them of money laundering involving an alleged N300 million payment.

On 19 April 2024, Judge Ekwo discharged Mr Adoke after upholding his no-case submission, finding that the prosecution had not established sufficient evidence to require him to defend the allegations.

However, the judge ruled at the time that the prosecution had established a prima facie case against Mr Abubakar in counts five to nine, requiring him to defend himself against the allegations.

The judgment brought those remaining counts against Mr Abubakar to an end, with the judge finding that the prosecution had failed to prove them beyond reasonable doubt.

Background to the Malabu case

The Malabu prosecution is linked to the controversy surrounding OPL 245, an oil block awarded to Malabu in 1998. The block later became the subject of investigations into a 2011 settlement involving the Federal Government, Malabu, Shell and Eni, valued at about $1.3 billion.

Investigators subsequently examined the transactions surrounding the settlement, including how the funds were distributed and whether any were diverted.

The EFCC’s prosecution of Mr Abubakar, Malabu Oil and the other companies concerned alleged money laundering arising from dealings linked to the oil block. The separate case involving Mr Adoke and Mr Abubakar concerned the alleged N300 million payment.

The two cases proceeded separately, and the judgments resolved the outstanding charges against the defendants in both proceedings.

World.title: NCDs fastest-growing disease burden in Nigeria — Official
World.content:
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, says Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) have become one of the fastest-growing segments of Nigeria’s disease burden, requiring urgent health system readiness.

Mr Pate said this on Thursday in Abuja at the unveiling of a book on Nigeria’s NCDs and health reforms, organised by the Health Reform Foundation of Nigeria (HERFON).

He said hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, stroke, sickle cell disease, cancers and neurological conditions were increasing due to lifestyle changes and an ageing population.

The coordinating minister said Nigeria’s health reforms began more than 20 years ago, culminating in the National Health Act, with significant progress recorded in the last three years.

He said the Maternal and Neonatal Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative (MAMII) had reduced maternal deaths by 22 per cent and newborn deaths by 10 per cent.

He added that a recent mini Demographic and Health Survey showed increased skilled birth attendance, antenatal care and contraceptive prevalence.

Mr Pate said that malaria incidence had dropped to 15 per cent, the lowest in 20 to 30 years, based on survey statistics, but said HIV, tuberculosis and maternal mortality remained challenges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“NCDs, even though smaller, are becoming an increasingly faster-growing segment of our burden of disease,” he said.

He said the federal government, through the Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, had strengthened governance by bringing federal, state and local governments, civil society and the private sector together.

Health investment

Mr Pate said the federal health budget allocation had increased to six per cent from about three to four per cent previously, while states were being encouraged to increase their funding.

According to him, the government had expanded the primary healthcare system, retrained nearly 80,000 frontline health workers in three years and doubled admission quotas for medical and nursing students.

Mr Pate said three of six world-class tertiary centres had been commissioned in Azare, Enugu and Benin.

He added that 10 world-class diagnostic centres equipped with MRI, CT scanners and catheterisation laboratories had been completed in partnership with MedServe and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA), including two recently completed in Ibadan and Bauchi.

He further added that the Federal Executive Council had recently approved more than N268 billion for major infrastructure projects at the National Hospital, Abuja.

Mr Pate said the government was promoting prevention through the National Health Promotion Policy and the Know Your Numbers campaign, which had reached 10 million Nigerians with checks for blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol and prostate-specific antigen.

He said the government had also introduced Medipool, a group purchasing organisation, to ensure the availability of quality, affordable medicines at primary healthcare centres and improve treatment compliance for hypertension and diabetes.

Mr Pate said affordability remained critical because NCDs required lifelong treatment, noting that more than seven million Nigerians had been added to health insurance in the last three years through the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA).

He added that local pharmaceutical manufacturing was being expanded through the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain (PVAC).

Mr Pate commended HERFON and the book’s authors for providing analysis and recommendations to guide Nigeria’s response to NCDs.

Also speaking, the Chairman of HERFON’s Board of Trustees, Idris Muhammed, said the foundation advocated better healthcare for Nigerians through policy advocacy, capacity building and evidence generation at local, state and national levels.

He said HERFON had a presence in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and had contributed to major health sector achievements, including the enactment of the National Health Act, 2014.

Mr Muhammed said the book was the product of months of review by more than 70 subject experts from Nigeria, South Africa, the Middle East, the United Kingdom and the United States.

“The book tells us where we are, what we are doing wrong and what we must do right to stem the tide of NCDs,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: Opposition parties backing Tinubu remind us of Abacha’s ‘leprous fingers’ transition — Duke
World.content:
Former Governor of Cross River State and presidential candidate for the Peoples Redemption Party in the 2027 general election, Donald Duke has likened opposition parties supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid to political manoeuvres during the late military ruler Sani Abacha’s controversial transition to civilian rule, warning that Nigeria is heading towards disaster.

Mr Duke, who made the claim while appearing on Arise TV Morning Show on Thursday said the alignment of opposition parties with Mr Tinubu undermined the prospect of a credible contest, recalling the five political parties that endorsed General Abacha’s transition programme in the 1990s.

“Some of the opposition parties supporting the president. It is reminiscent of what happened in Abacha’s transition. You know, the five leprous fingers? Yes. So you now have four leprous fingers, because one of the fingers has dropped off,” Mr Duke said.

He warned that Nigerians should take the political direction of the country seriously rather than treat the emerging alliances as routine political manoeuvring.

“You should find time because we shouldn’t be glib about where we’re going. I said that where we’re going in this country is, we’re looking at disaster. We are looking at disaster. We’re doing nothing about it. We’re playing politics with ourselves,” he said.

What were Abacha’s ‘five leprous fingers’?

Mr Duke’s reference was to the five political parties that supported General Abacha’s transition programme and endorsed his bid to become a civilian president before his death in June 1998.

The parties, often collectively described as the “five leprous fingers”, were the United Nigeria Congress Party, National Centre Party of Nigeria, Democratic Party of Nigeria, Grassroots Democratic Movement and Congress for National Consensus.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The expression captured the criticism of the transition programme, under which the five parties converged behind the military ruler rather than provide a meaningful contest for political power.

General Abacha seized power in November 1993, after the collapse of the short-lived Interim National Government established following the annulment of the 12 June 1993 presidential election, widely believed to have been won by Moshood Abiola.

Mr Abacha subsequently introduced a transition programme that critics regarded as an attempt to legitimise continued military rule through a civilian presidency. All five registered political parties eventually adopted him as their consensus presidential candidate.

His death on 8 June 1998 ended the controversial process. General Abdulsalami Abubakar, who succeeded him, initiated a fresh transition programme that culminated in the return to civilian rule in May 1999.

In the build up to the 2027 election, opposition figures from the Peoples Democratic Party, All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Accord Party have openly backed Mr Tinubu.

Also, some Labour Party youth leaders have proposed an alliance with the APC to support President Tinubu’s re-election bid, although the party has not formally endorsed him. This development has given birth to the Rainbow Coalition promoted by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike.

By invoking the analogy, Mr Duke suggested that the willingness of opposition parties to support an incumbent president could weaken democratic competition and leave voters without a credible alternative.

The comparison comes as political actors begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 general election, with the opposition facing questions about its ability to unite around a viable challenge to Mr Tinubu.

Duke criticises Tinubu’s economic policies

Mr Duke said the government should focus on expanding economic production and productivity rather than placing excessive emphasis on revenue collection.

He argued that high interest rates were discouraging businesses from borrowing and investing, limiting their capacity to expand and create jobs.

“You can’t grow your economy at 30-something per cent interest rate. It’s not possible. No one would go to a bank and borrow money at such high costs,” he said.

He also said inflation is caused by high energy costs, arguing that reducing petrol prices would help lower production expenses and ease pressure on households and businesses.

“The central bank will tell you it’s because of inflation. What are the inflationary items? Your cost of fuel is horrendous. So that is an inflation. And that’s why it makes it incumbent to try and bring down the price of fuel as low as possible,” he said.

Mr Duke criticised the government’s economic management, insisting that its focus on revenue generation did not adequately account for the productive capacity of the economy.

“This tax minister who sells himself coordinating minister of economy, you know, big names kill small dogs, right? He’s looking at revenue, not the totality of the economy,” he said.

He argued that Nigeria should be raising a larger share of its gross domestic product through its budget and expanding the tax base by growing economic activity.

“If you say you’re the largest economy in Africa and your GDP is about $400-and-something billion or so, the figures, you should be able to raise about 15 to 20 per cent of your GDP as your budget. We’re still at five per cent. So we’re not even capturing the numbers we should,” he said.

He warned that excessive dependence on petroleum-related earnings would perpetuate the country’s economic difficulties rather than promote sustainable development.

“We’re just focusing on petrol. But it’s a double-edged sword, because if you focus on that, you’ll remain poor, as we are,” he said.

Energy, healthcare, education priorities

Asked about his immediate priorities if elected president, Mr Duke identified energy, healthcare, education, infrastructure and the productivity of Nigerians as key areas requiring urgent attention.

“Everything in Nigeria is almost a state of urgency, but I’ll strengthen, I’ll come back to this energy thing because it’s what is stifling the country, right? I’ll focus on health, I’ll focus on education, of course, infrastructure, but more importantly, I’ll be focusing on the productivity of Nigerians,” he said.

He said that the cost of living had become unsustainable for workers, whose earnings were increasingly inadequate to cover basic expenses.

“Nigerians are not productive because the banks are not lending. The cost, look, the average, if you’re a worker, your one salary can’t fill your minimum wage, can’t fill your tank. Those are the things killing Nigerians,” he said.

Mr Duke declined to promise an immediate salary increase, saying a government should first examine the costs eroding workers’ incomes.

“I didn’t say I would increase salaries. Oh, okay. No, I can’t sit down on this chair and say I’m going to increase salaries because there’s so many things you’ve got to look at,” he said.

“What I will strive to do is reduce the cost of those things that grapple at our salaries.”

World.title: UEL: Lyon down Crystal Palace 3-2, Sunderland leave it late
World.content:
Crystal Palace’s Argentine goalkeeper #44 Walter Benitez clears the ball during the UEFA Europa League, league phase matchday 2, football match between Olympique Lyonnais and Crystal Palace at the Groupama Stadium in Decines-Charpieu, near Lyon, on October 15, 2026. (Photo by OLIVIER CHASSIGNOLE / AFP)

Ligue 1 club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense.

Bayer Leverkusen went top of the table with a 4-0 win, while AC Milan strolled to victory by the same scoreline.

It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions.

Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes when Corentin Tolisso was quickest to react to the dropping ball at a corner to prod the hosts in front.

Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage two minutes into first-half injury time as he tucked home Keito Nakamura’s cross at the end of a slick move.

A clever set-piece routine allowed Yeremy Pino to halve the deficit for Palace early in the second period.

A clever close-range flick by Pavel Sulc then restored the two-goal buffer for Paulo Fonseca’s charges just inside the final quarter hour.

Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes on the clock but the home side held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase.

In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki’s 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors.

The 15th-placed side in Portugal’s second division stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot.

Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores.

After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner.

– Cisse on fire –

Bayer Leverkusen sit pretty at the top of the standings as they followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan.

Czech striker Patrik Schick was on target twice from the penalty spot in the first half, either side of a Malik Tillman goal, to ensure the points were wrapped up for Carles Martinez’s side before the interval. Ibrahim Maza added a late fourth.

AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse.

Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim’s men.

La Liga’s Real Sociedad followed up their matchday one loss at home to Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Union Saint-Gilloise.

Later, Celtic travel to Lisbon to take on Benfica and Celta Vigo host Italian giants Juventus.

Bournemouth’s Vitality Stadium will welcome European football for the first time in the Premier League outfit’s history as they welcome Austrians Sturm Graz.

AFP

World.title: People move to Lagos because things are working  — Former lawmaker
World.content:
Hon. Taiwo Kolawole, former federal lawmaker.

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Deputy Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Hon. Kolawole Taiwo, has attributed the state’s growing population and pressure on public infrastructure to its perceived success, saying people continue to move to Lagos because “things are working.”

Taiwo, who represented Ajeromi-Ifelodun Constituency and served as Majority Leader in the Assembly, said this on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he discussed why the All Progressives Congress (APC) has continued to govern Lagos since 1999 despite persistent challenges.

Explaining why Lagos continues to experience population growth and infrastructure pressure, the former lawmaker said the situation partly reflects the state’s success, which has continued to attract people from different parts of the country.

“The problem in Lagos is a result of the success, and when you are successful, there are some things that will happen to you that, if you are not careful, it would look like it is consuming you,” Taiwo said.

He further argued that the state’s growing population had increased the pressure on infrastructure and public services, noting that Lagos had grown from about six million people in 1999 to an estimated 20 million today.

“What was the population of Lagos in 1999 compared to the population of Lagos now? 20 million. What was the population of Lagos then? It was around than 6 million,” he said.

Taiwo argued that people naturally move to places where they believe opportunities and public services are better, adding that Lagos’ appeal had contributed to the pressure on its infrastructure.

“Anywhere there is a good thing, people will move there, and that is what is happening; people are moving towards Lagos because things are working,” the former lawmaker added.

“We need a place to put our heads, and there is no government in Lagos that did not do one housing project or the other.”

The former Deputy Speaker maintained that successive administrations in the state had undertaken housing projects, insisting that Lagos was making progress despite residents’ concerns aboutits development challenges. “Lagos is improving,” he noted.

Taiwo also addressed complaints about refuse collection and waste management, arguing that the increased attention being paid to the problem reflected a change in residents’ awareness and willingness to speak up when public services fell short.

“The reason why people are complaining more about refuse now is that their consciousness is very high,” he added.

“In those days, the refuse situation was worse than this but nobody sees it. But now, if you ever see a small thing that is not working well, you will see somebody who will say something.”

World.title: Top 5 oldest countries in the world
World.content:
Some of the world’s oldest countries have histories stretching back thousands of years, with ancient civilisations that developed early systems of government, writing, trade, religion and law.

However, ranking the oldest countries in the world depends on whether age is measured by the emergence of ancient civilisation, the formation of a unified state or continuous sovereignty. Egypt, Iran, China, India and Greece are among the countries with some of the world’s oldest historical roots.

Here are five of the oldest countries in the world based on the history of their ancient civilisations and early states.

1. Egypt

Egypt is home to one of the world’s oldest civilisations, with the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt traditionally dated to around 3100 BC.

Ancient Egyptian civilisation flourished along the River Nile, producing monumental pyramids, hieroglyphic writing and sophisticated systems of administration. Despite centuries of foreign rule, Egypt has retained a strong connection to its ancient heritage.

Its capital is Cairo, and the country remains an important cultural and political centre in North Africa and the Middle East.

2. Iran

Iran, historically known as Persia, has roots in ancient civilisations dating back thousands of years. The region was home to Elamite societies, with organised political centres emerging during the third millennium BC.

The Achaemenid Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC, later became one of the largest empires of the ancient world.

Although Iran’s political systems have changed considerably over the centuries, the country has maintained a distinctive Persian cultural and historical identity. Its capital is Tehran.

3. China

China has one of the world’s longest recorded histories, with early civilisations developing thousands of years ago.

The Xia dynasty is traditionally dated to around 2070 BC, although details of its history remain debated. The Shang dynasty, which emerged around 1600 BC, is supported by archaeological evidence, including inscriptions on oracle bones.

China subsequently developed powerful dynasties, extensive administrative systems and influential philosophical traditions. Despite major political changes, its cultural and written historical heritage spans several millennia.

Beijing is the country’s capital.

4. India

India’s historical roots extend to the Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished in parts of present-day India and Pakistan more than 4,000 years ago.

Major urban centres such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro featured organised settlements, drainage systems and extensive trading networks. Later societies developed influential religious, philosophical and political traditions across the Indian subcontinent.

India’s modern republic was established in 1950, following independence from British rule in 1947. Its ancient civilisation, however, predates the modern state by thousands of years.

New Delhi is India’s capital.

5. Greece

Greece has a rich history associated with the Minoan and Mycenaean civilisations, which flourished in the Aegean region during the second millennium BC.

Ancient Greece later became known for its contributions to philosophy, mathematics, politics, drama and science. Its influence helped shape many aspects of modern Western thought and institutions.

However, the modern Greek state was established in the nineteenth century after a war of independence against Ottoman rule. Greece’s ancient civilisation and the modern country’s founding date therefore represent different historical milestones.

Athens is the country’s capital.

Vanguard News

World.title: Martinez apologises for outburst after meeting with Man Utd officials
World.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for publicly criticising the club’s board for a lack of investment in the transfer market following their defeat by Atletico Madrid.

The English giants lost 2-0 to Atletico in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League. They are also off to their worst start to a Premier League season for 40 years.

Martinez took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad during the transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season to return to Europe’s top competition.

United signed three midfielders — Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — for around £150 million ($198 million), but their spending fell far short of some of their Premier League rivals.

In a social media post earlier Thursday, Martinez said he had spoken “out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted”, but stopped short of apologising.

But having faced criticism for piling pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick following United’s poor start to the season, Martinez met with club officials.

– ‘Passionate’ –

Afterwards, Martinez issued a fresh statement saying: “Today (Thursday) I met with the club’s leadership and the manager.

“It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

“The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

The Argentina international’s post-match comments were backed by some fans.

But Martinez has been criticised for his own part in United’s sluggish start to the season.

He scored an own goal in a 1-1 draw at bottom-of-the-table Fulham last month and was outmuscled by Dominic Solanke as 10-man Tottenham salvaged a point at Old Trafford last weekend.

“When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level,” said Martinez.

“These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

“I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.”

Pressure is increasing on Carrick just months after he was appointed manager on a permanent basis.

Carrick’s men travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday before another Champions League trip, to Italian side Como, on Wednesday.

AFP

World.title: Kefas campaign challenges Taraba opposition to unveil manifestos
World.content:
Kefas

By Femi Bolaji

JALINGO — The re-election campaign council of Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, has challenged opposition parties and governorship aspirants to present their manifestos and policy alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections, rather than focus on criticism of the incumbent.

The Director of Media and Strategic Communications of the campaign council, Hon. Emmanuel Bello, made the call in a statement issued in Jalingo on Thursday.

Bello said election campaigns should focus on practical ideas, realistic policy proposals and competing visions for the development of the state, rather than personal attacks and complaints.

He accused some opposition figures of making Kefas the central focus of their campaign engagements without adequately explaining what they would do differently if elected.

“Election campaigns should be an opportunity for candidates to explain their manifestos, present workable solutions to public concerns, and convince voters why they deserve the mandate to lead.

“Unfortunately, much of the opposition’s campaign in Taraba State has been dominated by complaints, accusations and personal attacks rather than clear policy alternatives,” he said.

Bello asked opposition candidates to explain their plans for addressing the state’s challenges beyond criticising the incumbent administration.

He said their proposals should cover critical sectors, including security, education, healthcare, infrastructure, civil service welfare and youth empowerment.

The campaign spokesman also challenged opposition candidates to publish costed policy documents and financing plans outlining how they intended to fund their proposed programmes.

“Criticism is easy. Governing requires ideas, priorities and the capacity to deliver. If the opposition believes the present administration has fallen short, they should identify the gaps and offer practical, costed and achievable solutions,” he said.

Bello added that the 2027 election should provide an opportunity for candidates to demonstrate their preparedness for governance through clear policies and achievable commitments.

“Anger is not a development plan, accusations are not policy alternatives, and slogans cannot replace the hard work of leadership. The 2027 contest should be about who can present the clearest vision and the strongest commitment to delivering results for the people of Taraba State,” he said.

He maintained that the Kefas administration would continue to defend its Moving Forward agenda through what he described as achievements across key sectors.

Bello urged voters to scrutinise the manifestos, policy proposals and verifiable records of all candidates before making their choices in the 2027 elections.

World.title: 2027: Idris urges Nigerians to reject voter apathy, vote buying
World.content:
Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris

By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has urged Nigerians to reject voter apathy, vote buying and electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general election, calling for greater participation in the democratic process.

Idris said eligible voters had a responsibility to protect democracy by participating peacefully in elections, warning that staying away from the polls, selling votes and resorting to violence could undermine the electoral process.

The minister made the call in a statement issued on Thursday by his Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, following the flag-off of the National Orientation Agency’s nationwide grassroots mobilisation campaign for the 2027 general election.

The campaign, themed, “Your Vote, Your Voice, Our Future: Say No to Apathy, Vote Buying and Violence. Let’s Build a United Nigeria in 2027,” seeks to promote responsible electoral participation and peaceful elections across the country.

“An election is more than a day at the polling unit. It is an opportunity for citizens to decide who represents them and to influence the direction of their communities and country. When eligible voters stay away, sell their votes or resort to violence, the entire democratic process suffers,” Idris said.

He said the Federal Government, under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, remained committed to strengthening the democratic process and improving public confidence in elections.

According to him, Tinubu signed the Electoral Act 2026 into law, introducing reforms aimed at improving transparency and accountability in the electoral process.

Idris commended the Director-General of the NOA, Lanre Issa-Onilu, and the agency’s staff for initiating the campaign, urging them to sustain public engagement nationwide.

He said the initiative’s success would depend on collaboration among government institutions, electoral authorities, security agencies, community leaders and citizens.

Speaking at the event, Issa-Onilu said the agency would deploy its state directorates across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to mobilise citizens at the grassroots.

He said the campaign would use local languages, radio programmes, community dialogues, drama and digital platforms to tackle voter apathy, discourage vote buying and prevent electoral violence.

“The National Orientation Agency will take this campaign to communities across the country, engaging Nigerians in languages they understand to promote voter participation, discourage vote buying and electoral violence, and encourage the responsible sharing of verified information,” Issa-Onilu said.

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to conducting a credible and inclusive 2027 general election.

He urged Nigerians to work with electoral stakeholders to ensure peaceful participation, stressing that the success of the polls would require adequate preparation and collective responsibility.

“INEC is committed to conducting a free, fair, transparent, inclusive and credible 2027 General Election. Achieving this requires early preparation, strong collaboration among stakeholders and the active participation of Nigerians,” he said.

World.title: Caicedo calls Chelsea ‘home’, vows to repay Alonso’s faith after injury return
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo has described the Premier League club as his “home” and vowed to continue improving as well as become more of a leader on the pitch under manager Xabi Alonso following his return from injury.

The Ecuador international made his first start under Alonso in Chelsea’s 5-1 Premier League victory over Bournemouth on Saturday after recovering from a calf injury that restricted his involvement at the start of the season.

Speaking in an interview published on Chelsea’s official website, Caicedo expressed gratitude for the support he has received at Stamford Bridge and said he was determined to justify the trust placed in him by the club’s manager and supporters.

“I can say Chelsea is my home, because they treat me like I’ve been here for a long, long time,” Caicedo said.

“It’s a special place for me. I want to always give them happiness because I know they did everything for me.”

The 24-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Brighton and Hove Albion in 2023, also acknowledged Alonso’s influence on his development, promising to continue working to meet the manager’s expectations.

“With Xabi I am going to keep developing, for sure, and show him why he trusts me,” he said.

Caicedo made an immediate impact against Bournemouth, helping Chelsea establish control in midfield as they secured a convincing victory at Stamford Bridge.

He won a tackle in the build-up to Jordan Henderson’s opening goal before winning possession again in the move that led to Morgan Rogers doubling Chelsea’s advantage.

The midfielder was substituted in the 72nd minute after Chelsea had taken a 5-1 lead, receiving a standing ovation from the home supporters.

Beyond his performances on the pitch, Caicedo said he wanted to become more vocal as a leader within the Chelsea squad. The midfielder is part of the club’s leadership group but admitted that communicating more with his teammates remains an area he needs to improve.

“I think every coach tells me that I can improve talking on the pitch, you know? Because they know that I’m a leader, but it will be better for me if I start talking more with the players,” he said.

“I try my best, but it’s not in my nature. So when I’m not able to talk, I just try to show even more.”

Caicedo also credited former Chelsea defender Thiago Silva with providing an example of effective leadership during their time together at the club.

He described being part of the leadership group as a source of pride for himself and his family, adding that he preferred to lead through his performances and actions.

The Ecuadorian also praised Chelsea supporters for their backing, particularly fans in his home country, where the club has expanded its community presence.

He said hearing supporters sing his song was an amazing feeling and motivated him to deliver consistently strong performances.

Caicedo, who has won major honours with Chelsea, said he was confident he could achieve more success under Alonso as he looks to build on his progress at the club.

His return from injury and determination to develop further provide a timely boost for Chelsea as they seek to maintain their momentum in the Premier League.

World.title: NSITF boss calls for stronger collaboration to boost workers’ welfare
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Oluwaseun Faleye, has urged stronger collaboration among public service agencies to improve workers’ welfare, boost productivity and strengthen social security.

The NSITF MD made the call on Thursday in Abuja while delivering a goodwill message at the Technical Retreat on Presidential Priorities, Ministerial Deliverables and the Performance Management System (PMS).

He commended the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment for convening the meeting, describing it as a vital platform for dialogue, coordination and exchange of ideas among agencies with shared institutional responsibilities.

“I commend the Ministry for providing this platform for dialogue, coordination and the exchange of ideas, such engagements are important because the effectiveness of public service delivery depends not only on the performance of individual institutions, but also on how well we work together,” he said.

Faleye, who was represented at the retreat by his Technical Assistant, Dayo Aloa, noted that the collective responsibility of the Ministry of Labour and NSITF remains the same, “to deliver public value, strengthen institutions and improve the welfare and security of Nigerians.”

Speaking on the Fund’s mandate, Faleye explained that the NSITF administers the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS) established under the Employees’ Compensation Act 2010, which provides compensation and support for employees and their dependants in cases of work-related injuries, occupational diseases, disabilities and death.

“At the heart of this mandate is a simple but important principle: no worker or family should be left without support when a qualifying workplace incident disrupts their livelihood and future,” he said.

He stressed that workers’ welfare is inseparable from national productivity, industrial harmony and sustainable economic development, adding that a worker who feels protected contributes more meaningfully to the workplace.

Faleye further stated that the Fund’s role goes beyond claims processing and payment of compensation, but includes sustained engagement with employers and workers, improved awareness of the Scheme, stronger compliance with statutory obligations and commitment to workplace health and safety.

“We must remain focused on making the Scheme accessible, responsive, transparent and effective for those entitled to its protection,” he stressed.

Emphasizing that no single agency can address all dimensions of workers’ welfare, employment protection, workplace safety and social security alone, the NSITF boss called for reduced duplication, knowledge sharing and more coherent responses to challenges facing Nigerian workers and employers.

“I therefore see this meeting as an opportunity to deepen our working relationships, identify practical areas of collaboration and strengthen the alignment between our respective programmes and priorities,” he noted.

Looking ahead to 2027, the Managing Director reaffirmed NSITF’s commitment to strengthening implementation of the ECS, improving service delivery, promoting employer compliance and advancing workplace safety.

“As we deliberate on our institutional responsibilities and targets, we should remain mindful that the ultimate measure of our success is not merely the activities we undertake, but the tangible improvements our work delivers to the people we serve,” he said.

He thanked the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and participating agencies for their contributions to public service delivery and wished the meeting fruitful deliberations that will lead to a more productive and secure Nigeria.

World.title: Two Boko Haram Members Bag Life Sentences in Abuja
World.content:
Two men arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) have been sentenced to life imprisonment by a Federal High Court in Abuja for their membership of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group.

The convicts, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were handed the sentences after pleading guilty to charges bordering on membership of and providing support for the terrorist group, as well as concealing information on its activities.

Presiding over the case, Justice Salim Ibrahim sentenced the two men to life imprisonment on the first count and 20 years’ imprisonment on the second count.

The judgment was delivered during the Federal Government’s latest phase of mass trials of suspected terrorists, which began on Thursday and is being conducted across several courtrooms.

Other judges handling the proceedings include Justices James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu.

No fewer than 34 suspects were listed for proceedings before Justice Ibrahim, while 25 others were listed before Justice Lifu.

The mass trials form part of the Federal Government’s ongoing judicial proceedings involving suspected members and supporters of terrorist groups.

World.title: Cardoso Makes Case for Transparent, Consensus-driven Monetary Policy at IMF Forum
World.content:
Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, has emphasised that credible monetary policy depends on informed committee deliberations, independent perspectives and clear communication of decisions to financial markets and the public.

Speaking at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) seminar in Bangkok on Thursday, Cardoso explained how the CBN has strengthened these practices within its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), drawing on Nigeria’s experience of navigating complex economic reforms and restoring confidence in monetary policymaking.

The seminar, ‘How Central Banks Decide: Committee Decision-Making and Communication in an Era of Uncertainty,’ brought together Cardoso; Chairman of the Swiss National Bank’s Governing Board, Martin Schlegel; and Governor of the Banque de France and member of the European Central Bank’s Governing Council, Emmanuel Moulin. The discussion was moderated by IMF First Deputy Managing Director, Dan Katz.

Addressing the role of committee members in reaching credible decisions, Cardoso explained that the CBN provides external MPC members with dedicated technical support and opportunities to consult independent specialists.

The bank also organises retreats involving experts from other central banks and wider stakeholder engagements, allowing members to consider diverse economic perspectives beyond formal policy meetings.

These arrangements extend to Nigeria’s ongoing transition towards inflation targeting, supported by IMF technical assistance, with external members involved from the outset of the process.

Cardoso said the arrangements were particularly important in establishing the credibility of the MPC following the economic and institutional challenges confronting the CBN when the current leadership assumed office.

He also highlighted the bank’s practice of publishing individual MPC members’ policy statements, which provides greater transparency around the reasoning behind monetary policy decisions.

According to Cardoso, he personally reviews the statements to understand the different assessments informing committee deliberations, including opinions that may differ from the eventual decision.

On the role of leadership, he explained that effective deliberation requires identifying areas of agreement before addressing disagreements and proceeding to a vote.

“What are the things we all agree on? That should be number one. What are the things we don’t really agree on? And then number three, of course, is to vote,” he said.

Cardoso noted that this approach helps prevent committees from becoming absorbed in relatively minor disagreements while losing sight of the broader economic questions requiring decisions.

His remarks reflected a central theme of the IMF discussion: how central banks can encourage rigorous internal debate while maintaining a coherent institutional position.

Schlegel described the Swiss National Bank’s approach, where governing board members examine the merits and disadvantages of competing policy options before reaching consensus. The institution communicates a common position without attributing individual votes, a practice he said also helps protect members from external pressure.

Moulin discussed the European Central Bank’s consensus-building culture under President Christine Lagarde, highlighting inclusive deliberations, equal access to information and a shared monetary policy framework. He stressed that communication must help households understand the implications of policy decisions for prices, employment and borrowing costs.

Cardoso illustrated the application of Nigeria’s approach through the September MPC meeting, when members agreed that weaknesses in the monetary policy transmission mechanism required correction.

That common assessment helped focus deliberations on the appropriate response, resulting in a 350-basis-point reduction in the benchmark interest rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent.

He explained that Nigeria’s distinct inflation cycle, influenced by foreign-exchange harmonisation and subsidy reforms, required the committee to assess domestic economic conditions rather than simply follow monetary policy developments in other countries.

Although the decision surprised markets, Cardoso said earlier reforms, stronger economic fundamentals and carefully considered communication helped investors understand its rationale.

“To do such a thing successfully, you must have an element of credibility with the market,” he said.

Katz observed that financial markets absorbed the unexpected decision without significant disruption, describing the response as a testament to the clarity and credibility of the CBN’s communications.

The discussion also examined the growing role of artificial intelligence in interpreting central bank statements. Schlegel emphasised the importance of precise language, while Katz disclosed that the IMF had developed AI tools to analyse monetary policy communications in near real time.

In closing, Katz noted that although central banks operate under different governance arrangements, effective decision-making depends on candid debate, diverse perspectives, strong leadership and clear communication.

Cardoso’s contribution offered Nigeria’s experience of combining independent participation, transparent policy assessments and structured committee deliberations with the responsibility to communicate collective decisions clearly.

The exchange highlighted how the credibility of monetary policy is shaped not only by the decisions central banks announce, but also by the institutional processes through which those decisions are reached.

World.title: Senate Declares ‘No Vacancy’ As Akpabio, Barau Get Backing for 11th Assembly
World.content:
* Lawmakers endorse return of principal officers

* Dismiss politically motivated attacks on Senate President

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Thursday threw its weight behind Senate President Godswill Akpabio’s bid to retain his position in the 11th National Assembly, declaring that there would be “no vacancy” in the offices of the Senate President, Deputy Senate President and other principal officers who secure re-election in the 2027 general election.

The endorsement, which followed a spontaneous motion moved by the Senate Chief Whip, Tahir Monguno, and seconded by Senator Cyril Fasuyi, signalled an early attempt by serving lawmakers to consolidate support for the current leadership ahead of the inauguration of the next National Assembly.

The lawmakers also backed the return of Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin, Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, Monguno and Deputy Senate Whip Peter Nwaebonyi, alongside Minority Leader Abba Moro, Deputy Minority Leader Olalere Oyewumi and Minority Whip Tony Nwoye, provided they win re-election on January 16, 2027.

Monguno, who represents Borno North, moved the motion during plenary after Akpabio complained that political opponents were allegedly exploiting controversies surrounding recent Senate debates to undermine his reputation and weaken his chances of retaining the Senate presidency.

“Insha Allah, by the grace of God, the majority of us are going to make it back to the Senate, and this seat is hereby declared: there is no vacancy,” Monguno said.

He extended the declaration to the office of the Deputy Senate President and other principal officers, insisting that those who returned to the Senate after the elections should retain their positions.

“There is no vacancy at all, including the seat of the Deputy Senate President and all other principal officers. I hereby declare, there is no vacancy,” he added.

Fasuyi, who represents Ekiti North, immediately endorsed the motion, declaring that Akpabio’s position should not be open to a contest in the next Assembly.

“I hereby support the motion ably moved by Senator Monguno that the seat of the Senate President in the 11th Assembly is not open to any contest. It is already occupied by Senator Godswill Obot Akpabio,” he said.

Akpabio subsequently put the declaration to a voice vote, with senators present responding affirmatively when he called for those in support. No audible opposition was recorded during the exchange.

“I think that settles it,” the Senate President declared.

However, the endorsement does not remove the constitutional requirement for newly elected senators to elect their presiding officers when the 11th National Assembly is inaugurated. The declaration instead reflects the position expressed by the lawmakers who supported the motion.

The development comes amid speculation that other political heavyweights, including Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and Senator Adams Oshiomhole, may be interested in the Senate presidency.

Before the motion, Akpabio had defended himself against what he described as politically motivated attempts to misrepresent his comments during Tuesday’s debate on the Suicide Prevention Bill 2026.

The bill, sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, representing Cross River South, scaled second reading and triggered debate on whether survivors of suicide attempts should face criminal prosecution or receive medical and psychological assistance.

Akpabio cautioned commentators against interpreting individual contributions during legislative debates as the Senate’s final position.

“When we discuss here, we discuss for and against, and in the course of our discussions, whatever we say should not anger anybody outside this chamber, because at the end, what matters is our final decision,” he said.

He argued that lawmakers must be allowed to disagree during deliberations without their remarks being distorted to damage their reputations.

He said: “We want to make the best laws, so we are bound to oppose each other, and we are also bound to support each other,” urging television commentators to avoid politically motivated interpretations of parliamentary proceedings.

“No matter the discussion, please take the final decision of the Senate into consideration. Don’t go and sit down in panels and try to do politically motivated discussions,” Akpabio added.

The Senate President also rejected attempts to associate terrorism with any particular religion, insisting that acts of violence should not be used to stigmatise religious communities.

“Terrorists are not Muslims. Terrorists are not Christians. Terrorists are human beings who believe in taking their lives and the lives of others,” he said.

Akpabio maintained that Islam prohibits suicide and killing, adding that public discussions should distinguish between people experiencing mental health challenges and those who deliberately take their lives or harm others.

He also cited his longstanding relationships with Muslims and Christians, including his support for religious pilgrimages, to reject allegations of religious bias.

Akpabio’s defence and the subsequent endorsement of his leadership highlighted the political sensitivities surrounding the Senate presidency as lawmakers prepare for the 2027 elections.

While Thursday’s declaration demonstrated support for the current leadership among the senators who backed the motion, the final composition of the 11th Senate and its choice of presiding officers will be determined after the elections.

World.title: ODCF Lauds Makinde for Developmental Strides in Oke Ogun
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

President of the Oke Ogun Development Consultative Forum (ODCF), Alhaji Ahmed Raji (SAN), on Thursday, lauded Oyo State Governor, ‘Seyi Makinde, for the administration’s developmental strides in Iseyin and the wider Oke Ogun Zone.

Raji spoke at the inauguration and handover of the Alhaji Kazeem Owonikoko Building at L.A. Primary School, Oke Esa, Iseyin, which he donated to the state government.

He praised Governor Makinde for major infrastructure projects, including the Moniya–Iseyin Road, the Oyo–Iseyin Road, and the Iseyin–Fapote–Ogbomoso Road. The newly donated building, equipped with classrooms, offices, solar power, desks, chairs and modern learning gadgets, was described as a world class educational facility.

The legal icon particularly lauded the establishment of the College of Agricultural Sciences and Renewable Natural Resources, a campus of the Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, in Iseyin.

He said: “When those who call themselves progressives were in government, they didn’t give us this. You came and gave us what they could not.”

Raji appealed to the governor to grant autonomy to the Iseyin campus as a full fledged university, adding that the people of Oke Ogun deeply appreciate the governor’s contributions to infrastructure and education.

In his remarks, Governor Makinde thanked Raji for transforming the 92-year-old school, noting that the gesture demonstrated that government alone cannot meet all societal needs.

He said well-meaning individuals must continue to support education and community development.

Makinde said: “This building can stand anywhere in the world. It shows that no government can do everything alone. Those who are blessed must support the education of our children.”

The governor reiterated his commitment to serving Oyo State without bias for political affiliations, stressing that development, not party labels, guides his administration.

He encouraged Raji to continue his philanthropic efforts, noting that while governments and political parties come and go, Oyo State remains.

Makinde also highlighted ongoing industrial development in Iseyin, including the sugar factory near Fasola Farms, which is currently undergoing test running. He said improved road networks have made the project viable and positioned Iseyin for global recognition.

Responding to Raji’s request for autonomy for the LAUTECH Iseyin Campus, Governor Makinde said: “Regarding your request on the Iseyin Campus of LAUTECH becoming an autonomous university, we will go through the process. We will apply through the NUC, and I will carry out a sustainability study too. So, what you have asked for is done.”

Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Justice and Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), Prince Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), commended Raji for the project, just as he called on individuals to join hands to support the Makinde administration.

He said: “I am happy to witness a day like this. This is a very good project from my respected colleague. I want to add that all of us need to join hands together to keep supporting Governor Seyi Makinde.”

Speaking on behalf of the Owonikoko family, Mr Abduljelil Owonikoko (SAN) and the Headteacher of L.A. Primary School, Mr. Dauda, thanked Governor Makinde for prioritising education and transforming Iseyin into a hub of opportunities.

Present at the event included the Deputy Governor of Oyo State, Mr ‘Bayo Lawal; a retired Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Abdul Aboki (rtd); Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Hon. Adebo Ogundoyin; Member representing Iseyin/Itesiwaju/Kajola/Iwajowa Federal Constituency, Hon. Shina Oyedeji; Secretary to the State Government, Professor Musibau Babatunde; Chief of Staff to the Governor, Bashorun Akinwale Akinwole; Head of Service, Dr. (Mrs.) Adenike Fashina; Deputy Chief of Staff, Hon. Kazeem Adeniyi; and Senior Executive Assistant to the Governor on General Duties, Chief Bayo Lawal.

Others present included Chief Niyi Akintola (SAN); deputy governorship candidate of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), Mr. Mufutau Open Salawu; Director General of the APM Apex Campaign Council, Oyo State, Dr. Nureni Adeniran; and the House of Assembly candidate for Iseyin/Itesiwaju State Constituency, Mr Dasola Fadiran.

World.title: ASUU Condemns Arrest, Arraignment of ABU Don, Accuses Katsina Govt of Intimidating Academics
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Sokoto Zone, has condemned the arrest and arraignment of Dr. Kurfi of Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, describing it as intimidation of academics by the Katsina State Government.

The Zonal Chairman of the Union, Professor Abubakar Sabo Yabo, who briefed journalists in Sokoto said Dr. Kurfi was arrested by operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) allegedly on the instruction of the Katsina State Government over his comments on the security situation in the state.

Yabo said the development remains an issue of grave concern to the academic community and the general public, as it raises questions about the misplacement of government priorities.

According to him, it is evident that the recent antics of the government showcase a tendency to instil fear in an already traumatised nation, rather than provide solutions to pressing challenges.

He noted that while ASUU accepts the application of the rule of law in every circumstance, where it becomes a tool for intimidation, it becomes a serious matter of concern to the Union.

The Zonal Chairman stressed that deploying instruments of state security to harass an academic for expressing views on insecurity amounts to an assault on freedom of expression and academic freedom.

He therefore called on the Katsina State Government to focus sincerely on addressing the economic, social and security challenges affecting the state, rather than resorting to unnecessary intimidation of academics.

Yabo further called on relevant security agencies and the judiciary to be fair and impartial in treating Dr. Kurfi, insisting that due process must be strictly observed.

He added: “Let it be on record that Nigerians are watching as the legal processes take place. Justice to one is justice to all, while injustice to one is injustice to all.”

The Union warned that it would not stand aloof while its members are harassed under the guise of law enforcement, stressing that an injury to one academic is an injury to all.

Efforts to get the reaction of the Katsina State Government as at press time proved abortive.

World.title: Customs Intercepts Contraband Worth N722m in Sokoto
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command, has intercepted assorted contraband goods with a Duty Paid Value of N721.9 million.

The Acting Customs Area Controller of the Command, Deputy Comptroller Haliru Isah Abdullahi, disclosed this on Thursday at a press briefing held at the Command Headquarters in Sokoto.

Abdullahi said the seizures were made in line with the policy thrust of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, which emphasises consolidation, collaboration and innovation.

He said despite insecurity in parts of the two states, operatives of the Command have sustained anti-smuggling operations to secure the borders and protect the nation’s economy.

Giving a breakdown of the seizures, the Controller listed one used DAF truck with registration number JEG 199 XA and Chassis No. XLRAS85WCOE421859 used as means of conveyance, 599 bales of second-hand clothes and seven sacks of second-hand women’s bags.

Other items, according to him, include 43 cartons of cigarettes, seven cartons of Akouna coffee and a large quantity of unregistered pharmaceutical products.

He listed the pharmaceutical products as 100 packages of quinine, 500 packages of amodiaquine, 140 packages of paracetamol, 300 packages of anti-cold tablets, one carton of analgesic injections, two cartons of Dynewell syrup, one carton of Dynewell tablets and one carton of Clear Cold.

Abdullahi put the cumulative Duty Paid Value (DPV) of the seized items at N721,957,021.41.

He said the actions of operatives were in line with the provisions of Sections 245 and 248 of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023, which empowers the Service to seize and condemn any goods liable to forfeiture.

The Acting Controller appealed to well-meaning Nigerians to provide credible information that would aid the eradication of smuggling, noting that curbing the menace would prevent consumption of unregistered drugs that pose grave danger to citizens’ health.

He also warned smugglers and their collaborators to desist from the nefarious act, stressing that the Command under his watch would not be a safe haven for economic saboteurs.

Abdullahi commended the Comptroller-General of Customs, officers and men of the Command for their resilience, sister security agencies for their collaboration and members of the press for their support in sensitising the public.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, collecting revenue for national development and suppressing smuggling to the barest minimum.

World.title: FACC Disburses N2.428tn September Allocations as Federation Revenue Grosses N3.913tn
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has disbursed a total of N2.428 trillion to the Federal Government, states and local government councils, as Federation Revenue grossed N3.913 trillion for September 2026.

FAAC shared the amount during its October meeting in Abuja, Thursday, the Director of Press and Public Relations, Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation (OAGF), Bawa Mokwa, said in a statement.

The N2.428 trillion September allocations surpassed the sum of N2.338 trillion shared in the preceding month of August by N90 billion.

Citing the communiqué issued at the meeting, Mokwa said from the N2.428 trillion distributable revenue, the Federal Government received N832.242 billion, state governments received N799.872 billion, while local government councils got N560.660 billion.

The sum of N236.049 billion went to oil mineral producing states as 13 per cent derivation revenue.

The N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue for September comprised a distributable statutory revenue of N1.672 trillion and distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N756.587 billion.

Although gross revenue was N3.913 trillion in September, total deductions for cost of collection stood at N131.758 billion, while total transfers, refunds and savings accounted for N1.352 trillion.

According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of N3.096 trillion was received for September 2026, an amount higher than the sum of N2.850 trillion received in the preceeding month by N246.384 billion.

Value Added Tax (VAT) also posted a gross revenue of N816.872 billion in September, N17.972 billion, an amount less than the N834.843 billion recorded in August 2026.

However, from the N816.872 billion gross VAT revenue, distributable VAT revenue was N756.587 billion from which the Federal Government received N75.659 billion, state governments got N416.123 billion, and local government councils received N264.805 billion.

According to the figures, state and local government councils received larger shares of distributable VAT revenue, while the Federal Government got a smaller share.

The communiqué also showed that gross statutory revenue rose in September, while VAT revenue declined during the period.

It equally emerged that gross statutory revenue stood at N3.096 trillion in September, up from N2.850 trillion in August, the N246.384 billion rise reflecting higher revenue available from statutory sources.

Overall, FAAC attributed the changes in revenue performance to increases in some tax and petroleum-related revenue sources, alongside declines in others.

Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax, petroleum royalties, import duty, Common External Tariff (CET) levies and excise duty recorded significant increases in September.

But Companies Income Tax (CIT), Capital Gains Tax (CGT), Stamp Duties Tax (SDT), VAT, mineral royalties, gas-flaring penalties, rental gas-flaring fees and miscellaneous oil revenue declined during the period.

World.title: Arewa Group Lauds Tinubu’s Effort to Guarantee Food Security, Sustainable Economic Growth
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

A northern political pressure group, the Arewa Revival Project (ARP), has applauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration for its commitment to food security, climate resilience, rural development and sustainable economic growth in Northern Nigeria.

The group highlighted ecological interventions under the Kano River Irrigation Scheme, particularly the rehabilitation and expansion of Tiga Dam, Challawa Gorge Dam and Kafin Chiri Dam in Kano State, as initiatives aimed at boosting food production and improving the livelihoods of commercial farmers.

Declaring support for President Tinubu’s re-election bid, ARP Project Coordinator, Hon. Muttaka Ahmed Ibrahim, said the interventions were being implemented by the Ecological Project Office under the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

“We recognise these projects as practical investments in Kano State’s agricultural potential, with far-reaching benefits for farmers, rural households, agribusinesses and the national economy,” he said.

Ibrahim noted that Tiga Dam, completed in 1974, has a reservoir capacity of approximately 1.97 billion cubic metres, an irrigation potential of about 230,000 hectares and the capacity to support 10 megawatts of hydropower generation.

He explained that the ongoing intervention would open additional irrigation sectors in Yakasai, Gwamma and Gurjiya, covering approximately 875 hectares, through the development of irrigation canals and associated infrastructure.

At Challawa Gorge Dam, the project aims to develop 240 hectares of irrigable land through the construction and rehabilitation of canals, access roads and other hydraulic structures.

Meanwhile, the intervention at Kafin Chiri Dam is expected to open additional irrigation sectors covering approximately 164.91 hectares across Kunpada, Matanfa and Maida.

According to Ibrahim, the projects represent important investments in ecological infrastructure that could improve water management, agricultural productivity and rural livelihoods.

He added that improved irrigation would support year-round farming, increase agricultural output, create jobs and strengthen communities’ resilience to climate-related challenges.

The ARP coordinator also noted that the initiatives aligned with the Renewed Hope Agenda’s objectives of enhancing food security, diversifying the economy, reducing poverty and promoting inclusive development.

He emphasised that strengthening Kano State’s irrigation infrastructure would unlock farmers’ productive capacity, attract private investment in agribusiness and improve food supply chains.

In conclusion, Ibrahim reaffirmed the group’s support for President Tinubu’s re-election bid, expressing confidence that continuity in leadership would help consolidate ongoing projects, expand development initiatives and sustain efforts towards national economic transformation.

World.title: Andile Mpisane claps back with ‘AI-statement’
World.content:
Andile Mpisane claps back at claims he is a 'deadbeat dad'. Images via IG

Andile Mpisane has responded to a claim, reportedly by his ex, Sithelo Shozi, accusing him of neglecting his children.

The Royal AM soccer boss and amapiano artists has two daughters, Florence and Coco, with the influencer, and another two, Miaandy and Messiah Shauwn with his wife, Tamia.

In recent months, Tamia has dropped her marital surname, fuelling rumours that the couple have separated.



ANDILE MPISANE RESPONDS TO ‘DEADBEAT DAD’ CLAIMS

On his Instagram, Andile Mpisane denied allegations that he had neglected his children.

The “AI-generated” statement read: “My responsibilities and commitment as a father should not be judged on the basis of speculation, assumptions or one-sided narratives. I have continued to contribute towards my children’s education, including paying their school fees, and I remain committed to their well-being and future.

Andile claimed that his access to his children had been “limited” and that he had recently “reconnected” with them.

He continued: “My decision to remain silent about private family matters should never be mistaken for a lack of responsibility, love or commitment. I will not allow assumptions or speculation to define my role as a father or undermine the efforts I have continued to make for my children.

“My focus remains firmly on rebuilding and maintaining a meaningful relationship with my children, supporting their education, and ensuring their emotional, physical and overall well-being remain a priority”

Andile Mpisane – the son of businesswoman Shauwn Mkhize, or “MaMkhize” – did not specify which of his ex’s children he was referring to.

However, in the comments section, followers suggested his statement was in response to Sithelo Shozi’s TikTok claims that he had not seen their children in “six years and counting”.

Without naming him, Sithelo claimed that Andile was an “absolute deadbeat”.
