World.title: Brazil Judge Bars Flávio Bolsonaro Ad Boost
World.content:
BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Key Facts — What is happening On Wednesday, 14 October, Judge André Mendonça of Brazil’s electoral court barred Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign from paying to promote a video attacking President Lula, and gave Meta three hours to cut off the promotion.

— Why it matters The order lands 11 days before the 25 October runoff and shows Brazilian judges policing paid political speech on US platforms, with Meta’s Instagram and Facebook told to enforce it within hours.

— The numbers The paid promotion had to end within three hours, the video has run since 11 October, and a first-round fine for a piece with the same caption was 5,000 reais (about US$990).

— Who is who Mendonça sits on Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court and its electoral court, Flávio Bolsonaro is the conservative Liberal Party senator facing Lula, and Brasil Pronto Pra Mais is the coalition of Lula and running mate Geraldo Alckmin.

— What to watch The full electoral court must still review the order and no date is public, while the next test is the runoff on Sunday, 25 October, and the campaign’s reaction is not yet confirmed.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.6% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (15 October, 11:50 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 23% and 23% ), as of 15 October, 2:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you For US investors and readers following the runoff, the ruling signals a heavily litigated final stretch in which American platforms such as Meta must act on Brazilian court orders within hours.

A Brazilian electoral judge has ordered Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign to stop paying to push a video attacking President Lula. Meta, the US company behind Instagram and Facebook, was given three hours to comply.

Judge André Mendonça of Brazil’s electoral court barred Flávio Bolsonaro from paying to promote a video attacking Lula on Wednesday, 14 October. He gave Meta, the US company behind Instagram and Facebook, three hours to stop the paid promotion, 11 days before the runoff.

Correio Braziliense and Estadão Conteúdo reported that Brasil Pronto Pra Mais, Lula’s coalition with running mate Geraldo Alckmin, made the request. The video can stay online, but the campaign cannot pay to spread it.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Court Ordered Flávio Bolsonaro to Stop

The video began running on 11 October, Estadão Conteúdo said. Its caption, translated from Portuguese, says Lula “abandoned Brazil” and promises to “rescue the country”.

Mendonça said the irregularity lies in the paid boosting, Estadão Conteúdo reported. Paid boosting pushes a post to people who would not otherwise see it, which rules bar for attacks on an opponent.

He ordered the paid promotion of the video and its caption to end within three hours. He also barred any new paid ad with an identical caption, on any boost or provider, Terra and O Liberal reported.

The order reaches Meta, which has the same three hours to remove the boost from Instagram and Facebook. The video itself may remain online organically, meaning without payment to widen its reach.

The decision is that of a single judge, who sits on Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court as well as the electoral court. It has been submitted to the full electoral court, Terra and Correio Braziliense reported.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Repeat of a First-Round Case

Estadão Conteúdo said a piece with the same caption was boosted irregularly during the first round. The campaign was fined 5,000 reais (about US$990) for paid negative propaganda.

Mendonça issued that fine on Monday, 5 October, Agência Brasil reported. Conversions in this article use the central bank’s reference rate for 14 October, 5.0441 reais per US$1.

He followed the electoral prosecutor-general’s office, which said the message used rejection of the rival to promote Flávio’s own candidacy. The defence, the agency said, argued the post was a mere political judgment, with criticism of Lula a small part of it.

A Crítica and Jornal do Brasil reported that on Sunday, 11 October, Mendonça applied the same rule to Lula’s side. He barred Lula’s campaign from new paid promotion of ads saying Flávio opposes ending the six-day 6×1 work week.

What Brazilian Law Says About Paid Boosting

Article 57-C of Law 9,504 of 1997 bans paid online campaign propaganda except boosting by parties, coalitions and candidates. It allows boosting only to promote or benefit candidates or their parties.

Irregular boosting draws a fine of 5,000 to 30,000 reais (about US$990 to US$5,950), or twice the sum spent if larger. The first-round fine of 5,000 reais equals the legal minimum.

What It Means for US Readers

Meta, a US company, must enforce the order on Instagram and Facebook in a runoff that US investors watch closely. Brazilian judges can order American platforms to switch off paid political promotion within hours.

Paid attack ads are routine in US campaigns, so Brazil’s line between promoting a candidate and attacking a rival may look unfamiliar. The line applies to paid boosting only, because the video can stay online without payment.

Brazil votes on Sunday, 25 October, when Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro, the conservative senator and son of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro. That makes the court’s handling of campaign advertising a live issue for the final 11 days.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket’s winner market, with about US$182.9 million in bets, gave Flávio Bolsonaro 77.6% and Lula 22.5%. The prices were taken on 15 October at 11:50 a.m. ET and are bets, not polls.

Polymarket’s second-round margin market, with about US$1.3 million in bets, put a Flávio win by under four points at 40.5%. A Flávio win by four to eight points stood at 32.5%.

Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 77.1% · Lula 22.5% (US$184 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 78% · Lula 23% As of 15 October, 2:40 pm ET (19:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The decision text could not be opened, and the court’s news page carries no item on it. The details above come from Correio Braziliense, Estadão Conteúdo (carried by Terra and O Liberal), A Crítica and Gazeta do Paraná.

Whether Meta and the campaign complied within three hours has not been reported, and no campaign statement appears in the coverage found. The amount spent on the boost, the video’s reach and the date of the full court’s review are also unknown.

Reports differ on the first-round piece: Agência Brasil called it a photo, A Crítica and Times Brasil a video. Correio Braziliense says the first-round caption was identical.

What Comes Next

The full court is due to review the single-judge order, but no date has been published. The court’s agenda for Thursday, 15 October, names three cases and none is this order.

Readers can follow the court’s other rulings on campaign posts in Brazil Court Clears Vorcaro Ads 12 Days Out. The runoff takes place on Sunday, 25 October.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the judge decide about Flávio Bolsonaro?

Judge André Mendonça barred paid promotion of a video attacking Lula and gave Meta three hours to comply. The video may stay online without payment.

Is the Flávio Bolsonaro video banned?

No, it may stay online and spread organically. The campaign may not pay to widen its reach, and may not buy new paid ads with the same caption.

Why is paid boosting of attacks restricted in Brazil?

Brazil’s election law allows paid boosting only to promote or benefit candidates or their parties. Mendonça read that as barring paid promotion of messages against an opponent.

Who asked for the ruling?

Brasil Pronto Pra Mais, the coalition that brings together Lula and running mate Geraldo Alckmin, asked for it. Estadão Conteúdo and Correio Braziliense reported the request.

What was the earlier fine?

In the first round the campaign was fined 5,000 reais (about US$990) for a piece with the same caption. That equals the minimum fine in Brazil’s election law.

World.title: Cuba Inflation Rises to 28.44% in September
World.content:
CUBA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Cuba’s official price index for September, published on Wednesday, 14 October, shows prices up 3.37% in the month and 28.44% in a year, while the average state wage remains under US$10 a month.

— Why it matters Food accounts for nearly three quarters of the monthly rise, and Havana blames US pressure on fuel supplies for the shortages, though the data do not show how much of the rise that explains.

— The numbers Prices rose 3.37% in September and 24.85% from January to September, and the average state wage of 7,354 pesos is about US$9.25 a month at the informal rate of 795 pesos per US$.

— Who is who ONEI, the Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información, is Cuba’s official statistics office, and the Banco Central de Cuba is the central bank, whose official rates differ from the informal market rate.

— What to watch The informal rate stood at about 795 pesos per US$ on Wednesday, and ONEI’s October price index, expected in November, will show whether prices keep climbing.

— Power Index Cuba ranks 14th of 14 in Cuba ranks 14th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 22.5 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you A US$100 gift to a relative is worth about 79,500 pesos at the informal rate, nearly 11 months of the average state wage, while US agencies set the rules for travel and transfers to Cuba.

Cuba inflation reached 28.44% in September, official figures show. The average state wage of 7,354 pesos (about US$9.25 at the informal rate) is below US$10 a month.

Cuba inflation rose to 28.44% in the year to September, up from 25.19% in August, the statistics office ONEI said. Prices climbed 3.37% in September alone and 24.85% since January.

The data matter to US readers because Washington’s pressure on Cuba’s fuel supplies is part of the debate over the island’s slump. A US$100 gift to a relative converts to about 79,500 pesos at the informal rate, nearly 11 times the average state wage.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Cuba ranks 14th of 14 with 22.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (53); weakest: economic weight (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Cuba; see the index notes. WatchNo sovereign rating; economy contracting (-3.8%); incomplete data (‡). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Cuba Inflation Data Show

The Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información (ONEI), Cuba’s official statistics office, published the September consumer price index on Wednesday, 14 October. Diario de Cuba, OnCuba and 14ymedio all give the same monthly, cumulative and annual rates.

Annual inflation of 28.44% compares with 25.19% in August, when prices rose 4.92% in the month. September’s monthly rise of 3.37% was smaller, but the annual rate still climbed 3.25 percentage points.

Food and non-alcoholic drinks made up 73.39% of the monthly increase, Diario de Cuba and OnCuba reported from the ONEI data. Powdered soft drinks rose 17.73% in the month, sausages and hot dogs 11.72% and pork 10.69%.

Over twelve months, food and non-alcoholic drinks cost 42.66% more, restaurants and hotels 39.11% more and transport 24.80% more. Pork, eggs and ham pushed the monthly food increase most, Diario de Cuba and OnCuba said.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Cuba economy Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Average State Wage Buys

ONEI’s state sector report, released on Tuesday, 13 October, puts the average monthly wage at 7,354 pesos (about US$9.25). EFE, the Spanish news agency, says in a dispatch relayed by OnCuba that this is 6.12% above ONEI’s figure published in April.

Construction pays the most, at 14,743 pesos (about US$18.54) a month, Diario de Cuba, EFE and 14ymedio all say. Other community, association and personal services pay 5,795 pesos (about US$7.29), Diario de Cuba and EFE say.

14ymedio called the 6.12% rise small beside annual inflation of about 25%. The Rio Times explainer on Cuba’s minimum wage shows how the gap looks at the lowest pay level.

Which Exchange Rate This Article Uses

Pesos are converted at the informal rate of 795 per US$, as shown by El Toque and CiberCuba on 14 October. Both are Cuban news sites that track informal market quotes.

The central bank’s official rates differ from the informal one, and its rate table could not be opened for this article. The under-US$10 wage therefore holds at the informal rate used here, and no official conversion is given.

OnCuba, citing EFE, says informal and private markets are now the main source of supplies for millions of Cubans. That is why the informal rate, not the official one, is used here, as Diario de Cuba and EFE also do.

Why Real Inflation May Be Higher

The index covers the formal market, while a growing share of household buying happens in private and informal markets, OnCuba wrote. Prices there tend to be higher and more volatile, and Cuban economist Pedro Monreal says official statistics may understate the true rise.

14ymedio notes that ONEI’s method dates from 2010, which it says distorts the telecommunications part of the index. Alternative estimates, such as the Hanke Inflation Dashboard of US economist Steve Hanke, put price growth in July substantially higher, OnCuba wrote.

What It Means for US Readers

OnCuba, citing EFE, says the September price rise coincides with tighter US limits on fuel supplies to the island. It quotes Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy saying no Cuban state company has secured a fuel contract.

In OnCuba’s account, Washington says the measures aim to limit the Cuban government’s resources and force economic opening and political change. Havana calls the policy economic strangulation and blames it for the fuel shortages.

Anyone sending money to relatives should note that the informal market rate is about 795 pesos per US$, unlike official rates. Rules for travel and transfers to Cuba are set by US agencies, so check current guidance before sending money.

What Is Not Known

ONEI’s own website could not be opened for this article, so the figures rest on three outlets that agree with one another. The central bank’s site could not be opened either, so no official rate is used.

It is unclear whether 7,354 pesos (about US$9.25) is the August wage or the January to August average. EFE and Diario de Cuba say August, while 14ymedio says January to August.

The outlets also differ on which sectors pay least, with Diario de Cuba naming sugar and EFE naming education and community services. No forecast for the September figure was found, and the official index does not fully capture informal markets.

These data do not show how much of the rise comes from US fuel limits and how much from domestic shortages. No official comment from Havana on the September figures was found.

What Comes Next

ONEI has published its monthly index mid-month lately, with August’s released on 15 September and September’s on 14 October. The October figure should follow in November, though no date was found, and wage data come less often.

The informal dollar is the daily signal, at about 795 pesos per US$ on Wednesday after about 750 in late September. A further rise would cut the dollar value of the average wage again.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Cuba’s inflation rate?

Annual inflation was 28.44% in September, up from 25.19% in August, according to the statistics office ONEI. Prices rose 3.37% in the month and 24.85% from January.

What is the average wage in Cuba in US dollars?

ONEI’s state sector report puts the average monthly wage at 7,354 pesos, about US$9.25 at the informal rate of 795 per US$. Official central bank rates differ from the informal one, so the dollar figure depends on the rate used.

Why do Cuban wages convert to different dollar amounts?

Cuba has official central bank rates and an informal market rate of about 795 pesos per US$, and the two differ. The outlets reviewed use the informal rate because informal and private markets are now the main source of supplies.

What is pushing Cuban prices up?

Food made up 73.39% of the monthly rise, with pork, eggs and ham among the biggest contributors. OnCuba, citing EFE, says the rise coincides with tighter US limits on fuel supplies.

Is Cuba’s official inflation figure reliable?

Cuban economist Pedro Monreal says it may understate the true rise because it covers mainly the formal market. ONEI’s figures are the official benchmark, and three outlets that cite them agree on the numbers.

World.title: Mexico Deputies Pass US$576B Revenue Law
World.content:
MEXICO · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies backed the 2027 revenue law in the general vote on Wednesday, 14 October, by 331 votes to 118, and passed the reserved articles early on Thursday, 15 October, by 340 to 109.

— Why it matters The law sets what the Mexican government may raise and borrow in 2027, including dollar debt and borrowing limits for Pemex and CFE, and public debt is expected to reach 55% of GDP.

— The numbers Revenue is set at MXN 10.64 trillion (US$576 billion), of which taxes are MXN 6.26 trillion (US$339 billion); net domestic borrowing is capped at MXN 1.7 trillion (US$92 billion) and net foreign borrowing at US$13.5 billion.

— Who is who The Chamber of Deputies is the 500-seat lower house, where Morena, President Claudia Sheinbaum’s party, and its allies hold a majority; Ricardo Monreal leads Morena’s deputies, and Edgar Amador Zamora is finance secretary.

— What to watch The Senate must approve the law by 31 October and can still change it, including the tax-debt relief for firms of any size that deputies added during the final vote.

— Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US bond investors get the borrowing limits for 2027, up to US$13.5 billion abroad for the government and US$5.26 billion for Pemex, plus a 10% tax rate on gains from new Mexican share offerings.

Mexico’s lower house approved a 2027 revenue law worth about US$576 billion, with net domestic borrowing capped near US$92 billion. The bill now goes to the Senate, which must vote by 31 October.

Mexico’s lower house passed the 2027 revenue law early on Thursday, 15 October, setting income at MXN 10.64 trillion (about US$576 billion). It also caps net domestic borrowing at MXN 1.7 trillion (about US$92 billion) and net foreign borrowing at US$13.5 billion.

The vote on the reserved articles was 340 to 109, after a 331 to 118 general vote on Wednesday. US investors care because the law sets the foreign borrowing limit and debt limits for state firms Pemex and CFE.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Revenue Law Sets for 2027

Taxes bring MXN 6.26 trillion (about US$339 billion), or 59% of the total. Income tax is the largest line at MXN 3.29 trillion (about US$178 billion), ahead of value-added tax.

The total also counts MXN 1.48 trillion (about US$80 billion) of financing, the line that includes new borrowing. Article 2 separately caps net domestic borrowing at MXN 1.7 trillion (about US$92 billion).

The plan behind the law assumes 1.5% to 2.5% growth in 2027 and 17.9 pesos per US dollar on average. It also assumes Mexican export crude at US$61.8 a barrel.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Debt Ceilings for the Treasury, Pemex and CFE

The treasury may add net debt of up to MXN 1.7 trillion (about US$92 billion) at home and US$13.5 billion abroad. Either limit can rise if the other falls by the same amount.

Pemex, the state oil firm, can borrow up to MXN 160.6 billion (about US$8.7 billion) net at home and US$5.26 billion abroad. CFE, the state electricity utility, can borrow up to MXN 16.7 billion (about US$907 million) net at home and US$725 million abroad.

Hacienda, the finance ministry, expects public debt to reach 55% of GDP in 2027, Expansión and La Crónica de Hoy reported. The law belongs to the 2027 economic package that the ministry delivered to Congress on 8 September.

How Deputies Voted on the Revenue Law

In the general vote on Wednesday, 14 October, deputies backed the bill 331 to 118, La Razón and Aristegui Noticias reported. The Chamber’s own vote record, which dates the session 13 October, lists the same count.

Morena, President Claudia Sheinbaum’s party, voted yes with its allies, the Labour Party (PT) and the Green Party (PVEM). The conservative National Action Party (PAN), the once-dominant Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and the centrist Citizens’ Movement (MC) mostly voted no.

The final vote on the reserved articles came early on Thursday, 15 October, at 340 to 109, La Jornada reported. The Chamber’s vote record lists the same count, with two MC deputies among the yes votes.

Finance Committee chair Carol Antonio Altamirano said on Tuesday the law adds no new taxes or higher general rates, Excélsior reported. He said revenue should grow through stricter compliance and a crackdown on evasion.

In committee, Federico Döring of the PAN said the government has borrowed more than any before it, La Crónica de Hoy reported. Jericó Abramo Masso of the PRI said the borrowing would fund current spending rather than public works.

Deputies Add Tax-Debt Relief for Firms of Any Size

Only one proposed change passed: Ricardo Monreal’s, who leads Morena’s deputies, the Chamber’s vote record and La Jornada show. It lifts the MXN 300 million (about US$16.3 million) income cap on a scheme waiving fines and surcharges on overdue taxes.

Companies of any size could have fines, surcharges and enforcement costs waived if they pay the inflation-adjusted tax owed, El Financiero reported. Monreal said the main tax is not forgiven and linked the measure to a commitment President Sheinbaum made to business leaders.

Monreal said the capped version collected MXN 6.44 billion (about US$349 million) from about 38,000 taxpayers, El Financiero and MVS Noticias reported. The PAN called it unconstitutional, and Monreal denied it is a pardon.

What It Means for US Readers

The US$13.5 billion foreign borrowing ceiling and Pemex’s US$5.26 billion limit matter most to dollar bondholders. They are ceilings, not issuance plans, and Hacienda decides how much to borrow during the year.

The budget assumes 17.9 pesos per dollar on average in 2027, against 18.46 on the open market on 15 October. A weaker peso raises the peso cost of dollar debt, so the exchange rate bears watching.

The law also sets a 10% rate on 2027 gains from selling shares in Mexican initial public offerings. Foreign investors can qualify in full for firms valued up to MXN 50 billion (about US$2.7 billion), and in part above that.

Mexican units of US groups with firm tax assessments could use the fine waiver if the Senate keeps it. A separate income tax reform for large firms is covered in Mexico Tax Reform on Big Firms Clears House.

What Is Not Known

It is not known when the Senate will vote, though Article 42 of the federal budget law gives it until 31 October. Senators can amend the text, which would send it back to deputies.

No official estimate of what the expanded tax-debt relief will collect or forgo was available on Thursday. Monreal said about 30 million taxpayers could benefit, but MVS Noticias reported he did not explain the figure when asked.

A borrowing ceiling is not a forecast of how much Mexico will borrow. The spending bill, which sets what the government will spend, must still pass the lower house by 15 November.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Mexico’s lower house approve?

It approved the 2027 revenue law, which sets federal income at MXN 10.64 trillion (about US$576 billion). The general vote on 14 October was 331 to 118, and the reserved articles passed 340 to 109 early on 15 October.

How much can Mexico borrow under the law?

Net domestic borrowing is capped at MXN 1.7 trillion (about US$92 billion) and net foreign borrowing at US$13.5 billion. Pemex and CFE have separate limits, set in Article 4.

Is the revenue law final?

No, the Senate must still approve it, and the budget law gives it until 31 October. After approval it must be published in the official gazette within 20 calendar days.

What is the tax-debt relief deputies added?

It waives fines, surcharges and enforcement costs on overdue federal taxes for firms and people who pay the inflation-adjusted tax owed. Deputies removed the MXN 300 million (about US$16.3 million) income cap that limited it.

Does the law raise taxes?

Committee chair Carol Antonio Altamirano said it adds no new taxes and no higher general rates. Taxes are still expected to bring MXN 6.26 trillion (about US$339 billion), or 59% of the total.

World.title: Peru’s Lima Jobless Rate Falls to 4.4%
World.content:
PERU · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening On Thursday, 15 October, Peru published the capital’s July to September jobs data: employment in Lima rose 6.0% (339,300 jobs) to 6,013,300, and unemployment fell to 4.4% from 5.7% a year earlier.

— Why it matters Jobs are growing quickly but pay is not: Lima consumer prices rose 4.55% in the 12 months to September, so average pay up only 0.4% buys less than it did a year ago.

— The numbers Average monthly pay from the main job is S/ 2,302 (about US$669), up 0.4%; services added 285,400 jobs (up 9.3%) while manufacturing lost 43,500 (down 5.2%); the US jobless rate for September was 4.2%.

— Who is who INEI is Peru’s national statistics institute, led by Gaspar Morán Flores, which runs the household employment survey; Elmer Cuba is the economy minister, who has said the government will act to stop the economy cooling.

— What to watch The August to October reading should follow in mid-November, and the economy minister is preparing a countercyclical plan to keep investment and jobs growing, with no date or figures confirmed.

— Power Index Peru ranks 5th of 14 in Peru ranks 5th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 54.7 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you Lima’s 4.4% jobless rate is close to the US rate of 4.2%, but pay is flat against 4.55% inflation, and manufacturing jobs fell while Peru’s clothing exporters face 12.5% extra US duties.

The Lima jobless rate fell to 4.4% in the July to September quarter, from 5.7% a year earlier, as employment rose 6.0%. Average pay from the main job rose only 0.4% to S/ 2,302 (about US$669) a month.

Peru’s statistics institute INEI said on Thursday, 15 October, that the Lima jobless rate fell to 4.4% in July to September. Employment in the capital rose 6.0% from a year earlier, to 6,013,300 people.

For US readers, the survey is a gauge of consumers in a country that ships clothing and fruit to the US. It shows pay up only 0.4% while Lima consumer prices rose 4.55%.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Lima Jobless Rate Shows

INEI counted 6,013,300 employed people in Lima Metropolitana, the capital’s urban area, in the July to September quarter. That is 339,300 more than a year earlier, a rise of 6.0%.

The unemployment rate was 4.4%, down 1.3 percentage points from 5.7% in the same quarter of 2025. INEI estimates that 274,900 people were actively looking for work.

INEI put the rate at 4.8% for June to August in its 15 September release, so the latest reading is lower. INEI said in its 15 August release that 4.7% for May to July was the lowest in the survey’s history.

The figures come from the national household employment survey, known as EPEN, and cover rolling three month periods. Each new reading drops the oldest month and adds the newest, so neighbouring readings share two months.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Peru economy Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Gained the Jobs

Women gained most, with employment up 7.4% (190,300 jobs), against 4.8% (149,100 jobs) for men. Women now hold 46.0% of Lima’s jobs, or 2,763,500 positions.

Workers aged 45 and older drove the increase, with 261,800 more jobs, up 11.5%. Employment among 14 to 24 year olds fell 1.6%, a loss of 10,300 jobs.

Services added 285,400 jobs, up 9.3%, while commerce rose 6.3% and construction 6.2%. Manufacturing lost 43,500 jobs, a fall of 5.2%.

Firms with 51 or more workers added 178,700 jobs, up 11.0%, and firms with up to 10 workers added 187,800, up 5.7%. Employment fell 3.6%, or 27,000 jobs, at firms with 11 to 50 workers.

Pay Barely Moved While Prices Rose

Average monthly income from the main job in Lima was S/ 2,302.0 (about US$669), up 0.4% from a year earlier. Conversions in this article use S/ 3.44 per US$, which matches the central bank’s interbank selling rate of 13 October.

Men earned S/ 2,593.8 (about US$754) and women S/ 1,954.1 (about US$568), up 0.5% and 0.7%. Income rose 7.5% (S/ 97.9, about US$28) for 14 to 24 year olds.

Income fell 5.1% (S/ 126.3, about US$37) for workers aged 45 and over. It fell 3.5% (S/ 124.7, about US$36) for workers with a university education, while those with primary education or less gained 6.8%.

In the June to August reading INEI had average income at S/ 2,308.4 (about US$671), up 2.6%. Lima consumer prices rose 4.55% in the 12 months to September, INEI said on 1 October.

Pay up 0.4% against prices up 4.55% implies roughly 4% less buying power, a Rio Times calculation. It is not an INEI estimate and mixes a quarterly pay average with a 12 month price change.

Formal Hiring and the Minimum Wage

Peru’s labour ministry said on 5 October, citing central bank data, that formal employment grew 4.4% in July, or 268,000 jobs. Formal private sector jobs rose 6.1%, led by services, farming and commerce.

The minimum wage rose from S/ 1,130 (about US$328) to S/ 1,230 (about US$358) on 1 October, after the survey period ended. The ministry said a second step of S/ 70 (about US$20) is due in the first half of 2027.

Economy Minister Elmer Cuba said on 14 October that the government will act to stop the economy cooling. He cited El Niño, higher fuel prices and higher global rates, and said on 7 October that fiscal policy must be expansive.

What It Means for US Readers

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics put the US jobless rate at 4.2% for September, close to Lima’s 4.4%. The surveys differ in method and geography, so the comparison is only a rough yardstick.

For investors the signal is mixed: more people in work supports spending, but flat pay against 4.55% inflation could limit it. US firms selling to or hiring in Lima face a minimum wage that rose 8.8% on 1 October.

The US Trade Representative, Washington’s trade office, set a 12.5% duty on most Peruvian goods, applied since 24 July. ADEX, the exporters’ association, says the US took 64.2% of Peru’s clothing exports from January to August, as earlier coverage showed.

INEI’s 5.2% fall in Lima manufacturing jobs is separate data, and INEI does not link it to the duties. Clothing is one part of manufacturing, so the two should not be read as cause and effect.

What Is Not Known

INEI’s release does not say why manufacturing jobs fell 5.2% or whether US duties played any part. It does not say whether 4.4% is a record, but INEI called the earlier 4.7% the survey’s lowest in August.

The release covers Lima only, so it gives no national unemployment rate for July to September. INEI’s press release also leaves out informality and underemployment, so the quality of the new jobs is not yet clear.

The estimate of roughly 4% less buying power is approximate. It compares a quarterly pay average with a 12 month inflation rate that ends in September.

What Comes Next

INEI has published this survey monthly, so the August to October reading should follow in mid-November, though the date is not confirmed. Cuba’s countercyclical plan is the next policy test, but no date or figures have been confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Lima’s jobless rate?

INEI put it at 4.4% for July to September 2026, down from 5.7% a year earlier. About 274,900 people were actively looking for work.

How many people work in Lima?

INEI counted 6,013,300 employed people in Lima Metropolitana, up 6.0% or 339,300 from a year earlier. Women hold 46.0% of those jobs.

Did pay rise in Lima?

Average monthly income from the main job rose only 0.4% to S/ 2,302.0 (about US$669). Lima consumer prices rose 4.55% in the 12 months to September.

Which jobs fell in Lima?

Manufacturing employment fell 5.2%, or 43,500 jobs, and jobs for 14 to 24 year olds fell 1.6%. Employment also fell 3.6% at firms with 11 to 50 workers.

Does this cover all of Peru?

No, it covers Lima Metropolitana only and comes from the national household employment survey, known as EPEN. INEI publishes the Lima reading as a rolling three month average.

How does Lima compare with the US?

The US unemployment rate was 4.2% in September, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics published on 2 October. The surveys differ, so the comparison is only a rough guide.

World.title: Brazil Arrests Guarulhos Shootout Suspect
World.content:
BRAZIL · SECURITY

Key Facts — What is happening On Wednesday, 14 October, security forces arrested a man in Governador Mangabeira, Bahia, who is suspected of shooting at Federal Police agents at Guarulhos airport near São Paulo on 31 July.

— Why it matters Guarulhos is Brazil’s main international gateway, and the July clash began when an armed group allegedly tried to load cocaine onto a plane bound for Europe from a restricted area.

— The numbers The man had 2 outstanding arrest warrants; about 10 suspects in 4 vehicles took part in the July clash, which injured no one, and agents recovered about 400 kilograms (880 pounds) of cocaine.

— Who is who FICCO-BA is the Bahia unit of the task forces against organised crime that the Federal Police coordinates, led there by delegate Eduardo Badaró; GISE/SP is the Federal Police’s São Paulo investigations unit.

— What to watch The suspect’s name, his charges and the court holding his warrants are not public, and the investigation into everyone involved in the July clash continues.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you No one was injured in the July clash, and Brazil carries a Level 2 US travel advisory, exercise increased caution, so travellers should keep the usual care in transport hubs.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 76.8% · Lula 23.5% (US$184 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 78% · Lula 23% As of 15 October, 2:20 pm ET (19:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Federal and Bahia forces arrested a man on Wednesday over the 31 July gunfire at Guarulhos airport. Officials have not named him or said what charges he faces.

A Guarulhos shootout suspect was arrested in Bahia on Wednesday, 14 October, after a July clash with Federal Police. He was caught in Governador Mangabeira, in Bahia’s Recôncavo region, 75 days after the 31 July clash at the airport.

Guarulhos is São Paulo’s main international airport, so the case matters to US travellers who fly to Brazil. Bahia’s security secretariat, SSP-BA, announced the arrest, and BNews, Acorda Cidade and Aratu On carried it that evening.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Happened in Bahia on 14 October

The arrest came on Wednesday afternoon, the SSP-BA statement says. The man tried to flee in a Chevrolet Montana pickup, but officers surrounded the vehicle and detained him.

The SSP-BA statement says he had two outstanding arrest warrants. It does not say which court issued them or for what offences.

Three units took part, the SSP-BA statement says. They were the Federal Police’s São Paulo Sensitive Investigations Group (GISE/SP), FICCO-BA and the 27th Independent Company of the state Military Police.

FICCOs are task forces against organised crime, coordinated by the Federal Police, Brazil’s national investigative agency, with state agencies in every state. FICCO-BA is the unit for Bahia.

Eduardo Badaró, the federal police delegate who coordinates FICCO-BA, said the suspect “chose the wrong state to try to hide”. The words are translated from Portuguese, and he stressed the value of shared intelligence, the SSP-BA statement said.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Known About the Guarulhos Shootout Suspect

Neither the SSP-BA statement nor the outlets name the man. The statement describes him as an alleged faction member but does not say which faction, so that detail remains unconfirmed.

He is suspected of shooting at federal forces at the airport, but no report describes his alleged role in the clash. Nor do they say whether his two warrants relate to that case.

The 31 July Clash at Guarulhos Airport

On Friday, 31 July, at about 2:30 p.m., agents detected unusual movement in a restricted area of Guarulhos airport. About ten people in four vehicles had cut a hole in the perimeter fence, Metrópoles reported, citing the Federal Police.

The Federal Police said the group was trying to load cocaine onto an aircraft bound for Europe. Agents and suspects exchanged gunfire, and no one was injured, Metrópoles and BNews São Paulo reported.

Agents recovered about 400 kilograms (880 pounds) of cocaine: five bags already on the aircraft and four abandoned boxes. The suspects fled into woodland near the airport, leaving phones for forensic analysis, Metrópoles and O Antagonista reported.

At least two people had been arrested by 2 August, Metrópoles and Diário do Grande ABC reported. Accounts of the exact number differ, and the Federal Police said it would keep working to identify and locate everyone involved.

Why Guarulhos Matters Beyond Brazil

Guarulhos handled 47.2 million passengers in 2025, its operator GRU Airport said, Gazeta de São Paulo and Aviacional Dia reported. Gazeta de São Paulo calls it the main arrival and departure point for Brazil’s international flights.

The Federal Police seized almost 4,000 kilograms (about 8,800 pounds) of drugs at Guarulhos in 2025, SBT News and Metrópoles reported. Cocaine was 46% of the total, mainly bound for Europe, and 820 people were arrested at the airport that year.

What It Means for US Readers

Guarulhos is Brazil’s main international gateway, so the case is relevant to Americans flying to São Paulo. Reports of the July clash mention no injuries, and the group was after a drug shipment bound for Europe.

The US State Department rates Brazil Level 2, exercise increased caution, and advises care at major transportation centres, especially at night. The advisory was last issued on 31 August 2026, after the July clash, and does not mention it.

The Brazilian website of American Airlines lists flights from Guarulhos to Miami, Dallas-Fort Worth, New York JFK and other US cities. The page is a fare listing and does not state how often the flights operate.

Americans planning a trip can check entry rules in The Rio Times guide to the Brazil e-visa for US citizens. Airline schedules change by season, so confirm flights with the carrier.

What Is Not Known

The suspect’s name, the court that issued his two warrants and any formal charges have not been made public. Officials have also not said what role he allegedly played in the July clash or which criminal faction he is linked to.

The SSP-BA statement is the only official account published so far, and no Federal Police release on the arrest could be found. The number of people arrested in July also varies between outlets, from one to three.

What Comes Next

No court date or transfer has been announced for the suspect. The Federal Police said in July that it would keep working to identify and locate everyone involved.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was arrested in Bahia on 14 October?

A man suspected of shooting at Federal Police agents at Guarulhos airport was arrested in Governador Mangabeira on Wednesday. Officials have not released his name.

What happened at Guarulhos airport on 31 July?

Federal Police say about ten people opened a gap in the fence and tried to load cocaine onto a plane for Europe. Agents and suspects exchanged gunfire, and no one was injured.

Was anyone hurt or were flights disrupted?

The reports on the July clash say no one was injured. They do not say whether any flights were affected.

What is FICCO?

FICCOs are task forces against organised crime that the Federal Police coordinates with state agencies. FICCO-BA is the unit in Bahia, coordinated by delegate Eduardo Badaró.

What does the State Department say about travel to Brazil?

It rates Brazil Level 2, exercise increased caution, in an advisory last issued on 31 August 2026. It advises care at major transportation centres, especially at night.

Where is Governador Mangabeira?

It is a town in the Recôncavo region of Bahia, in north-eastern Brazil. The arrest took place there on Wednesday afternoon.
