World.title: UK: Harry and Meghan make high-profile comeback six years after royal exit
World.content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex, made their first official joint public engagement since returning to the UK in August when they visited charities in Nottingham on Thursday, 15 October.

 

They were greeted with cheers, hugs and handshakes as they arrived at the Community Recording Studio, a youth charity in St Ann's that provides access to music, recording facilities and mentoring. There, they met young people, watched a drama workshop and listened to a recording session.

The couple applauded the performers, embraced a singer and spoke with well-wishers, while Meghan received several bouquets of flowers as they left.

The visit was the first of three planned stops in Nottingham, followed by Himmah Hub, a community organisation tackling food poverty, and Epic Partners, which supports young people through sport, education and mentoring.

The trip marks a significant public return for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, six years after stepping back from royal duties. Nottingham holds particular significance for the couple, as it was the setting for their first joint public engagement following their engagement announcement in 2017. Their visit to the Community Recording Studio highlighted its work using music, performance and sport to help young people develop confidence and practical skills, as the couple seek to rebuild their public profile in Britain.

World.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro pleads not guilty to torture charges
World.content:
Maduro and his wife were charged with leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims during his presidency from 2013 to 2026.

Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro appeared in court on Thursday, where he rejected newly unsealed torture charges against him and his wife, Cilia Flores.

He said the indictment represented "false accusations" against him.

Maduro was combative in court as he was asked to enter a plea to the charges, condemning allegations of torture as "false accusations and false testimony."

Ultimately, Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein interjected to declare that "a plea of not guilty will be entered on behalf of Mr. Maduro."

Flores told the judge through the Spanish interpreter: "I am completely innocent. I am not guilty."

The court appearance was the latest for the pair, who are currently in US custody in New York City, now eight months since they were seized from their Caracas home by the US military in a nighttime raid.

The new torture charges against the couple have been added to the drug-trafficking charges they previously faced.

Maduro and Flores' trial is set to begin June 14, 2027, according to a schedule approved by the judge Thursday.

What are the torture charges?

Maduro and his wife have been accused of leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans, during his presidency from 2013 to 2026.

They are said to have committed human rights violations as part of a scheme to hold on to power.

Security forces have been accused of torturing prisoners with electric shocks, beatings and asphyxiation at Maduro's behest.

Maduro stands accused of personally recommending torture methods, receiving updates on specific victims' treatment, and threatening to kill one prisoner's child as a form of psychological torture.

For her part, Cilia Flores has been accused of helping develop the repressive system and ordering the torture of some specific people, the indictment alleges.

Human rights groups have long accused Venezuelan officials of torturing detainees, but the US indictment marks the first time that Maduro could be held to account over the allegations.

Maudro has been under investigation by the International Criminal Court (ICC) over allegations of crimes against humanity, tied to his crackdown on opponents, but the court has not served him with a warrant.

Torture is considered a crime under international law and can be prosecuted outside of the nation where the abuse occurred and regardless of the victims' nationality.

But in the US, the prosecution of foreign officials is exceedingly rare. The only recent cases include the son of Liberian President Charles Taylor, Russians responsible for war crimes in Ukraine and a former prison warden in Bashar Assad's Syria.

World.title: Self-replicating AI: Is your fridge a cybersecurity risk?
World.content:
Anthropic researchers warn that AI worms could soon target connected household devices and spread from one device to another. Cyberattacks on French supermarkets illustrate just how vulnerable such systems can be.

In the living room, a robot vacuum cleaner moves back and forth, the lights are dimmed by voice assistants, the heating is controlled via smartphone and the TV connects to the internet to access a favorite streaming service. These are all examples of the "Internet of Things," in which connected electronic devices exchange data and communicate with one another.

According to recent market research by industry association Bitkom , about half of all households in Germany use such or similar "smart home" applications — and the figure is rising.

Now, the artificial intelligence company Anthropic has published a report warning that AI-powered malware could soon infiltrate connected household devices, copy itself to other devices and become active there.

52% of German households use devices like this robot vacuum cleaner Image: Jean-François Frey/PHOTOPQR/L'ALSACE/MAXPPP/picture alliance

Computer viruses that copy themselves from one machine to another have existed for decades. They are also known as worms and follow a predefined sequence of instructions. They exploit known security vulnerabilities or poorly protected access points. However, once the vulnerabilities are patched up or suitable attack vectors are no longer available, a worm can no longer spread so easily.

AI worms, however, would be far more complex and potentially much more harmful. They could solve problems autonomously and adapt to different devices, for example by coping with a different operating system or limited memory. They might also figure out for themselves how to operate on other devices or identify and circumvent new security updates

What is AI's biggest risk: Speed or autonomy? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Spreading via TVs

Anthropic researchers investigated whether AI models could also run on relatively inexpensive hardware. In an experiment, they distributed an AI model across 15 low-cost Android TV boxes, with each device handling part of the computation. This demonstrated that certain AI applications can run without a large data center.

In a controlled test environment, the researchers set up eight additional simulated Android devices. The AI model was able to infiltrate one of them, replicate itself and infect other devices. In four out of five attempts, it reached all eight target devices. In the remaining attempt, it reached seven of the eight.

If equipped with malware, such an AI model could potentially adapt relatively quickly to previously unknown environments and disrupt processes and operations. It could learn to circumvent various security measures rather than simply exploiting a single vulnerability. According to Anthropic's developers, this sort of "AI worm" could take roughly one to two days to establish itself on a new, previously unknown device.

A botnet of household devices?

One particularly worrying possibility is that AI could link the infected devices into a large botnet. A single infected device has limited computing power, but the more devices are compromised, the faster the AI worm could spread. The malware would no longer depend on a central server that could simply be shut down.

It might also continuously learn as it spreads. It is conceivable that it could jump to entirely different types of electronic devices, all running different software.

Infected devices could be disconnected from the network and security vulnerabilities could still be patched. The malware's decentralized structure, however, would make it difficult to contain. Anthropic itself compares this potential development to a digital slime mold slowly spreading.

Researchers at Anthropic deliberately made access to the test devices very easy and left out major digital safeguards. Even so, the company believes smaller AI models could reach the necessary level of capability later this year to spread in the real world.

Overheating cooling systems

The potential consequences of cyberattacks on connected control systems has already been seen in an incident in France. Overnight into Monday, attackers tampered with refrigeration and freezer systems at numerous supermarkets. Temperatures in the affected units rose to as high as 50 degrees Celsius. Food spoiled, and some incidents also involved fires and technical damage.

France's cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR , initially confirmed that remote-control systems made by Danish manufacturer Danfoss had been compromised. The warning was later extended to systems made by other manufacturers. Investigations into the circumstances of the attack are ongoing.

Many perishable foods had to be discarded after the massive cyberattack on supermarkets in France Image: Fred Tanneau/AFP

Modern supermarkets use digital controllers to monitor and regulate refrigeration systems. Maintenance companies can access these systems remotely, for example to check temperatures. However, some of the security software was reportedly outdated, which the attackers may have exploited as an entry point for their cyberattack.

A new dimension in cyberattacks?

It remains unclear who was behind the attacks in France and what motivated them. There is also no evidence so far that a self-replicating AI worm was used in the attacks on French refrigeration systems. However, Anthropic's latest research shows how significantly AI could facilitate the development of malware, potentially enabling attacks on connected devices with serious consequences and without requiring much computing power.

Fearing further attacks, France's cybersecurity agency advised all companies to update their connected devices regularly, install essential security patches and, where possible, to disable unnecessary internet access altogether.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: Middle East updates: Houthis target Yemen government palace in Aden
World.content:
Skip next section Iran steps up attacks on shipping near Strait of Hormuz

10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 Iran steps up attacks on shipping near Strait of Hormuz

Containers float in the water after a cargo ship was sunk near the Strait of Hormuz this week Image: Social Media/REUTERS

Iran's military on Thursday said an oil tanker caught fire in the Gulf of Oman, just south of the Strait of Hormuz, while trying to pass through a "prohibited" area.

Although Iran did not directly claim responsibility for the tanker fire, state television cited an army statement saying an "offending" and "non-compliant" tanker had switched off its tracking system while trying to pass thought "the prohibited zone."

The US military, which is also enforcing a maritime blockade in the region, has not issued a statement.

The reported incident comes a day after Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said a cargo vessel was sunk while passing through Strait of Hormuz after striking a mine.

Iranian state media quoted the IRGC as saying the ship was sailing on an "unauthorized route," but did not share details of the vessel's identity or the fate of its crew. The state television report included footage of an unidentified ship listing and billowing a plume of smoke.

Meanwhile, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said a Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride was hit by "unknown projectiles" on Tuesday and sank.

US broadcaster CNN reported that the GFS Pride is the ship the IRGC claimed struck a mine, and cited expert assessment that a drone strike is likely what actually caused the sinking.

How much oil is getting through the Strait of Hormuz? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In a statement , the MPA said all crew members were evacuated from the ship.

The MPA also reported a second vessel, the GFS Giselle, was attacked by projectiles on Tuesday, and sustained damage but was able to reach safe anchorage.

"Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law," the authority said. The US military has not commented.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck on Tuesday by projectiles but sustained only minor damage.

According to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) , the GFS Pride is one of only two ships to have been sunk in the Strait of Hormuz out of 114 reported incidents since the US launched the war with Iran in February.

World.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
World.content:
Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

On Wednesday morning, the live broadcast was halted, Halk TV's headquarters in the city of Istanbul were searched, and a new administrator was appointed by the government to run the media outlet. An arrest warrant was issued for the station's CEO, Cafer Mahiroglu, who currently lives in London. According to prosecutors, 11 people were arrested.

Turkey has faced criticism for years over restrictions on press freedom. Halk TV is one of the country's best-known opposition television stations and regularly broadcasts critical reports about Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his Justice and Development Party (AKP). After the raid, journalists were initially prevented from entering the building. Pre-recorded programs were broadcast instead of live reports.

The timing is particularly sensitive: Halk TV was raided on the very day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoglu was scheduled to begin his defense against corruption charges in court. The channel has been an important source of information for those following the trial.

Imamoglu, who won the mayoral election in Istanbul in 2019 and remained in office until his arrest on March 19, 2025, is one of Erdogan's most significant rivals, considered a beacon of hope for the opposition. He is still expected to run for president in 2028.

He is accused of establishing and running a criminal organization, as well as of various related financial crimes. Prosecutors are seeking a prison term of 2,352 years related to 142 charges. Imamoglu denies the allegations, arguing that the case is politically motivated.

11 people were arrested in conjunction with the raid on Halk TV headquarters Image: ANKA

Raid linked to investigation into Cafer Mahiroglu

Istanbul prosecutors said that the raid on Halk TV was linked to an investigation into its CEO Mahiroglu, who is accused of bribery, bid rigging and money laundering.

They said that arrest warrants had been issued for 17 people, on top of the 11 arrests. Assets belonging to companies allegedly linked to Mahiroglu were also seized and a trustee appointed to run the firms.

The opposition responded with sharp criticism of the police raid. Ozgur Ozel, the leader of the social democratic New Party (Yeni Parti) said it was a dark day for Turkey.

"The public's right to information is being seized for political reasons," Mahiroglu said.

"Showing solidarity with Halk TV means supporting the struggle for democracy in Turkey," Ozel said.

He added that "only dictators" would launch "a dawn raid on a television channel, appointing a trustee […]" and criticized the fact that this had occurred on the day that Imamoglu was due to begin his defense.

Many people in Turkey protested in support of Ekrem Imamoglu when he was jailed in 2025, like here in Izmir on May 19, 2025 Image: Berkcan Zengin/Middle East Images/picture alliance

Journalists' union slams raid

The Journalists' Union of Turkey (TGS) also condemned the raid on the platform X, describing it as arbitrary and arguing that the press was free and should not be censored.

Editor-in-chief Suat Toktas tried in vain to persuade the new state-appointed administrator to continue live broadcasts. In a video released by the TV channel, he said that what was happening was "illegal."

Halk TV began broadcasting on January 10, 2005 and its live broadcasts gained widespread attention particularly during the 2013 Gezi Park protests. Cafer Mahiroglu took over the station in 2020.

This article was translated from German.

World.title: Trump says execution of Fort Hood shooter will not be livestreamed
World.content:
Trump said the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan can be viewed in person by families of the victims if they wish. The decision comes after bipartisan backlash regarding the Pentagon's plans to livestream the execution.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will not be livestreamed.

The announcement comes after the Trump administration faced criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, as well as rights groups and many in the international community. Vice President JD Vance also said he would not watch such a livestream.

Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social that publicly airing the execution “might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan."

But the president added that "any very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device."

Trump said he "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed." He noted that the execution can be viewed in person by immediate families of the victims, "if they so choose."

Hasan's execution is scheduled for Deccember 3 at the US military prison in Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

Hasan said he had perpetrated the shooting to protect Taliban members in Afghanistan from US troops [FILE: June 29, 2012] Image: Bell County Sheriff's Office/REUTERS

A slew of criticism

The public execution idea drew wide condemnation from lawmakers of both main US parties, Republicans and Democrats, including top House Republican Mike Johnson, who said it could be a "recruiting tool for future terrorists."

Dozens of retired US military officers also published an open letter warning against broadcasting the execution, saying it "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it."

The letter added that such a move woud "ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr for attacking and killing his fellow soldiers," said the officers, including more than 40 generals and admirals.

Even Vice President JD Vance was reticent about the plan.

When asked about the public execution and whether it was acceptable in his Christian faith, Vance said he didn't know that it would actually happen.

"So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don’t forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people,” Vance said, adding: “Now, that said, I mean, look, if it’s ultimately livestreamed, I’m not going to be watching it."

Hegseth had sought to make execution 'public'

The plan to livestream Hasan's execution was announced last week by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

In a video posted on X by official Pentagon accounts, Hegseth had said that Hasan would get "a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be, and we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public."

Hasan was an Army psychiatrist who held the rank of major when he carried out the shooting in a medical building on November 5, 2009.

Soldiers were waiting in long lines to receive immunizations and medical clearance for deployment at the time of the shooting. Hasan shouted “Allahu akbar” — Arabic for “God is great!” — as he opened fire on his fellow soldiers

He was left paralyzed from the waist down after being shot in the back by law enforcement. He now uses a wheelchair.

During his trial, Hasan said he had perpetrated the shooting to protect Taliban members in Afghanistan from US troops.

The last time the US military carried out a service member execution was in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

World.title: Russia arrests Swedish national, claims he's Ukraine fighter
World.content:
Russian intelligence agents have arrested a Swedish man they say led a Ukrainian drone unit. He was detained at Russia's western border and is accused of planning acts of terrorism and sabotage.

Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) on Thursday announced the arrest and detention of a Swedish national who, authorities say, fights for Ukraine.

What do we know so far?

The 35-year-old Swede, detained near Pskov on Russia's western border, has been charged with illegally entering the country and may face additional terrorism charges, FSB representatives said.

Russia claims to have secured documents proving that the man led a Ukrainian drone unit.

They are now investigating whether he could be charged with organizing terror attacks on behalf of Ukraine or other Western intelligence services.

According to the FSB, the man "entered the Russian Federation under the pretext of joining the ranks of the Russian armed forces with the aim of carrying out acts of sabotage and terrorist attacks on military installations."

The FSB also released a video that it claimed showed the man confessing that he had entered Russia to commit "terrorist attacks" and sabotage.

Putin on a war footing: escalation on all fronts? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

During the video the man spoke in English, saying that he was from Stockholm, had signed a contract with Ukraine's Defense Ministry and had received drone training. Russian state TV showed images of what it said was the man's contract with Ukraine.

The Pskov region borders Belarus, Estonia and Latvia — the latter two being EU and NATO member states — FSB officials did not specify where exactly the man had arrived from.

Sweden aware of incident, with no comment yet from Ukraine

The Swedish Foreign Ministry has said that it is aware of the situation but not involved.

Ukraine has not commented on the arrest.

On Tuesday, Russia arrested a Japanese journalist that Moscow accused of spying, a claim that Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi rejected.

Russia itself has been accused of hiring and deploying numerous individuals to commit acts of sabotage abroad or to recruit locals willing to do so — this, beyond the country's legions of malign cyber actors.

None of the claims made by Russia and the FSB on Thursday can be substantiated.

World.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries as Zelenskyy says 'we're done'
World.content:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine will again attack Russian energy sites, as Moscow has ignored a claim by US President Trump that an "energy ceasefire" had been agreed. Russia reported two attacks on refineries.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday said that military strikes on Russian energy infrastructure would resume, despite US President Donald Trump's insistence that such attacks stop.

In an interview with London's Financial Times (FT) newspaper, Zelenskyy said, "The block [on energy infrastructure attacks] is out. We're done."

The announcement came after Russia reported Ukrainian attacks on oil processing plants in Ryazan, where fire broke out, and Saratov.

Kyiv had refrained from making attacks to give Trump's "energy ceasefire" a chance for success.

On Thursday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov praised "vigorous [US] efforts to initiate the peace process," and claimed that by resuming attacks, Ukraine "is coming into serious conflict with the peace efforts of the United States and American negotiators."

Russia, however, has paid no heed to Trump, instead continuing to hit Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure, for instance on Wednesday, when Russian strikes cut power to 600,000 Ukrainian citizens.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy said of Trump's 'ceasefire' on energy sites: 'We're done' Image: Dan Bashakov/AP Photo/picture alliance

Kyiv blasts dangerous lack of US intel

Ukraine had gone along with Trump's public proposal — despite not being notified of any "ceasefire" ahead of time — but it seemed to have helped little in the eyes of US leadership.

To that end, Zelenskyy railed against a "dangerous" lack of US intelligence information this week as well as the throttling of SpaceX Starlink satellite access for Ukraine's troops after Trump last week announced a number of decisions that have had adverse consequences for Ukraine.

The Ukrainian president said his country's military leaders had been warned that they would not be receiving US intelligence if they did not abide by Trump's "ceasefire."

Ukraine: Russian strikes continue as ceasefire questions remain To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Despite Ukraine's restraint, that withholding of intelligence was on full display this week when Kyiv was blindsided by Russian drones and missiles without any prior warning from the US.

"We will find a way out," said Zelenskyy of the situation as Ukraine's Western allies scramble to pick up the intelligence and defensive slack left by the US.

Zelenskyy said he would be willing to halt energy infrastructure attacks again but only if the US supplied Patriot interceptors that would allow Kyiv to down incoming the Russian ballistic missiles and drones that have been raining down on Ukraine since February 24, 2022.

Zelenskyy: Starlink throttling a question of US 'will'

Despite US claims that the Starlink situation was the result of a technical glitch, Zelenskyy told the FT, "It was not a technical problem, it was will."

SpaceX owner Elon Musk said the US owns and operates the Starshield military version of Starlink used by Ukraine, adding that he and his company had nothing to do with the issue.

Ukraine presses allies on intelligence sharing To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The FT interview comes in the wake of Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil as well as his promise to buy "millions of barrels" of Russian diesel fuel amid high fuel prices caused by the US war with Iran.

The deal, just weeks from the US midterm elections, is unlikely to bring down oil prices. But it does extend a lifeline to Russian President Putin, allowing him to continue his illegal invasion of neighboring Ukraine.

Trump has repeatedly lashed out at Zelenskyy and went so far as to call for him to be replaced this weekend.

Trump's sanctions actions fly in the face of nearly five years of allied political efforts to pressure Moscow to end its invasion.

Trump's actions have enraged NATO allies and European leaders, with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, for one, calling the US agreement to purchase Russian diesel "a very risky decision."

Meloni pointed out that the spike in oil prices was clearly precipitated by Trump's war in Iran and that his dealings with Putin would result in the Russian leader continuing his invasion of Ukraine rather than ending it.

World.title: Can Kenya preserve the democratic space Raila Odinga fought for?
World.content:
One year after the former prime minister's death, Kenyans are reflecting on his contribution to democracy and national reconciliation. Odinga's "handshakes" with his political rivals remain the subject of much debate.

AsKenya marks the first anniversary of Raila Odinga's death on Thursday, the former prime minister remains a towering figure. For many, he symbolizes the struggle for multiparty democracyand constitutional reforms. For others, his political alliances raise questions about compromise, opposition politics and the direction of the movement he built.

The question is not only how Kenya remembers Odinga — but whether the principles he championed can survive. "I want his legacy to live beyond the party," 20-year-old Nairobi resident Beatrice Chebet told DW.

Chebet said Odinga wanted a Kenya grounded in peace, democracy, constitutionalism and the rule of law. She said younger generations must carry those aspirations forward.

Odinga was fondly referred to as "Baba," or father, by his supporters Image: Halima Gongo/DW

Odinga had a lasting effect on the experiences and political journey of younger Kenyans, Chebet said. "Some of us were Gen Zs," she said. "We did not know any form of multipartyism without reading Raila.”

Forged in struggle

Odinga's influence was shaped by decades of opposition politics, detentions and campaigns for democratic change. His role in the disputed 2007 presidential election placed him at the center of one of Kenya's most consequential political crises. The postelection violence killed more than 1,100 people and displaced hundreds of thousands.

A power-sharing agreement brokered with international mediation led by Kofi Annan, the former secretary-general of the United Nations, made Odinga prime minister in a coalition government with President Mwai Kibaki. The settlement also established a reform agenda, including constitutional change. Kenya adopted a new constitution in 2010, introducing a devolved system of government.

The security and intelligence strategist Byron Adera said Odinga's impact extended beyond electoral politics. "Raila was an institution that rocked institutions, bringing about lasting and very impactful institutional reforms for the betterment of Kenya," Adera told DW. He identifies constitutional reform and efforts to bring competing political interests together as important parts of Odinga's legacy.

A look at the life of Kenya's Raila Odinga To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Reconciliation also became one of the most contested aspects of Odinga's career. His "handshakes" of reconciliation with Kibaki in 2008 and President Uhuru Kenyatta in 2018 and cooperation with President William Ruto in 2024 illustrated his willingness to pursue political agreements with former rivals.

Supporters saw dialogue as a way to reduce tensions and advance national interests; critics questioned what such arrangements meant for an independent opposition. Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has strongly criticized the political rapprochement between President William Ruto and the late Raila Odinga.

In May, Gachagua called the handshake process "nonsense" and said it had eroded Kenya's democracy by weakening the opposition's ability to hold the government accountable. His position offers a contrasting view of the alliances that shaped Odinga's later political years.

What happens to Odinga's ODM party?

The debate over Odinga's legacy is especially pressing within the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), the party he helped found and led for years.

Edwin Sifuna, a potential presidential candidate in the 2027 election, who describes Odinga as both his leader and friend, said the ODM's identity and direction had changed fundamentally. "We run the risk of losing our core support, people who believed in the ideals of ODM, because we were always the party of the people," Sifuna told DW.

Sifuna said Odinga's influence on national politics and public debate was greatly missed. His remarks point to a central challenge for ODM: whether it can preserve its identity and connection with ordinary Kenyans while navigating a changing political landscape. However, in a bid to keep the Odinga name in politics, Winnie Odinga, daughter of Raila Odinga, declared that she will run for Senator of Nairobi County in the 2027 election.

Chebet said Odinga's legacy would be measured by whether future generations continue to defend the principles associated with his political journey. Adera, meanwhile, emphasizes the lasting importance of institutional reform and building bridges.

Their perspectives highlight the tension at the heart of Odinga's legacy: a leader remembered for expanding democratic possibilities, but whose political compromises remain debatable. A year after his death, Odinga's influence is still visible in Kenya's political arguments, party divisions and public calls for democratic accountability.

The lasting test will be whether Kenya's institutions, political parties and younger generation can carry those principles forward — and whether the democratic space Odinga helped shape can endure beyond the man himself.

Edited by: Chrispin Mwakideu

World.title: La Junta Electoral abre expediente sancionador a Sánchez por la rueda de prensa en La Moncloa donde anunció los decretos sobre vivienda
World.content:
La Junta Electoral Central (JEC) acordó este jueves abrir expediente sancionador al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, por el contenido de una rueda de prensa que ofreció en La Moncloa el pasado 6 de octubre donde anunció los dos decretos sobre medidas de vivienda. La sanción podría oscilar entre 300 y 3.000 euros. El órgano que vigila los procesos electorales celebró este jueves una larga reunión con más de 20 puntos en las que resolvió, para empezar, propuestas de sanción contra el presidente Sánchez denunciadas por Vox, el PP y Se Acabó la Fiesta. La Junta determinó que no tenía sentido abrir expediente de sanción por la comparecencia de Sánchez en La Moncloa en la que anunció con una declaración institucional la convocatoria anticipada de elecciones para el 29 de noviembre, porque entiende que esa presencia no estaba dentro aún de un periodo electoral, pero sí ha decidido contemplar la posibilidad de sanción contra el líder del PSOE por la rueda de prensa que dio al día siguiente, el 6 de octubre, tras un Consejo de Ministros, en la que comunicó el contenido de los dos decretos sobre vivienda que aún debe convalidar la Diputación Permanente del Congreso.

Vox, Se Acabó la Fiesta y el PP habían presentado ya el pasado 6 de octubre denuncias ante la JEC contra Sánchez por considerar que utilizó el día 5 y el 6 de ese mes la sede de la Presidencia del Gobierno para realizar mensajes y actos propios de carácter electoral. El PP entendió así que el presidente habría expuesto en la rueda de prensa del 6 de octubre logros de su Ejecutivo, criticado a la oposición y reclamado una mayoría parlamentaria más amplia, lo que vulneraría la Ley Orgánica del Régimen Electoral General (LOREG) y reclamó la sanción más amplia porque defendía, además, que había antecedentes porque no era la primera vez que sucedía.

La JEC archiva la primera denuncia de la declaración institucional y permite que prospere la segunda, sin precisar aún si la sanción será la mínima posible, 300 euros, o la máxima, 3.000. Lo que sí concluye es que en esa cita Sánchez pudo vulnerar “la prohibición establecida en el artículo 50.2 de la LOREG y el deber de neutralidad política que deben respetar los poderes públicos durante los períodos electorales”. La JEC ordena retirar esas manifestaciones de la web y otros canales oficiales de La Moncloa.

El PP se apresuró a celebrar la sanción de la JEC contra Sánchez “por hacer trampas el mismo día que convocó las elecciones generales que le pueden suponer una multa de hasta 3.000 euros, la séptima en ochos años de gobierno. Dijimos que no le dejaríamos pasar ni una: primera victoria conseguida”. El PP subraya, además, que “Sánchez es reincidente” y que las juntas electorales “ya declararon que vulneró la ley en seis procesos electorales y ha recibido cuatro multas por valor de 6.600 euros, además de dos sanciones confirmadas por el Tribunal Supremo”. También destacan, en este caso, que el presidente “batió su propio récord el pasado 6 de octubre porque no tardó ni un solo día en vulnerar la LOREG”, en alusión a la comparecencia justo al día siguiente de convocar las elecciones.

En la resolución sancionadora de la JEC se exponen algunas de las expresiones que usó Sánchez en aquella rueda de prensa. Como: “Y con esa forma de hacer política, y ahí están los resultados económicos, en términos de empleo y también de desigualdad, hemos sacado adelante nada más y nada menos que 33 leyes, 43 reales decretos ley y dos reformas constitucionales en esta legislatura”. O: “Y es que en 2018 la hucha de las pensiones estaba en 5.000 millones de euros y hoy la hucha de las pensiones está en 20.000 millones”. También: “Yo creo que este gobierno ha hecho mucho durante estos últimos ocho años por la vivienda”. Y finalmente: “Hemos multiplicado por ocho los presupuestos. Hemos también dado a las comunidades autónomas 7.000 millones de euros para que construyan más vivienda protegida”. También se recogen apreciaciones críticas hacia partidos de la oposición.

La JEC, por tanto, acuerda instar al presidente del Gobierno a que, durante el período electoral, “observe el deber de neutralidad política exigible a los poderes públicos y se abstenga de realizar manifestaciones contrarias al artículo 50.2 de la LOREG en actos institucionales”.

World.title: Aagesen pide apostar por energía autóctona y renovable ante un coste extra de 100.000 millones en la UE por la guerra
World.content:
La vicepresidenta tercera del Gobierno avanza que septiembre ha sido el más cálido de la serie histórica. Demanda que se regule la IA para ponerla al servicio de los países

La vicepresidenta tercera del Gobierno y ministra para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, Sara Aagesen, defendió la necesidad urgente de transformar el modelo energético europeo durante su intervención en la tercera edición del foro CREO. Aagesen advirtió de que los conflictos internacionales, como la guerra en Ucrania y las tensiones en Oriente Próximo, han dejado al descubierto las debilidades del continente. Según afirmó la ministra, la coyuntura geopolítica actual “ha demostrado que Europa es muy vulnerable y precisamente vulnerable por nuestra dependencia de los combustibles fósiles”.

Frente a esta dependencia exterior, Aagesen recordó las cifras aportadas por la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, señalando que la Unión Europea ha tenido que soportar “un extracoste respecto a los mismos combustibles que habían sido importados por encima de los 100.000 millones de euros” desde el inicio del conflicto. Para combatir este menoscabo económico, la vicepresidenta instó a acelerar el uso de recursos propios inagotables: “Creo que la gran apuesta es buscar energía autóctona”, basándose en “nuestro entorno natural, el sol y el viento”. Asimismo, destacó que las tecnologías limpias generan ya cerca del “60% de la energía eléctrica en nuestro país”, aportando precios competitivos que posicionan a España como “la primera economía avanzada que más crecerá por tercer año consecutivo” según las previsiones del FMI.

Avance de AEMET y estragos de la crisis climática

En el ámbito de la emergencia climática, la ministra avanzó un dato de gran relevancia institucional y ambiental. Aagesen anunció que mañana la AEMET va a hacer público el balance climático del mes y “nuevamente tenemos una mala noticia”. En concreto, confirmó que el mes de septiembre “ha sido el más cálido de la serie histórica con una temperatura media 3,4 grados superior al promedio de referencia”, tras un periodo caracterizado por olas de calor y precipitaciones extremas.

La titular de Transición Ecológica subrayó que este incremento térmico no representa una cifra abstracta, sino que entraña “consecuencias reales, palpables, muy claras y materiales para la prosperidad”. Puso el foco en el impacto directo que sufren “los que trabajan al aire libre, los que cultivan nuestros alimentos y la gestión del agua”. Ante estos estragos, incidió en que “la adaptación tiene que formar parte de las decisiones de inversión y de la planificación del territorio” para reforzar infraestructuras y prevenir pérdidas, remarcando que “competitividad y descarbonización son las dos caras de la misma moneda”.

En línea con lo anterior, Aagesen ha hecho un alegato a favor de apostar en el futuro por decisiones concretas como optar por la ciencia frente al negacionismo.

Regular la IA y ponerla al servicio del bien común

Por último, la ministra abordó el reto de la transformación digital, defendiendo la urgencia de regular los avances tecnológicos con un enfoque humanista. Respecto al despliegue de algoritmos e innovación digital, Aagesen abogó por “avanzar hacia una inteligencia artificial que se desarrolle de forma ética con una regulación que asegure que esta inteligencia artificial se pone al servicio del bien común”. Especificó además que este marco regulatorio debe ser una herramienta que “protege a los más pequeños” y que contribuya decididamente a “la sostenibilidad y a la soberanía de los países”. Las palabras de la vicepresidenta se dan en plena carrara por aprobar el real decreto que impone nuevas exigencias a los proyectos de centros de datos, que el Gobierno busca elevar al Consejo de Ministros antes de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre.

Para finalizar, Sara Aagesen apeló a la responsabilidad colectiva y al rigor institucional, señalando que “la toma de decisiones requiere de conocimiento riguroso”. Reclamó a la sociedad civil y a los representantes políticos que “nos alejemos del ruido, de la polarización, de la desinformación y del descrédito a la ciencia”. Concluyó su intervención recordando que el futuro del país depende de las decisiones estratégicas que se adopten en el presente: “El futuro no nos espera, se crea”.

Un proyecto de país frente a la polarización

Más allá de las cifras energéticas y ambientales, la intervención de Sara Aagesen dejó un trasfondo eminentemente político estructurado en torno al modelo de Estado y de sociedad. La vicepresidenta contrapuso -a pocas semanas de las elecciones generales que se celebrarán el próximo 29 de noviembre- visiones de futuro planteando abiertamente la cuestión central que, a su juicio, afronta el país: “¿Qué modelo tenemos para España? ¿Qué modelo queremos para el futuro?“. En su discurso, dibujó un proyecto basado en la igualdad y la justicia social, defendiendo que ni el género, ni el tamaño del municipio de origen ni el nivel de renta familiar deben determinar las oportunidades de la ciudadanía. Para ello, reivindicó el papel vertebrador de unos servicios públicos sólidos —sanidad, educación y sistema de cuidados— y un crecimiento económico de corte humanista e inclusivo.

Asimismo, Aagesen situó la acción exterior de España en la defensa del multilateralismo, el derecho internacional y la paz en el seno de la Unión Europea. Ante las transformaciones en curso, la ministra hizo un llamamiento explícito a preservar el consenso institucional frente a la crispación: “Es importante que como sociedad nos alejemos del ruido, de la polarización, de la desinformación y del descrédito a la ciencia”. Aagesen definió el momento actual como una encrucijada donde cada decisión concreta moldea el rumbo de las próximas generaciones, llamando a elegir la autonomía, la inversión pública y la cooperación frente a la dependencia externa y la confrontación.

World.title: Amancio Ortega realiza una de sus grandes operaciones en EE UU con el cierre de la compra de un rascacielos en Chicago
World.content:
Amancio Ortega, fundador de Zara, ha cerrado una de sus grandes operaciones inmobiliarias en EEUU. El multimillonario español se ha hecho con el edificio One North Wacker, un rascacielos de 50 plantas en pleno Loop (distrito financiero) de Chicago, Estados Unidos. En junio se conoció que Pontegadea, el vehículo inversor del magnate del textil, estaba negociando la adquisición de esa torre al empresario inmobiliario Donald Bren. El precio pagado finalmente es de 550 millones de dólares, alrededor de 490 millones de euros, según avanzó este jueves la web especializada estadounidense CoStar.

El rascacielos, ubicado en el número uno de North Wacker Drive y que mide 199 metros de altura, fue construido entre 1999 y 2022 como sede para la entidad financiera suiza UBS. Actualmente, cuenta también con inquilinos como la consultora PwC, el despacho jurídico Barnes & Thornburg y Fitch Ratings.

Este edificio es uno más de los que Ortega va englobando en la cartera inmobiliaria de Pontegadea, que ya tiene un valor superior a los 21.000 millones, lo que le convierte en el mayor propietario inmobiliario del mundo. Y vuelve a poner los ojos en EE UU, uno de sus mercados favoritos para invertir, junto a Reino Unido y España.

Uno North Wacker, en 1 N. Wacker Drive Chicago.

En Chicago, Pontegadea ya ha realizado importantes adquisiciones. Este family office adquirió en 2023 el edificio de viviendas de alquiler de 727 de West Madison Street por 232 millones de dólares (alrededor de 212 millones de euros, al cambio de entonces). Además, en esa ciudad cuenta con el hotel Eurostars Magnificent Mile en River North, que compró por aproximadamente 65 millones en 2019.

En la ciudad del viento, Ortega también había adquirido en 2015 el antiguo Esquire Theater, reconvertido en tiendas de Christian Louboutin, ​​Tom Ford, Dolce & Gabbana y varios restaurantes. Una de sus primeras compras también se produjo en Chicago, cuando pagó 350 millones por el 730-750 de Michigan Avenue (en la zona de Magnificent Mile), por un edificio de tiendas en el mejor eje comercial.

Entre las compras inmobiliarias de Ortega en este año se encuentra un almacén logístico de Lactalis en Canadá o la inversión valorada en más de 1.000 millones en la empresa australiana de puertos Qube.

La presencia inmobiliaria en EE UU

El máximo accionista del grupo textil Inditex realizó en julio otra operación en EE UU, concretamente en Boston, donde se hizo con una torre de vivienda de lujo para alquiler -llamada The Kensigton- por 234 millones. El conjunto de todas las adquisiciones en vivienda de alta gama para alquilar en el mercado estadounidense alcanza en los últimos años los 1.350 millones invertidos.

Ortega ha utilizado históricamente los multimillonarios dividendos procedentes de Inditex, grupo del que controla el 60% del capital, para crear su enorme cartera inmobiliaria durante los últimos años. La huella en EE UU es muy extensa, donde cuenta con edificios de oficinas, tiendas, viviendas en alquiler o almacenes logísticos.

Precisamente, en logística realizó la que es su mayor adquisición inmobiliaria, ya que en 2022, a través de la filial Ponte Gadea Compass compró a la inmobiliaria Realty Income siete naves logísticas por 905 millones de euros en los Estados de Texas, Pensilvania, Wisconsin, Carolina del Sur, Virginia y Tennessee. Estos almacenes tenían en común largos alquileres a inquilinos de renombre como Amazon, Nestlé, Fedex o Home Depot.

También en EE UU, en 2022, se hizo con el rascacielos de viviendas de lujo para alquiler en el número 19 de Dutch Street, en pleno distrito financiero de Nueva York, cerca del World Trade Center.

En oficinas, Miami también ha sido uno de los puntos favoritos para Ortega, quién pagó 470 millones por Southeast Financial Center en 2016. En 2025, igualmente, adquirió Sabadell Financial Center, un inmueble de 31 plantas ubicado en esa ciudad de Florida donde el Banco Sabadell tiene su sede en Estados Unidos. O, en otra ocasión, desembolsó más de 320 millones por toda una manzana en la peatonal Lincoln Road, una de las calles más icónicas de Miami Beach, en ese caso con tiendas que albergan marcas como Apple, Gap o Nike.

En EE UU igualmente adquirió por 377 millones Arbor Blocks en Seattle, una de las sedes de Meta a nivel mundial, además de parte de la sede central de Amazon en Seattle, un complejo de edificios llamados Troy Block, por 655 millones. En Washington DC, pagó 207 millones a Blackstone por un complejo de oficinas junto a la Casa Blanca.

World.title: Cómo crear contraseñas que protejan nuestra vida digital
World.content:
1 Debe ser variada Una clave de acceso se puede componer a partir de distintos tipos de caracteres, como letras mayúsculas y minúsculas, números y caracteres especiales. Utilizar la mayor variedad posible aumenta la dificultad para ser descifrada

2 Debe ser larga Como referencia, es preferible utilizar 16 caracteres o más, cuando el servicio lo permita. Utilizar una frase puede ser más fácil de recordar

3 Evitar la información personal Eludir el propio nombre o el apellido, así como los de familiares, las fechas de nacimiento, los apodos, los nombres de mascotas, los de equipos de fútbol favoritos o cualquier otra información que se pueda encontrar en las propias redes sociales

4 Evitar combinaciones predecibles Muchos usuarios recurren a composiciones como 123456, password y otras secuencias sencillas que conviene eludir

5 Utilizar un gestor de contraseñas Existen programas seguros, de pago y gratuitos, que permiten generar y almacenar estos códigos sin tener que memorizarlos

World.title: Yolanda Díaz, a los empresarios: “Mejoren los salarios. El esfuerzo no puede caer solo en el SMI”
World.content:
La vicepresidenta segunda y ministra de Trabajo, Yolanda Díaz, dio el primer paso la semana pasada para volver a subir el salario mínimo interprofesional con la convocatoria de la comisión de expertos que recomendará cuándo debe crecer para no perder poder adquisitivo ni alejarse del 60% del salario medio. El suelo salarial ha crecido mucho en los últimos años (un 66% desde 2018, 40 puntos más que la inflación), pero el resto de retribuciones, las que deciden los empresarios, no siguen esa estela. “España tiene un reto, mejorar los salarios. El esfuerzo no puede recaer solo sobre el artículo 27 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores [el que regula el SMI]. Hago un llamamiento con todo el cariño a que mejoren los salarios”, ha dicho este jueves en la segunda jornada del Foro CREO, organizado por Cinco Días.

“He convocado al comité de expertos en salario mínimo [un equipo formado por académicos, miembros del Gobierno y sindicalistas] para que den cumplimiento a que el SMI se equipare al 60% del salario medio neto y que no pierda poder adquisitivo”, ha explicado Díaz. Los salarios pactados en convenios están creciendo a un ritmo del 3%.

No lo ha dicho en su discurso, pero fuentes de su departamento sostienen que su intención política es aprobar el incremento antes de las elecciones generales. No necesitaría pasar por la Diputación Permanente, ya que el incremento se aprueba por decreto. Díaz ha pedido a los expertos que entreguen su recomendación como tarde para finales de octubre, lo que le dejaría unas cuatro semanas hasta los comicios. Para la subida de 2025, el ministerio presentó el informe elaborado por esos especialistas el 9 de enero de ese mismo año. Para la de 2026, lo hizo el 12 de diciembre de 2025.

Díaz ha subrayado que una vez que los expertos entreguen su recomendación (que si sigue la estela del IPC promedio del año rondará el 3,5% y si se limita a los últimos datos, se acercará más al 5%) abrirá la negociación con los agentes sociales, donde se precisará la cifra de subida del SMI para 2027. Los sindicatos UGT y CC OO reclaman que el suelo retributivo suba un 7%.

El salario mínimo vigente es de 1.221 euros brutos al mes en 14 pagas, un 3,1% más que en 2025. Esa subida supuso un alza de 37 euros mensuales, producto de un acuerdo entre el Ministerio de Trabajo, CC OO y UGT. Ese incremento fue rechazado por las patronales CEOE y Cepyme, como prácticamente todas las subidas impulsadas por Díaz desde que es ministra. La única que sí recibió el respaldo de las organizaciones empresariales fue la primera, cuando subió en 2020 de 900 a 950 euros. Desde que Pedro Sánchez es presidente del Ejecutivo, el SMI ha crecido de 736 a 1.221 euros.

En su discurso, Díaz ha abordado otros asuntos de actualidad, como la crisis de acceso a la vivienda. Ha llamado a que “se cumpla el mandato constitucional” del derecho a la vivienda. “La fábrica de desigualdad hoy en día se llama vivienda”, ha dicho, antes de cargar contra la derecha por sus críticas de los últimos días al sistema de pensiones, de nuevo con un argumento constitucional: “La pensión media de jubilación es de 1.576 euros, 500 más que cuando el PP dejó el Gobierno. El sistema de pensiones es sostenible y la suficiencia es un mandato constitucional. No está en riesgo, es sólido y robusto”.

Díaz también ha defendido la regularización extraordinaria de extranjeros, “de los que 420.000 ya cotizan a la Seguridad Social”. Ha rechazado que esta política del Gobierno implique un “efecto llamada”. “Lo que tiene es efecto en la dignidad. Es una referencia para el mundo”, ha comentado. También ha dicho: “No nos acostumbremos a vivir con umbrales de pobreza como si fueran parte del paisaje; reducir la desigualdad es una decisión política”.

World.title: Pablo Bustinduy: “Hay una deriva oligárquica que amenaza nuestras democracias”
World.content:
El ministro de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, Pablo Bustinduy, cree que el “creciente poder” de las corporaciones y el reparto “injusto” de la riqueza es una “amenaza” para el orden democrático. Esa ha sido la línea vehicular de su discurso este jueves en el Foro CREO de Cinco Días, en la apertura de la segunda jornada. “Hay una deriva oligárquica que amenaza la supervivencia de nuestras democracias tal como las conocemos”, ha dicho el también diputado de Sumar, que antes de empezar su discurso, ante las preguntas de los periodistas, ha defendido a sus compañeros del Frente Amplio (Ada Colau y Emilio Delgado) en la disputa por el liderazgo de la izquierda.

Bustinduy ha iniciado su discurso afirmando que “la democracia no ha llegado a las relaciones económicas” y que ello “es visible en el consumo, en la asimetría estructural entre consumidores y grandes empresas”. “Nuestro diagnóstico es que esa asimetría se ha visto agravada en las últimas décadas y se ha resentido la situación de desamparo, cuando no de maltrato, ante prácticas flagrantemente ilegales”, ha considerado el responsable de Consumo.

Ante ese escenario, Bustinduy ha reivindicado la acción de su ministerio, “con sanciones muy sonadas, desde el transporte a las aerolíneas de bajo coste, las plataformas de comercio online, las de pisos turísticos, el alquiler de coches o las grandes inmobiliarias”. Cree que esas sanciones “han aflorado un gran consenso social” en torno a los abusos empresariales.

Bustinduy ha considerado que en estos años “de robusto crecimiento económico” el Gobierno ha tomado medidas para que se redistribuya mejor la riqueza generada, “especialmente mediante la palanca del salario mínimo interprofesional”, pero ha reconocido que “ha funcionado de forma incompleta e insuficiente”. “Los deciles más bajos de la renta han tenido un incremento superior gracias al SMI”, ha subrayado, antes de reseñar que “la vía fiscal ha fracasado”. Bustinduy cree que la riqueza generada en los últimos años “gracias al esfuerzo de millones de trabajadores, de su tiempo y sus manos, no se ha repartido de forma justa y eficaz”, y por ello ha llamado a emprender una profunda reforma fiscal. “Nuestro sistema fiscal ha fracasado en la tarea de redistribuir esa riqueza. Es necesaria una reforma fiscal para que esa riqueza vuelva a quienes la producen”, ha agregado.

En la misma línea, el diputado de Sumar también ha dicho: “En España tienen que subir los salarios. Se lo digo a los empresarios que están aquí, con los márgenes en máximos”. Ha criticado a los que denuncian que el salario mínimo se parezca cada vez más al salario medio: “El análisis es al revés. Es inexplicable que en un momento de crecimiento económico sostenido el Gobierno haya subido el salario mínimo y las patronales hayan arrastrado los pies en la negociación colectiva. Es injusto y antieconómico”.

Tras presentar este escenario, Bustinduy ha considerado que la falta de redistribución de la riqueza es “una amenaza a la democracia, que depende de que existan condiciones de igualdad”. “Un sistema en que la economía funciona mediante la desposesión y la acumulación obscena no es una democracia. Cuando una minoría cada vez más reducida acumula cada vez más resortes de poder tiene otro nombre, oligarquía. Hay una deriva oligárquica que amenaza la supervivencia de nuestras democracias tal como las conocemos”, ha dicho Bustinduy, antes de criticar al “rentismo” y el problema de acceso a la vivienda en España: “Los grandes fundadores del capitalismo lo justificaron como el sistema más eficiente contra el rentismo, el que extrae rentas de abajo hacia arriba. Es un problema económico porque cada euro que una familia pone en el alquiler no crea trabajo. Desaparece como en una aspiradora”.

World.title: Juan Bravo (PP): “Hay que cambiar el modelo de crecimiento del país”
World.content:
Reconstruir el país a partir del establecimiento de reglas claras, sin castigos para aquellas empresas que quieran crecer y donde innovar salga a cuenta. Estas son las tres líneas centrales sobre las que el vicesecretario de Economía del Partido Popular, Juan Bravo, ha adelantado que su grupo trabajará a partir del 29 de noviembre, si resulta victorioso en las elecciones generales. El mandatario popular, que ha participado este jueves en la segunda jornada del Foro CREO de CincoDías y Prisa Media, ha señalado que “es responsabilidad de todos hacer un país más competitivo”, y que “cambiar el modelo de crecimiento no se hace con un decreto o en un trimestre”, por lo que ha reclamado el apoyo de las empresas para poder emprender esa transformación si se produce un cambio de Gobierno.

Bravo, que ha comenzado con un “reconocimiento sincero” a la trayectoria de CincoDías por “poner primero los datos y después las opiniones”, se ha agarrado a esa máxima para detallar la situación económica del país y adelantar algunos de los cambios que propone el PP, singularmente en materia de crecimiento productivo.

Según el relato que ha realizado, pese a que los datos macro están siendo positivos, esta aparente bonanza del país no se está trasladando a la ciudadanía y las empresas. Las empresas no dejan de crecer por falta de ambición, sino por supervivencia", ha declarado, en alusión a las trabas fiscales a las que se ven sometidas las compañías cuando deciden ampliar su plantilla hasta los 50 trabajadores.

“Según datos de Fedea, hay un 62% más de empresas con 49 trabajadores”, ha dicho Bravo, que en esta línea ha planteado incentivos fiscales que alienten la fusión de las pymes, y así puedan ganar tamaño “para poder innovar, ser más productivas y poder pagar mejores salarios”.

Para que esto sea así, el líder económico del PP también ha solicitado que se lleven a cabo “tests de pymes” antes de elaborar leyes que afecten al tejido productivo. “Porque hacemos leyes pensando en que todas las empresas son grandes, y no es así”, ha indicado. Junto con esta monitorización más precisa, Bravo ha señalado la necesidad de fomentar la innovación de las empresas, para lo que ha propuesto la compra pública como impulso.

“Las empresas prefieren ir a Estados Unidos con un contrato de tres millones con el Gobierno que con una subvención de tres millones, porque allí lo valoran más”, ha puesto como ejemplo. “España es la cuarta potencia económica de Europa, pero la novena en patentes”, ha lamentado Bravo. “Es necesario que se cree un puente entre el conocimiento y el mercado, para que la ciencia que se hace en nuestras universidades termine en las empresas, en las start-ups, y no en un cajón; para que el ingeniero que se formó aquí no tenga que irse; o para que la próxima empresa tecnológica que nazca en España se quede aquí”, ha enumerado.

Para amplificar este impulso a la innovación, Bravo ha propuesto la creación de una unidad aceleradora de proyectos estratégicos “de verdad”, que coordine al Estado con las comunidades autónomas. Sin embargo, uno de los epicentros de su diagnóstico acerca de por qué la economía española actualmente “suma, pero no multiplica” tiene que ver con la inseguridad jurídica de la que adolecen las empresas. “Creo en un país donde crecer no se castigue, donde innovar salga a cuenta, y donde haya reglas claras y no sorpresas”, ha remachado.

Nada de pensiones

En su intervención, Bravo ha evitado referirse a la sostenibilidad del sistema de pensiones, un tema que ha encontrado de nuevo un hueco destacado dentro de la precampaña electoral. La viabilidad económica de las prestaciones contributivas, cuya partida total escaló en 2025 hasta los 189.598 millones de euros ―lo que supone un alza del 6,2% respecto a los 178.500 millones gastados en 2024 y del 13,1% respecto a 2023, cuando se destinaron 168.000 millones― ha vuelto a la primera plana del debate político, a partir de las declaraciones que realizó la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, este miércoles, en las que alertó de que el sistema “va a petar”.

En ese contexto, Muñoz alentó un cambio de modelo, para el que reclamó valentía “a la hora de tomar decisiones”. Este planteamiento entronca con el de Vox, cuyo portavoz económico, José María Figaredo, reclamó la semana pasada una reforma estructural hacia un modelo mixto que combine el reparto con la capitalización individual, como han hecho con éxito otros países europeos.

World.title: Mi piso está en una planta baja. ¿Quién debe pagar la pintura y mantenimiento de las rejas?
World.content:
Pregunta. Vivo en una planta baja de una comunidad de vecinos en Cambrils (Tarragona), edificio construido hace 26 años. El constructor puso rejas en mis ventanas, que dan a una vía pública. Con el paso de los años se han deteriorado y pido que las pinte la comunidad. Me responden que son privadas. ¿Quién debe mantener y pintar las rejas? A. Oton

Respuesta. Las rejas instaladas en las ventanas o balcones de una vivienda situada en una comunidad de propietarios tienen carácter privativo en cuanto a su propiedad y uso. Sin embargo, su instalación y apariencia afectan directamente a la fachada del edificio, que tiene la consideración de elemento común según el Código Civil de Cataluña.

En Cataluña, la obligación de conservar y pintar las rejas depende de su origen y de quién asumió su instalación. Si las rejas formaban parte del edificio desde su construcción o fueron instaladas y aprobadas por la comunidad, su mantenimiento y pintura corresponden a la comunidad de propietarios. De acuerdo con el Libro Quinto del Código Civil de Cataluña, las ventanas y los elementos incorporados a la fachada forman parte de la configuración e imagen exterior del inmueble, por lo que la comunidad debe asumir los gastos necesarios para garantizar su adecuada conservación, seguridad y uniformidad estética (artículo 553-44 CCCat).

Si las rejas fueron instaladas posteriormente por un propietario por motivos de seguridad, su mantenimiento, limpieza y pintura corresponden exclusivamente a ese propietario. En este supuesto, se consideran un elemento privativo o un elemento común de uso exclusivo destinado a su aprovechamiento particular. El artículo 553-43 del CCCat establece que quien disfruta de forma exclusiva de un elemento debe asumir los gastos derivados de su conservación ordinaria. No obstante, cualquier actuación sobre las rejas deberá respetar el color, diseño y criterios estéticos establecidos por la comunidad para preservar la uniformidad de la fachada.

En cualquier caso, resulta recomendable revisar los estatutos de la comunidad de propietarios, ya que pueden contener disposiciones específicas sobre cerramientos exteriores, rejas u otros elementos que afecten a la estética del edificio.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Nazi-looted Kandinsky from Amsterdam family sold for almost €32m
World.content:
A painting by Wassily Kandinsky looted from a Jewish family in Amsterdam has sold at Christie’s in London for £27 million, (€32 million), broadcaster NOS reported.

Kandinsky painted Das bunte Leben (The colourful life) in Paris in 1907. Emanuel and Hedwig Lewenstein, who ran a sewing machine factory on the Dam, bought it in 1927. Their collection also included works by Jan Toorop, Jozef Israëls, and Jean Metzinger.

The painting was auctioned shortly after the German occupation began and was bought by Jewish collector Sal Slijper. His family later sold it to the Bayerische Landesbank, which loaned it permanently to the Lenbachhaus museum in Munich, where it hung for decades.

Researchers found that in 1940 a museum employee, acting for an unknown person, had the work taken to the auction house by courier. They said there were many indications the Nazis had seized it.

In 2023, the German public prosecution department classified the painting as looted art and the bank returned it to the Lewensteins’ heirs.

That same year, the heirs sold another Kandinsky, Bild mit Häusern, for more than €60 million. Amsterdam city council returned that work after a years-long dispute. It had hung in the Stedelijk Museum until February 2022.

World.title: Thousands of women abused in postwar Dutch camps, study finds
World.content:
A study released Thursday by the NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies has found that thousands of women imprisoned in internment camps after World War II were systematically sexually abused but that evidence of the crimes was hidden away.

The women, who were accused of having relationships with Germans during the Occupation of the Netherlands or were suspected collaborators, were subjected to “rapes, sadistic torture, forced undressing and public humiliations” in dozens of the country’s more than 200 internment camps, said NIOD.

Some 200 victims and witnesses gave statements to then-retired police inspector Johanna van Schilfgaarde for parliament’s 1950 Committee of Inquiry, but their accounts never made it into the final report.

Lead researcher at the time, Arnaud Baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken, was appointed to investigate reports of camp abuses, but concluded he couldn’t finish his assignment because witnesses were too afraid to speak out.

But the women’s testimonies were indeed in the archives, with almost all of them reporting sexual abuse and sadistic abuse by camp guards, including rape and sexual assault.

“In dozens of internment camps, structural sexual violence has been used by guards,” said historian and journalist Ewoud Kieft, who conducted the research for NIOD. “The lead investigator was grossly negligent, he told broadcaster NOS. “He failed to do his job.”

Because the committee’s final report contained no reference to the women’s testimonies, the Dutch government was never held to account.

Sixteen internment camp officials were eventually punished for murders and torture and were given fines or one-year prison sentences, but no one is known to have been punished for rape and sexual violence against women.

Kieft calls the testimonies “the tip of the iceberg” and has vowed to continue his research.

World.title: No Picnic: inquiry reveals Dutch cycling team’s toxic culture
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Dutch cycling team Picnic-PostNL has been silently struggling with an oppressive atmosphere and culture of intimidation, according to an investigation published by broadcaster NOS and cycling platform In De Waaier.

Many of the team’s former members have been left traumatised and described a “culture of fear” and “unsafe working conditions”.

Reporters confidentially spoke with 71 current and former employees of the team, which competes in the World Tour, the sport’s top division. It currently employs around 120 people. Many people described how management would punish criticism and ignore mental health complaints.

One interviewee described the management structure as a “dictatorship” and another said team members were treated as “puppets”.

This began after the team’s successes in the Tour de France in 2013 and 2014, when German rider Marcel Kittel won stages as a sprinter. After that, the managers became paranoid about losing control of the team, one person told NOS.

More rules were established and people were told “everyone is replaceable.”

After Dutch racer Tom Dumoulin won the 2017 Giro d’Italia, one of cycling’s three Grand Tours, the managers became even more “radicalised”, according to another interviewee.

Dutch rider Martijn Tusveld described how he was dropped from major races for questioning the team’s tactics. He became so anxious he considered harming himself. He left the team and said he is still mentally unwell.

Another, who was suffering mentally, said he was told by sports director Rudi Kemna “I don’t believe in psychologists” after he asked for help.

The Dutch professional cyclists’ association VVBW told NOS it had heard similar accounts over the past 18 months, with some riders calling in tears.

NOS has asked the team owner Iwan Spekenbrink for a comment but he has so far refused to reply to any allegations in person or in writing.

World.title: MPs move to curb small schools amid cost and curricula concerns
World.content:
MPs and the cabinet want to curb the growth of small, independent schools in the Netherlands, after a school linked to the far-right Forum for Democracy (FVD) opened with just four pupils, according to broadcaster NOS.

A 2021 law made it easier to set up state-funded schools based on new educational ideas or on religious or other “worldview” beliefs. Since then, more schools have opened every year, a large share of them Islamic.

The “Renaissance School” in Almere, which opened in August, was approved partly on the basis of market research showing around 350 people were positive about it.

MPs from both coalition and opposition parties said the research amounted to little more than an online survey, and that respondents often did not know what kind of school was planned. It is linked to the far-right FVD party.

Junior education minister Judith Tielen told parliament on Wednesday she would look at whether that part of the law should be tightened or scrapped. She had already written to MPs that keeping so many small schools going was “no longer sustainable”.

Tielen said she saw no reason to intervene at the Renaissance School for now. It must have at least 139 pupils by the start of its fourth school year or close.

The law originally was a VVD initiative, which the FVD voted against it at the time.

The debate comes a year after research by current affairs programme Nieuwsuur found that a number of orthodox Protestant and Islamic schools were teaching messages at odds with democratic values, such as rejecting same-sex relationships or teaching that women should be subordinate to men.

All schools in the Netherlands are legally required to stick to democratic values, including equality and non-discrimination. The schools inspectorate said it would investigate where necessary.

World.title: Dronten wreckage identified as British WWII bomber
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Aircraft wreckage uncovered four years ago in Dronten has been identified as a British WWII bomber, according to local officials.

Discovered in what is now the Van Veldhuizenbos forest in Dronten, the aircraft is said to be a British Avro Lancaster Mk III that was shot down by German forces on the night of September 27-28, 1943, while attempting to target Hanover, Germany.

The aircraft, run by the Canadian 405 Pathfinder Squadron stationed near Cambridge, England, crashed into what was then the Ijsselmeer.

The plane was carrying seven crew members – four Canadians, one Australian, and two Britons – whose bodies were never recovered. But human remains were found in 1959 and buried in the Jonkerbos War Cemetery in Nijmegen.

Additional human remains were discovered and are now being examined by the Ministry of Defence’s Recovery and Identification Service to see if they belong to the slain crew members.

“Behind every plane wreck lies a human story,” said Dronten mayor Jean Paul Gebben, who said the aircraft’s identification was of great historical significance.

Some of the recovered wreckage will be loaned to museums and foundations.

The government estimates that some 5,500 aircraft were lost over the Netherlands during the Second World War. Annually, a maximum of three aircraft recovery operations are carried out in the country, with the costs mostly covered by the national government.

World.title: Police urge Ahold to file a report over cybersecurity breach
World.content:
Dutch police and the Public Prosecutors Office have asked Ahold Delhaize, the parent company of Albert Heijn, to file a report on what the company is still calling a “cybersecurity incident”.

“There is currently no criminal investigation into the incident,” the police said in a press release issued on Wednesday. “Police and the OM have been in contact with Ahold Delhaize. The company has been invited to file a report.”

“In order to successfully track down and prosecute, it is crucial to always get information from victims as quickly as possible.”

Although Ahold did report the incident, which began on Sunday night, to the National Cyber Security Centre as required by law, a criminal investigation can’t be started without a formal police report.

The company says it will “work with all relevant authorities”, but it gave no explanation as to why it hasn’t filed a report and said it is not currently making any further statements.

The incident hit other Ahold chains Etos and Gall & Gall, leading the company to shut down several of its IT systems that has continued to make online shopping and deliveries impossible.

Sector insiders told the Financieele Dagblad, on condition of anonymity, that the crisis is costing Ahold Delhaize “tens of millions” of euros a day. Ahold told the paper it was too early to say what the financial impact would be.

Fresh produce took a particularly hard hit, with the supermarkets’ fruit and vegetable sections very low on stock.

Albert Heijn said on Thursday that its distribution centres are running again, but its website and delivery services are still not operating, meaning customers still can’t place orders online or via app. Deliveries of fresh products were also said to be resuming as of Thursday night, while delivery of non-perishable products has been fully restored.

“This is a positive step forward in the recovery of our supply chain,” said the company. “The investigation into the nature and cause of the cybersecurity incident is ongoing. At this time, there is no indication that any customer or employee data has been involved in the incident.”

Bad actors

“We can no longer see cybercrime as a collection of separate crimes, but as a criminal ecosystem,” said a police statement. “Behind almost every attack lies a chain of cooperating perpetrators, resources and criminal services that reinforce each other: a criminal supply chain.”

Several foreign servers are known to be used in the attack, including in the US, Poland, Moldova and Turkey, but that doesn’t necessarily mean that’s where the attacks are coming from as traffic can be routed through other countries.

Ahold supermarkets in Belgium (Delhaize) and the US (Stop & Shop and Food Lion) have also been affected.

The Albert Heijn incident came on the same weekend as a separate cyberattack on hundreds of supermarkets in France.

World.title: Dutch cabinet wants AI to help slash civil service: Telegraaf
World.content:
The cabinet is planning to slash the civil service with the help of new AI technologies, which could save hundreds of millions of euros, the Telegraaf reported on Thursday.

Sources told the paper that Eric van der Burg, the VVD junior home affairs minister, will soon present targets for cutting staff numbers, although estimates are not yet known.

Experts told the Telegraaf the rise in civil servants, which went from 140,000 in 2021 to 170,000 last year, that things are not improving. One said the government is being stifled with ever more rules and subsidies.

Policy officials in particular, who have almost doubled to 20,000 in the past decade, are putting needless pressure on the government, one analyst said.

Insiders said using AI could save an extra €200 million in both 2028 and 2029. A further €200 million has been planned for the interior ministry’s budget for the following year, rising to €1 billion a year from 2035.

Van der Burg is reported to be partly following the thinking of an advisory committee on the future of the civil service, which is due to present conclusions this year.

Ahead of a meeting with MPs, the committee said digitalisation and AI can make government more efficient, but only if the build-up of rules and checks is also tackled.

Government economist Jos Blank wrote that the state had been underperforming for decades, and that a constant stream of new rules, subsidies and mergers was making public services worse.

Former senior civil servant Roel Bekker criticised growing “policy overload” and called for the number of policy officials to be cut by 20% to 30%.

World.title: Unemployment remains at 4%, 408,000 out of work
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Over 408,000 people were out of work in September, national statistics office CBS said on Thursday.

The number of jobless people rose by an average of 5,000 a month over the past three months. The number of people in paid work stayed level.

Unemployment returned to 4% in July after dipping slightly in June. A year ago, 409,000 people were out of work, also 4% of the workforce.

The recent rise is mainly down to fewer unemployed people finding work rather than people losing their jobs.

Benefits agency UWV was paying out 197,100 unemployment benefits at the end of September. The UWV figures are not directly comparable with the CBS total, which counts everyone without paid work who is actively looking for a job.

A further 3.2 million people aged 15 to 75 are not counted as part of the workforce because they have not recently looked for work or cannot start straight away. Most are retired or unable to work because of illness or disability.

World.title: Ukraine finds remains of 30 people in search for victims of massacre by Polish WWII partisans
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
